##### 1. Story

As a **tech lead**, I want **the published contract baseline of the permission matrix as a versioned load — an OpenAPI 3.1 document for the load, the matrix read, the version read and the versions list, the `PermissionMatrix`, `PermissionMatrixRow`, `PermissionMatrixVersion` and `PermissionMatrixPage` schemas with the status and the effective dates, the whole-matrix rule, the rule that a version takes effect only when approved and only from its valid-from date, the `rwb.access.AccessPolicyChanged.v1` declaration with change kind `MATRIX`, one RFC 9457 error envelope, the consumed parameters and reference-data reads and the read-only ACE group view, the contract tables of section 12 and the fakes**, so that **the app story builds on Day 1 against a fixed, testable contract, and every consumer knows which version of the matrix it is checked against and on which date**.

The deliverable is the matrix **as a dated version**: the load, the two reads, the list and the event that tells the services a version was loaded. The approval is not contracted here — it is RWB-P4-AD010-APP's on the reference-load path and RWB-P4-AD010-CON declares the console side — and the enforcement of the letters is RWB-P4-E1037-CON's guard.

##### 2. Business rationale

Contract-first REST, one hop and a 2 s timeout is the decoupling decision (DP-11, ADR-020). In the monolith the matrix was a table read in the same connection, and a change of rights was a release or a manual data fix nobody outside the team could describe. In the target the matrix is rows of P4's own `permission` with a label, a status and an effective date, so the two answers that matter — which letters does this role hold on this date, and which version is in force — are written down once, with their fields, rights, versions and event.

The first consequence is the whole-file check. A row-level check would accept a file that silently omits a role, and an omitted role removes a right from every person holding it; the contract states that a complete matrix holds every active role once against each of the 14 areas of LOV-CAPABILITY, that a file with any gap is refused in full and that the missing role is named, because the refusal text and the message identity are what the administrator acts on.

The second consequence is the split between loading and taking effect. A loaded version is not a permission change: it is a proposal that waits for the approval of RWB-P4-AD010-APP and changes no answer until it is approved **and** its valid-from date has arrived. Both states use LOV-VERSION-STATUS (LOADED, VALIDATED, APPROVED, IN_FORCE, SUPERSEDED, ROLLED_BACK, REFUSED) of TSD P4 v3 T3.2, the vocabulary the reference loads and the rule packages use, so the service has one answer to "which value was in force when".

The third consequence is one event name. `rwb.access.AccessPolicyChanged.v1` is the one access-policy event the architecture gives `rwb-access` (Architecture v5 slides 14 and 43), services already refresh their cached permission data on it (slide 20), and a matrix load **is** an access-policy change; the payload carries the version, its status and its effective date and no letter of a role.

##### 3. Preconditions

- The service template and the naming library are available (RWB-PLT-TPL), so the base, topic and event names follow the platform rule rather than a local choice.
- The guard contract is published: RWB-PLT-E1037-CON and RWB-P4-E1037-CON fix the authorise contract and the library (DP-08) through which every operation demands its letter; the dependency is carried by RWB-P4-AD002-APP.
- RWB-PLT-E1027-CON is published: the decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` (DP-03), whose `AC-VERS` entry records every load; carried by the app story.
- RWB-PLT-E1042-CON and RWB-P3-E1042-CON are published: the parameters library and contract (DP-06), through which the approver role is read; carried by the app story (ASM-3728).
- RWB-PLT-E1043-CON and RWB-P3-E1043-CON are published: the reference-data library and contract (DP-07), through which LOV-CAPABILITY and its 14 values are read; carried by the app story.
- RWB-PLT-N001-CON is published: the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19) that serves SCR-43 and merges the matrix read with the access-log read; carried by the app story.
- `v_ace_iam_group` (DF-ACE-301 to DF-ACE-304) is granted and contracted by RWB-P1-E1069-APP (DP-05); this document declares it as a read-only consumed read with its `data_as_of`.
- The version status, the effective dates and the approver reference are **Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2264; ASM-3727)**: `permission` in TSD P4 v3 T3.1 carries `matrix_version` (DF-REF-044) and the standard `state` column (T3.0) and no date column, while legacy AC3 needs an approved version with a valid-from. This document fixes the field names and types of the four schemas and leaves the physical columns to the app story.
- The four operations have no ownership-map row and no T-A row, which holds only `GET /admin/roles` (API-P4-007), `GET /admin/access-log` (API-P4-008) and the reference-load paths (API-P4-005, API-P4-006, API-P4-009, API-P4-010) — **Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2264; ASM-1453)**.
- The rights are Platform administration in TSD P4 v3 T6.1 — `R` for the reads and `C` for the load, held by RW-SECADM (CRUDA) and RW-PLATADM (CRUD) — and the legacy rows "Reference data C: RW-COE, RW-REFADM" and "Rules and parameters A: RW-RISK" are not kept: the matrix is role administration, `permission` is P4's, and reference data is P3 rwb-case's (ASM-1454).
- The approval is not this document's: the legacy criterion names "the application owner's approval", TSD P4 v3 T6.1 holds no application-owner role, and the approval of a loaded version is RWB-P4-AD010-APP's with the approver role read from `rwb.refload.approver.permission=RW-SECADM` (ASM-3728).
- The completeness rule is a rule and not a count: the count is computed from `role` and LOV-CAPABILITY, and the labels `PM-2026.11`, `PM-2026.12` with 756 rows and the refused `PM-2026.13` are the values of FSD P4 v3 AC-P4-004-01 and of the fakes (ASM-3729).
- No build dependency: Day 1 by rule (Template and Rules §R5.7), in contract group CG-W4 because business epic EP08 is wave 4 in the W-MAP (§R5.6).

##### 4. Flow

1. Draft the OpenAPI 3.1 document for the four matrix operations under `/api/recovery/access/v1`, with the shared components the `rwb-access` operations use.
2. Draft `PermissionMatrix`, `PermissionMatrixRow`, `PermissionMatrixVersion` and `PermissionMatrixPage`: role code and name, class, default scope, area, letters, version label, status, valid-from and valid-to, row and role counts, author and approver references, decision-record reference, the role the version waits for and the page of rows.
3. State the completeness rule: one row for every active role against each of the 14 areas; an omitted role, a repeated pair and a letter outside the vocabulary are one refusal with the gap named, and the whole file is refused.
4. State the load-and-approve-before-effective rule: the load writes VALIDATED and no more; a version is APPROVED only through the gate of RWB-P4-AD010-APP and in force only from its valid-from date after that approval; an applied version is never edited and a change is a new dated version.
5. State the version-in-force rule: the matrix read answers the version whose valid-from is the latest not after the date asked and whose status is APPROVED or IN_FORCE, one version whole; a VALIDATED version is never answered as the matrix in force.
6. State the rights: Platform administration `R` for the three reads and `C` for the load, with an active role on every call and the 401 and 403 of the default deny rule.
7. Agree the error envelope and the message mapping for 401, 403, 404, 409, 422 and 503, with the business texts copied unchanged from the legacy story where the message exists.
8. Declare `rwb.access.AccessPolicyChanged.v1` on `rwb.access.events.v1` with change kind `MATRIX`, the version, the status, the effective date and the row count, and the decision-record type on `rwb.decision-record.v1`; declare no third event name.
9. Declare the consumed parameters read, the consumed reference-data read and the read-only ACE view with their owners and the one-hop budget, and declare no operation of another service as provided.
10. Publish the contract tables of section 12 and the fakes, then add the contract tests: schema validation, the whole-matrix rule, the version and date rule, the rights, the envelope, the owner declarations and the drift between a fake and the document.
11. Tag the baseline and hand it to RWB-P4-AD002-APP, to RWB-P4-AD010-APP for the approval side and to RWB-P4-E1037-CON and RWB-P4-E1037-APP, whose guard checks every endpoint against the version this document declares.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The document fails OpenAPI 3.1 validation | The pipeline fails and no baseline is tagged | None | AC1 |
| X2 | A schema declares a person's name, an e-mail address or the letters of a named individual | The review fails and the property is removed | None | AC2 |
| X3 | A field of the matrix or the version has no source definition | The field is named by this document's own decision and the gap is carried | None | AC2 |
| X4 | The document declares a load that approves, or a version in force with no valid-from date | The review fails: the load writes VALIDATED, the approval is another gate, an applied version is never rewritten | None | AC3 |
| X5 | The document declares another event name, or a second access event for a matrix load | The review fails; the event is `rwb.access.AccessPolicyChanged.v1` with change kind `MATRIX` | None | AC4 |
| X6 | The document declares an operation or a table of another service as provided | The review fails; the parameters read, the list read and the ACE view are documented as consumed | None | AC5 |
| X7 | An error response carries no `messageId`, or one outside the agreed set | The contract test fails and the merge is blocked | None | AC6 |
| X8 | A fake drifts from the document | The contract test fails and the merge is blocked | None | AC7 |
| X9 | The parameters read, the reference read or the ACE view misses the 2 s budget | The call answers 503 and the document declares the 503 | MSG-GEN-006 | AC5, AC6 |
| X10 | The document declares a complete matrix as a fixed row count | The review fails: the count is computed from `role` and LOV-CAPABILITY, never a constant | None | AC3 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | No build dependency; it reads the ownership map, the platform envelopes, the guard contract, the parameters and reference-data contracts of RWB-P3-E1042-CON and RWB-P3-E1043-CON and the ACE-view contract of RWB-P1-E1069-APP |
| Negotiable | The field-level detail of the four schemas and the payload are settled with the app story and the approval story; the base, rights, event name and envelope are fixed by the architecture and the Workbench |
| Valuable | Unblocks the app story on Day 1 with a written answer to "which letters does this role hold on this date, and which version is in force", and keeps the approval, the masking rules and the roles catalogue out of the matrix contract |
| Estimable | One document, four schemas, one error envelope with seven message IDs, one event declaration, nine contract tables, six fakes and eight contract tests |
| Small | Fits one sprint with the contract tests |
| Testable | Every criterion is tested against the artefact, not against a business outcome |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: The permission matrix as a versioned load, contract baseline for rwb-access

  Background:
    Given the service naming rule of the platform library is in force
    Given the permission matrix is the "permission" rows of one "matrix_version" of one environment in "rwb_access"
    Given a complete matrix holds every active role once against each of the 14 capability areas of "LOV-CAPABILITY"

  Scenario: AC1 The OpenAPI 3.1 document describes the four matrix operations (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the OpenAPI 3.1 document of rwb-access is published
    When it is validated against the OpenAPI 3.1 schema
    Then it validates with no error
    Then it declares the base /api/recovery/access/v1
    Then it declares POST /admin/permission-matrix-loads, GET /admin/permission-matrix, GET /admin/permission-matrix-versions and GET /admin/permission-matrix-versions/{matrixVersion} with the owner rwb-access
    Then the three reads declare Platform administration with the right R, and the load declares Platform administration with the right C
    Then every operation declares 401, 403, 404, 409, 422 and 503
    Then the load declares the Idempotency-Key header and the three reads declare none

  Scenario: AC2 The four schemas carry the matrix, the version and the dates (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the schemas PermissionMatrix, PermissionMatrixRow, PermissionMatrixVersion and PermissionMatrixPage of the document
    Then PermissionMatrixRow carries roleCode, roleName, roleClass, defaultScope, capabilityArea, letters and matrixVersion
    Then PermissionMatrix carries matrixVersion, versionStatus, validFrom, validTo, validOn, rowCount and the rows
    Then PermissionMatrixVersion carries matrixVersion, versionStatus, validFrom, validTo, rowCount, roleCount, capabilityAreaCount, authorReference, approverReference, decisionRecordEntryRef, pendingApproverRole and the rows
    Then PermissionMatrixPage carries items, page, size and total with a default of 50 and a maximum of 200
    Then the letters are declared as C, R, U, D and A in that order or a dash, and the version status is declared with the values of LOV-VERSION-STATUS
    Then no schema, no parameter and no example declares a person's name, an e-mail address, an identity number or the letters of a named individual
    Then the valid-from and valid-to dates, the approver reference and the pending approver role are declared as fields of the version, because no physical column is specified for them in the source documents

  Scenario: AC3 The whole-matrix rule and the load-and-approve-before-effective rule (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the description of the load operation and of the three reads
    Then the load declares that a complete matrix holds exactly one row for every active role against each of the 14 areas of LOV-CAPABILITY
    Then the load declares that a file with a missing role, a repeated role and area pair or a letter outside the vocabulary is refused in full with the gap named, and that no row of a refused version is stored
    Then the load answers the version VALIDATED, and the document states that the approval of a version is not the load and belongs to the gate of RWB-P4-AD010-APP
    Then the document states that a version is in force only when it is APPROVED and only from its valid-from date, and that an applied version is never edited
    Then the matrix read answers the version whose valid-from is the latest not after the date asked and whose status is APPROVED or IN_FORCE
    Then the document states that a VALIDATED version is never answered as the matrix in force, that the expected row count is computed and never a constant, and that a new matrix needs no deployment and no code change

  Scenario: AC4 The matrix load is published as the access-policy event (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the events section of the document
    Then rwb.access.AccessPolicyChanged.v1 is declared on the topic rwb.access.events.v1 with change kind MATRIX, the version label, the resulting status, the effective date and the row count
    Then rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1 is declared on the shared topic rwb.decision-record.v1 for the entry of the load and of the refusal
    Then no other event name is declared for this capability, and no second name for a matrix load appears anywhere in the document
    Then no payload carries a letter of a role, a user reference or a personal field

  Scenario: AC5 The consumed reads are declared as consumed (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the consumed section of the document
    Then GET /api/recovery/case/v1/admin/parameters is declared with the owner rwb-case and the parameters contract RWB-P3-E1042-CON, for the approver role rwb.refload.approver.permission
    Then GET /api/recovery/case/v1/admin/lists/{listCode} is declared with the owner rwb-case and the reference-data contract RWB-P3-E1043-CON, for LOV-CAPABILITY and its 14 values
    Then the read-only ACE group view v_ace_iam_group is declared with the owner of RWB-P1-E1069-APP, its fields DF-ACE-301 to DF-ACE-304 and its data_as_of
    Then all three are declared one hop, with the 2 s budget and the 503 when the read does not answer in time
    Then no operation, table or list owned by another service is declared as provided

  Scenario: AC6 Every failure is one envelope with one message (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the error envelope component of the document
    When a 401, 403, 404, 409, 422 or 503 response is produced by any of the four operations
    Then the body carries the code, the message, the messageId, the traceId and the field list, with the problem media type
    Then 401 carries MSG-P4-001, 403 carries MSG-P4-002, 404 and 409 carry MSG-GEN-004, 422 carries MSG-GEN-001 or MSG-P1-002 and 503 carries MSG-P7-003 or MSG-GEN-006
    Then the 422 of the completeness rule carries MSG-P1-002 with the missing role or the repeated pair named
    Then the message texts are the legacy texts where the message already exists, and the break-glass warning MSG-P4-004 is declared on no operation

  Scenario: AC7 The fakes match the document and carry no personal data (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the six contract fakes of section 12.8
    When a fake is compared with the document
    Then the matrix fake answers the four paths of 12.1: PM-2026.11 in force, PM-2026.12 VALIDATED with its valid-from date and 756 rows, the refused PM-2026.13 with a missing role and a repeated pair, 409 for an existing label and 403 with MSG-P4-002
    Then the reference-data fake answers LOV-CAPABILITY with its 14 values in force, and one value list version later
    Then the parameters fake answers rwb.refload.approver.permission as "RW-SECADM"
    Then the decision-record fake answers the entry append and the 503 with MSG-P7-003
    Then a contract test fails on any drift between a fake and the document, and no fake carries a name or an e-mail address
```

These seven criteria test the artefact only. None restates a legacy criterion: the three legacy criteria of RWB-AD-002 are owned by RWB-P4-AD002-APP and their tests sit in section 16 as the cases this contract is the ground of.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | One REST base per service: `/api/recovery/access/v1`; the document never declares another service's path, table or event | DP-13; Architecture v5 slides 14, 41 |
| BR2 | A consumed read is described as consumed, never as provided; its owner comes from the ownership map | DP-11; Ownership Map v1 |
| BR3 | Events are named `rwb.<short>.<Event>.v1` on `rwb.<short>.events.v1`, the shared record type stays on `rwb.decision-record.v1`, and the envelope is CloudEvents 1.0 | Architecture v5 slides 14, 20, 43; Template and Rules §R4 |
| BR4 | This capability publishes one event, `rwb.access.AccessPolicyChanged.v1`, with change kind `MATRIX`; `rwb.access.DoaLimitChanged.v1` belongs to the delegation table and no third name exists | Architecture v5 slides 14, 20, 43; ASM-3730 |
| BR5 | The contract declares no table of another service: `lov_value`, `reference_row`, `reference_version`, `parameter_catalog` and `parameter_value` are P3's, `decision_log_entry` and `approval` are P7's, `assignment` is P3's and `document` is P5's | DP-01; ownership map |
| BR6 | A complete matrix holds exactly one row for every active role against each of the 14 areas, a file with any gap is refused in full with the gap named, and the expected count is computed and never a constant | Legacy AC1, AC2; FSD P4 v3 AC-EXC-P4-004-02; TSD P4 v3 T3.2; ASM-3729 |
| BR7 | The letters are `C`, `R`, `U`, `D` and `A` in that order or a dash, and the version status is LOV-VERSION-STATUS (LOADED, VALIDATED, APPROVED, IN_FORCE, SUPERSEDED, ROLLED_BACK, REFUSED) | FSD P4 v3 A2.4; DF-REF-043; TSD P4 v3 T3.2 |
| BR8 | The load writes a version VALIDATED and never APPROVED or IN_FORCE; the approval is the gate of RWB-P4-AD010-APP and a version is in force only from its valid-from date and only after it | Legacy AC1, AC3; ASM-3728; ASM-3727 |
| BR9 | An applied version is never edited: a change is a new version with its own label and effective date | Legacy AC3; TSD P4 v3 T4; DP-15 |
| BR10 | The three reads need Platform administration `R` and the load needs `C`; an active role is required on every call, and the default deny rule answers 401 and 403 | TSD P4 v3 T6.1; FSD P4 v3 VR-P4-004-1, VR-P4-004-2; ASM-1454 |
| BR11 | The approver role and the 14 areas are read as data through the parameters and reference-data contracts, and neither is declared as a constant or an enumerated list of the document | DP-06; DP-07; ASM-3728 |
| BR12 | Error responses use one envelope and one message ID per condition, and the business texts are copied unchanged from the legacy story where the message exists | Architecture v5 slide 11; Template and Rules §R7.2 s14 |
| BR13 | No schema, parameter, example or fake declares a name, an e-mail address, an identity number or the letters of a named individual | REQ-ACA-005; guardrails |
| BR14 | A schema change is additive within major version 1; a removed, renamed or retyped field is a new major version | Architecture v5 slide 42 |

| In review | Consumer sign-off | RWB-P4-AD002-APP, RWB-P4-AD010-APP and the wave 4 harness accept the document and the fakes | Baselined |

| Baselined | Breaking change | A field is removed, renamed or retyped | New major version drafted |

A matrix version has its own states — VALIDATED, APPROVED, IN_FORCE, SUPERSEDED, ROLLED_BACK, REFUSED — and they are the app story's and the approval story's data states, declared here and not states of this document.

##### 11. Data

The contract baseline declares shapes, not business values.

| Item | Content |
|---|---|
| Matrix row | `roleCode` (DF-REF-035), `roleName` (DF-REF-036), `roleClass` (DF-REF-037, LOV-ROLE-CLASS), `defaultScope` (DF-REF-038, LOV-SCOPE), `capabilityArea` (DF-REF-042, LOV-CAPABILITY), `letters` (DF-REF-043), `matrixVersion` (DF-REF-044) |
| Matrix | `matrixVersion`, `versionStatus`, `validFrom`, `validTo`, `validOn`, `rowCount`, `rows[]` |
| Matrix version | `matrixVersion`, `versionStatus`, `validFrom`, `validTo`, `rowCount`, `roleCount`, `capabilityAreaCount`, `authorReference`, `approverReference`, `decisionRecordEntryRef`, `pendingApproverRole`, `rows[]` |
| Matrix page | `items[]`, `page`, `size` (default 50, maximum 200), `total` |
| Load request | multipart: the file, `matrixVersion` and `validFrom`; the `Idempotency-Key` header |
| Version status | The values of LOV-VERSION-STATUS; the storage is the standard `state` column of TSD P4 v3 T3.0 |
| Version dates and approver | `validFrom`, `validTo`, `approverReference`, this key's own decision (GAP-2264; ASM-3727) |
| Capability areas | LOV-CAPABILITY with its 14 values, read through DP-07 |
| Approver role | `rwb.refload.approver.permission`, read through DP-06 |
| Event payloads | IDs, codes, counts and times only; no letters, no user reference, no personal field |
| Decision-record entry | The `AC-VERS` and `AC-DENY` entries through DP-03; their fields are the library's and are not redefined here |

Two values the sources do not fix are this baseline's own decision. The valid-from and valid-to dates, the approver reference and the pending approver role have no physical column in TSD P4 v3 T3.1 while legacy AC3 needs them — **Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2264; ASM-3727)**. The operation paths, their rights and their answer shapes have no ownership-map row and no T-A row, and the legacy rows name Reference data and Rules and parameters — **Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2264; ASM-1453, ASM-1454)**. The field names, types and lengths of the four schemas are fixed by this document and its own decision, and no physical column is dictated by it (ASM-3732).

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner `rwb-access` (P4); base `/api/recovery/access/v1`.

| Method | Path | Documented shape | Access |
|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/admin/permission-matrix-loads` | multipart with the file, `matrixVersion` and `validFrom`, and the `Idempotency-Key` header; `PermissionMatrixVersion` out with status VALIDATED | Platform administration `C` |
| GET | `/admin/permission-matrix` | `PermissionMatrixPage`: query `roleCode`, `capabilityArea`, `matrixVersion`, `validOn`, `page`, `size`; the rows in force on `validOn` | Platform administration `R` |
| GET | `/admin/permission-matrix-versions/{matrixVersion}` | `PermissionMatrixVersion`: status, dates, row and role counts, author and approver references, decision-record reference, pending approver role and rows | Platform administration `R` |
| GET | `/admin/permission-matrix-versions` | `PermissionMatrixPage` of the versions: label, status, dates and row count; query `status`, `page`, `size` | Platform administration `R` |

Errors for all four: 401 no session or no Workbench role (MSG-P4-001), 403 no right (MSG-P4-002), 404 an unknown label (MSG-GEN-004), 409 a label that exists or a repeated key answered differently (MSG-GEN-004), 422 a missing or invalid field (MSG-GEN-001) or an incomplete matrix (MSG-P1-002), 503 the record entry not written (MSG-P7-003) or the reference list not readable (MSG-GEN-006). The load is idempotent by `Idempotency-Key`; the same key returns the first answer and writes no second version. Major version 1 sits in the path (BR14).

`GET /admin/roles` (API-P4-007), `GET /admin/access-log` (API-P4-008) and `GET /me/session` (API-P4-012) are the service's own operations of RWB-P4-E1019-APP, RWB-P4-E1037-CON, RWB-P4-AD007-APP and RWB-P4-E1022-CON; this document neither restates nor changes them, and the matrix answer here is the flat `permission` rows of one version, not the roles catalogue answer.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

One hop per call, 2 s timeout and a breaker per downstream (DP-11).

| Method | Path | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/admin/parameters` | P3 `rwb-case`, RWB-P3-E1042-CON (DP-06) | The approver role `rwb.refload.approver.permission`, so the role a version waits for is data |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/admin/lists/{listCode}` | P3 `rwb-case`, RWB-P3-E1043-CON (DP-07) | LOV-CAPABILITY with its 14 values in force, which a complete matrix must cover |

The ACE group reference is a read-only SQL read and not a REST call: `recovery.v_ace_iam_group` (DF-ACE-301 to DF-ACE-304), owner RWB-P1-E1069-APP (DP-05), one hop in the same database, declared with its `data_as_of` and its 503. Nothing else is consumed. The service's own `POST /api/recovery/access/v1/authorise` is declared by RWB-P4-E1037-CON and is not declared again here.

###### 12.3 Events published

| Event | Topic | Owner | Contract element |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.access.AccessPolicyChanged.v1` | `rwb.access.events.v1` | P4 `rwb-access` | Change kind `MATRIX`, the version label, the status VALIDATED, the effective date, the row count and the time |
| `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` | `rwb.decision-record.v1` | PLT library, consumed by P7 | Entry id, decision code (`AC-VERS`, `AC-DENY`), the version label, the row count and the time |

Both use the CloudEvents 1.0 envelope with id, source, type, specversion, time, subject and datacontenttype. No message carries a letter of a role, a user reference, a name, an e-mail address or an identity number. `rwb.access.DoaLimitChanged.v1` is not declared here and no second name exists for a matrix load (BR4, ASM-3730).

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. `rwb-access` is a reference-data owner in Architecture v5 slide 14 (events: none) and this capability adds no subscription.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None. The four operations are synchronous REST answers in the caller's thread with no workflow, activity or signal. The six-monthly access review Schedule (JOB-18) is RWB-P4-AD008-CON's.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. Nothing about a matrix runs on a clock: the valid-from date is a row value the read resolves.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Contracted use |
|---|---|---|
| `permission` | P4 (`rwb_access`) | The matrix rows and their version label (DF-REF-040 to DF-REF-044); the version dates and the approver reference are this key's own decision (GAP-2264; ASM-3727) |
| `role` | P4 (`rwb_access`) | The role code, name, class and default scope a row and a complete file are checked against; read only |
| `v_ace_iam_group` | ACE, read-only view, owner RWB-P1-E1069-APP | The group reference of the caller: `entra_group`, `role_code`, `source_system`, `data_as_of`; never written |
| `lov_value`, `reference_row`, `reference_version`, `parameter_catalog`, `parameter_value` | P3 (`rwb_case`) | Appear nowhere as tables; the list and the parameter are consumed operations (DP-01, DP-06, DP-07) |
| `decision_log_entry`, `approval` | P7 (`rwb_decision`) | Appear nowhere; the local entry is the library's and the central ledger is P7's |
| `assignment` | P3 (`rwb_case`) | Appears nowhere; the legacy Data table names it |
| `document` | P5 (`rwb_document`) | Appears nowhere; the legacy Data table names it |

No foreign key crosses a schema, and the contract names no table outside `rwb_access` except the read-only ACE view it consumes.

| Fake | Documented answer | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| `rwb-access` permission-matrix WireMock | The four paths of 12.1: `PM-2026.11` in force, `PM-2026.12` VALIDATED with validFrom 1 December 2026 and 756 rows, the refused `PM-2026.13` with a missing role and a repeated pair, the stored answer for a repeated `Idempotency-Key`, 409 for an existing label, 422 with MSG-GEN-001 and MSG-P1-002, 403 with MSG-P4-002 and 503 with MSG-P7-003 | App story, approval story, contract tests, wave 4 harness |
| Matrix file fixtures | The accepted `PM-2026.12` and the refused `PM-2026.13` | App story, contract tests |

| Parameters fake (RWB-P3-E1042-CON) | `rwb.refload.approver.permission` = "RW-SECADM" | App story, contract tests |

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Count | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| REST | 4 provided, 2 consumed | The load, the matrix read, the version read and the versions list provided; the parameters read and the list read consumed; one hop, 2 s timeout; plus one read-only SQL read of the ACE view |
| Kafka | 2 published, 0 consumed | `rwb.access.AccessPolicyChanged.v1` and `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` |
| Temporal | None | No workflow, activity or Schedule |
| File | One upload | The matrix file arrives in the multipart body of the load; no file is stored or served |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Deliverables.** `openapi/rwb-access-permission-matrix-v1.yaml` (OpenAPI 3.1) with the four operations and the shared components, the four schemas, the `contract/error-envelope.yaml` with the agreed message IDs, the event declaration with change kind `MATRIX`, the parameters stub with its owner, the LOV-CAPABILITY stub, the ACE-view stub with its `data_as_of` and the six WireMock mapping sets.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-08 | RecoveryAccessGuard | Authorise contract of rwb-access and the guard library | H RWB-PLT-E1037-CON; C RWB-P4-E1037-CON |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

A contract story adds no build dependency of its own: each DP above is **referred to, and the consuming story carries the dependency**, and that story is RWB-P4-AD002-APP, whose H row carries the five platform CON stories and RWB-P4-E1037-CON and whose C row carries RWB-P3-E1042-CON and RWB-P3-E1043-CON. DP-03 is contracted as the entry declared on `rwb.decision-record.v1`; DP-05 as the read-only ACE view through the P1 contract; DP-06 as the consumed parameters read; DP-07 as the consumed list read; DP-08 as the guard of every operation; DP-13 as the base of the document; DP-19 as the composite route of SCR-43.

**Build steps**

1. OpenAPI 3.1 skeleton with the base path, the security scheme, the error responses and the shared components; schema lint in the pipeline.
2. The four operations and the four schemas of section 11, with the page, the version, the status and the dates.
3. The completeness rule and the version rule in the operation descriptions: one row per role per area, a whole-file refusal, VALIDATED at the load, APPROVED only by the gate, in force only from the date, an applied version never edited (BR6, BR8, BR9).
4. The rights of the three reads and of the load, and the 401 and 403 of the default deny rule.
5. The error envelope and the message-ID mapping with the legacy texts copied unchanged and the note on MSG-P4-004.
6. The event declaration and the decision-record type with the change kind and the payload.
7. The consumed parameters read, the consumed list read and the ACE view with their owners, the one-hop rule, the 2 s budget and the 503.
8. The six fakes and the fixtures of section 12.8.
9. The eight contract tests; a drift between a fake and the document fails the build.
10. Baseline tag and the sign-off note of the app story, the approval story and the guard story.

**Feature switch.** None. The four operations are operations of the service; the load is a data change guarded by the `C` letter.

**Consumer sign-off**

| Consumer | What it accepts |
|---|---|
| RWB-P4-AD002-APP | The four operations, the four schemas, the completeness and version rules, the event declaration and the six fakes |
| RWB-P4-AD010-APP, the approval gate | The state a load leaves (VALIDATED), the version read and the pending approver role it approves against |
| RWB-P4-E1037-CON, RWB-P4-E1037-APP, the guard | The letters, the version-in-force rule and the matrix row the guard reads at every endpoint |
| The wave 4 harness | The fakes of 12.8 and the parameters, list and ACE-view stubs |

The deprecation window of a published field and the retention of the contract fakes are **Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2264; ASM-3733)**, and the baseline is used while its stories remain Draft under D-RCV-60 with no approval record (ASM-3733).

**Done when.** The OpenAPI document validates in the pipeline, the eight contract tests pass, the six fakes answer every consumed and every provided path, and the app, approval and guard stories have accepted the baseline.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P4-001 | No session, no Workbench role | You have no Recovery Workbench role. Ask your team manager to request one. |
| MSG-P4-002 | No Platform administration `R` for a read, or no `C` for the load | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-GEN-001 | A required field is empty, the label is too long or the valid-from is in the past | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-P1-002 | A role is missing, a pair is repeated, a letter is outside the vocabulary or a role code is unknown | The {source} load for {date} was refused: {check}. The previous load is still in use. |
| MSG-GEN-004 | The label exists, or the version asked for does not exist | Someone else changed this record. Reload it to see their change. |
| MSG-GEN-006 | The reference list or the parameter cannot be read | The reference data is not available. Try again later. |
| MSG-P7-003 | The decision-record entry could not be written | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |

The message IDs are contract elements; the text is the agreed text, taken from the legacy story where the message already existed. The legacy warning MSG-P4-004 ("Emergency access is on until {time}. Every action is recorded.") is the break-glass warning of RWB-P4-AD006-APP and RWB-P4-E1039-APP and is declared on no operation. The legacy permission rows "Reference data C: RW-COE, RW-REFADM" and "Rules and parameters A: RW-RISK" are not carried as the rights of these operations; the rights are Platform administration `R` and `C` (ASM-1454).

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in the contract: labels, dates, letters, the approver role and the 14 areas are rows, parameters and consumed contract answers; the document fixes names and types only.
- No personal data in a schema, an example or a fake: a matrix row is a role code, an area and letters, and a name or an e-mail address in the document fails the review (BR13).
- The contract names only `rwb-access` tables, the read-only ACE view it consumes, and operations owned by `rwb-access` or declared as consumed (DP-01, BR5).
- One REST base, one topic and one event name for the capability, with the shared record type on `rwb.decision-record.v1` (DP-13, BR3, BR4).
- The load and the approval are two acts: VALIDATED is the declared end state of the load, so no consumer can read the load as an approval (BR8).
- A version is in force only from its date and only after its approval, and an applied version is never edited, so no consumer reads "the latest rows" as the truth (BR6, BR9).
- The reference list and the approver role are consumed, never enumerated, so a new area or a new approver role is a data change with no contract change (BR11).
- Every example and every fake is synthetic; no production role, person or entitlement is copied into a schema or a fake.
- The error envelope and the CloudEvents envelope come from the platform library; this story narrows them but never redefines them.

##### 1. Story

As an **application owner**, I want **the permission matrix of roles against the 14 capability areas loaded as one complete, dated version of `permission` in `rwb_access`, checked as a whole**, so that **a permission changes without a code release and every change waits for an approval and takes effect on its date**.

This is the rwb-access slice of legacy RWB-AD-002 and its load half: the matrix rows of one version, the whole-file checks, the version status before approval, the effective-from date, the matrix read, the version read and the versions list.

- **Naming:** base `/api/recovery/access/v1` (DP-13), schema `rwb_access`, topic `rwb.access.events.v1` with names `rwb.access.<Event>.v1`, queue `rwb-access` in namespace `rwb-recovery` (unused here), package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.access`.
- **A matrix row:** one `permission` row is one role against one capability area — `role_id` (DF-REF-041), `capability_area` (DF-REF-042, LOV-CAPABILITY), `letters` (DF-REF-043, varchar(5), `C`, `R`, `U`, `D`, `A` in that order or a dash) and `matrix_version` (DF-REF-044, varchar(20)) (FSD P4 v3 A2.4 field catalog; TSD P4 v3 T3.1). The legacy wording stands: "the permission matrix of roles against the 14 capability areas".
- **The 14 areas:** CASE_RECORD, QUEUE_AND_ALLOCATION, TREATMENT_AND_OFFER, LITIGATION, ASSET_AND_DISPOSAL, DEBT_SALE, WRITE_OFF_AND_POSTING, DOCUMENTS, RULES_AND_PARAMETERS, REFERENCE_DATA, DECISION_LOG, PARTNER_PORTAL, REPORTING, PLATFORM_ADMINISTRATION (TSD P4 v3 T3.2), read through the reference-data contract of rwb-case (DP-07), never by SQL and never as a constant.
- **Version and status:** the label is `matrix_version`; the status is the standard `state` column (TSD P4 v3 T3.0) in the vocabulary LOV-VERSION-STATUS (LOADED, VALIDATED, APPROVED, IN_FORCE, SUPERSEDED, ROLLED_BACK, REFUSED). The valid-from and valid-to dates and the approver reference have no column in TSD P4 v3 T3.1 — **Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2263; ASM-3727)**.
- **The boundary with the approval:** this story writes a version and stops at VALIDATED. **RWB-P4-AD010-APP owns the approve, the verify and the rollback**, and AC1 ends where the legacy criterion ends, at "waits for the application owner's approval"; the approver role is read as the parameter `rwb.refload.approver.permission` through DP-06 (ASM-3728).
- **The four operations:** the matrix load, the matrix read, the version read and the versions list, at the paths fixed by RWB-P4-AD002-CON on the service base. Neither the paths nor their right has an ownership-map row or a T-A row, where the only role read is `GET /admin/roles` (API-P4-007) — **Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2263; ASM-1453)**.
- **The check is whole:** one row per active `role` row per area, computed from `role` and LOV-CAPABILITY and never a constant; any gap or letter outside the vocabulary refuses the file in full and names the missing role (legacy AC2; ASM-3729).
- **The effective date:** a version answers as the matrix in force only when it is APPROVED and only from its valid-from date; from that date every endpoint checks against it through the guard of RWB-P4-E1037-CON and RWB-PLT-E1037-CON (DP-08), which reads the `permission` rows in force on the day of the request (legacy AC3).
- **The change is recorded:** every load and every refusal writes one local decision-record entry through DP-03 — `AC-VERS` for a version written, `AC-DENY` for a refusal — on the shared topic `rwb.decision-record.v1`; the central ledger stays P7 rwb-decision's.
- **The signal:** `rwb.access.AccessPolicyChanged.v1` on `rwb.access.events.v1` with change kind `MATRIX`, the version, the status, the effective date and the row count, and no personal data (ASM-3730).
- **Authority:** the letters come from the caller's own `role` and `permission` rows through the authorise contract (DP-08). The matrix is Platform administration in TSD P4 v3 T6.1 — `R` for the reads, `C` for the load, held by RW-SECADM (CRUDA) and RW-PLATADM (CRUD); the legacy rows "Reference data C: RW-COE, RW-REFADM" and "Rules and parameters A: RW-RISK" are not carried (ASM-1454).
- **Screens:** SCR-43 Roles and access shows the roles, their permissions, the scope and the group mapping, served by the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19; RWB-PLT-N001-CON). Where the load form sits is **Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2263; ASM-3731)**.
- **Not this story:** the approval, verify and rollback (RWB-P4-AD010-APP, RWB-P4-AD009-APP); the roles catalogue and the masking policy (RWB-P4-E1019-APP, RWB-P4-E1037-APP, RWB-P4-E1037-CON); the sibling slices RWB-P4-AD001-APP, RWB-P4-AD004-APP, RWB-P4-AD005-APP, RWB-P4-AD008-APP and RWB-P4-AD006-APP; and the legacy Data rows `assignment` (P3 rwb-case) and `document` (P5 rwb-document), neither read nor written here.

##### 2. Business rationale

What a role may do lives in documents and people's heads today, so a permission change needs a code release or a manual data fix, and audit findings record unsuitable access for that reason. Legacy RWB-AD-002 answered it by loading the matrix as one versioned file approved before it took effect. The realignment keeps the answer and makes it a service answer: the matrix is rows of `permission` in `rwb_access`, a version is a label with a status and an effective date, and a file is checked as a whole before a single row is stored.

Three consequences are the point of the split. The matrix is data, not a release — the measure is rule and limit changes made without a code release, target 100 percent (FSD P4 v3 A2.4). The check is whole-file, because a missing role silently removes a right from everyone holding that role, so a refused load leaves the version in force untouched and names the gap. And the load and the approval are two acts with two owners: the load needs the `C` letter of Platform administration, and the approval is RWB-P4-AD010-APP's gate, so a version cannot approve itself by being loaded (ASM-3728).

The realignment also corrects the legacy right. The legacy row set made the load "Reference data C" for RW-COE and RW-REFADM, but the matrix is role administration and TSD P4 v3 T6.1 puts the `permission` rows in Platform administration; the reference data of the estate (`lov_value`, `reference_row`, `reference_version`) is P3 rwb-case's. The letters are therefore read from Platform administration (ASM-1454), and the reference-data contract is consumed for one thing only: the 14 areas a complete file must cover.

The matrix reaches the estate as one signal. `rwb.access.AccessPolicyChanged.v1` is the one access-policy event the architecture gives this service (Architecture v5 slides 14 and 43), services refresh their cached permission data on it (slide 20), and a matrix load **is** an access-policy change (ASM-3730).

##### 4. Flow

1. The administrator opens SCR-43 through the composite route of DP-19; the route calls the matrix read (or the versions list) and the access-log read in parallel, one hop each, and merges them.
2. The guard authorises at the door (DP-08): `R` of Platform administration for the reads, `C` for the load. No Workbench role is 401 with MSG-P4-001 and a missing letter is 403 with MSG-P4-002; both write one `AC-DENY` entry before the answer leaves.
3. The load is `POST /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/permission-matrix-loads` with a multipart body — the file, the `matrixVersion` label, the `validFrom` date — and an `Idempotency-Key`; a repeated key answers the first answer and stores no second version.
4. `CapabilityAreaReader` reads LOV-CAPABILITY through DP-07 and gets the 14 areas in force; where the read misses the 2 s budget the load answers 503 with MSG-GEN-006 and writes nothing.
5. `PermissionMatrixChecks` runs over the whole file before a row is written: every active `role` row once per area, no repeated pair, letters within `C`, `R`, `U`, `D`, `A` or the dash and at most 5 characters, every role code an active role, the label present and within 20 characters, the valid-from present and not earlier than the load day, no required field empty (MSG-GEN-001).
6. A file that fails any check is refused in full: 422 with MSG-P1-002 naming the check, the missing role or the duplicate pair; no row is stored and the version in force is unchanged (legacy AC2).
7. An existing label is 409 with MSG-GEN-004 and nothing is written.
8. The rows are written in one transaction with the standard columns, the version's dates and approver reference; the version is LOADED while written and VALIDATED on commit. No version is APPROVED and none is IN_FORCE.
9. `MatrixVersionRecorder` writes one `AC-VERS` entry in the same transaction through DP-03 — label, row count, role count, effective date, acting user reference, time, no name — with its outbox row; where the entry cannot be written nothing is stored and the call is 503 with MSG-P7-003.
10. After the commit one `rwb.access.AccessPolicyChanged.v1` is published with change kind `MATRIX`, the version, the status VALIDATED, the effective date and the row count — no letters, no user reference (ASM-3730).
11. The load answers 201 with the version: label, status VALIDATED, dates, counts, author reference, decision-record reference and the role it waits for from the parameter (DP-06). The version waits for the application owner's approval (legacy AC1).
12. The version read answers one version by label whether or not it is in force; a valid-from in the future or a status VALIDATED is answered as a version, never as the matrix in force.
13. The versions list answers the labels with their status and dates, filtered by status.
14. The matrix read answers the rows in force on the date asked: the version whose valid-from is the latest not after that date and whose status is APPROVED or IN_FORCE, one version whole and never a mixture.
15. From its valid-from date every endpoint checks against the new version, because the guard reads the `permission` rows in force on the day of the request (legacy AC3); no deployment, restart or manual cache flush is needed.
16. Every call is one hop on the caller's thread inside the 2 s budget (DP-11); the group reference arrives read-only from `v_ace_iam_group` of the same database (DP-05).

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A required field is empty, the label exceeds 20 characters, or the valid-from is in the past | 422 with the field named; nothing written | MSG-GEN-001 | AC2 |
| X2 | A role of the environment is missing from the file | 422, refused in full with the missing role named; the version in force stays | MSG-P1-002 | AC2 |
| X3 | A role and area pair appears twice | 422 naming the duplicate pair; nothing stored | MSG-P1-002 | AC2 |
| X4 | A letter is outside the vocabulary, or the letter string is longer than 5 characters | 422 naming the row and the letters; nothing stored | MSG-P1-002 | AC2 |
| X5 | The file names a role code the environment does not hold as an active `role` row | 422 naming the role code; nothing stored | MSG-P1-002 | AC2 |
| X6 | The version label already exists | 409 with the envelope; the stored version is answered | MSG-GEN-004 | AC1 |
| X7 | The caller holds no `C` for the load or no `R` for a read | 403 before any row is read or written, one `AC-DENY` entry | MSG-P4-002 | AC1 |
| X8 | The caller holds no Workbench role | 401, one `AC-DENY` entry | MSG-P4-001 | AC1 |
| X9 | LOV-CAPABILITY cannot be read through DP-07 | 503; nothing written and the version in force unchanged | MSG-GEN-006 | AC1, AC2 |
| X10 | The decision-record entry cannot be written | 503; no row stored and the version in force unchanged | MSG-P7-003 | AC1 |
| X11 | Two loads of the same label arrive at once | One stored, one entry; the other 409 and writes nothing | MSG-GEN-004 | AC1 |
| X12 | A read arrives while a load commits, or asks for a VALIDATED version | The read answers one version whole; a VALIDATED version is never answered as in force | None | AC3 |

No path of this story approves, verifies or rolls back a version; its only writes are the `permission` rows of a new version, its decision-record entry, its outbox row and the stored answer of an `Idempotency-Key`.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Builds against the matrix contract and its fakes, the decision-record library, the parameters and reference-data contracts and the guard; writes one service's own `permission` rows and reads its own `role` rows |
| Negotiable | Labels, dates, letters and the approver role are data rows and parameters; the story fixes the checks, the version rule and the read shapes |
| Valuable | A permission change is one checked file, one dated version, one recorded decision and one published access-policy event, with no release |
| Estimable | One migration adding the version dates, one check set, four operations, one record entry and one event |
| Small | Fits one sprint with its tests; the approval, the masking rules and the screens are other stories' |
| Testable | Every criterion is one automated test over synthetic role rows and a stubbed reference-data contract; no real role, person or entitlement is needed |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Permission matrix as a versioned load

  Background:
    Given the rwb-access base path is /api/recovery/access/v1 and the schema is rwb_access
    Given a matrix version is the "matrix_version" of the "permission" rows of one environment in "rwb_access"
    Given a complete matrix holds every active role once against each of the 14 capability areas of "LOV-CAPABILITY"

  Scenario: AC1 Load a matrix version (legacy RWB-AD-002 AC1)
    Given the rwb-case contract mock returns the 14 capability areas of LOV-CAPABILITY in force
    Given a matrix file with every role and area
    When the reference data administrator loads it
    Then it passes the checks and waits for the application owner's approval

  Scenario: AC2 Incomplete matrix refused (legacy RWB-AD-002 AC2)
    Given a file with a role missing
    When it is loaded
    Then the system refuses it in full with the missing role named

  Scenario: AC3 Takes effect on its date (legacy RWB-AD-002 AC3)
    Given an approved version with a valid from date
    When the date arrives
    Then every endpoint checks against the new version
```

The three criteria are the legacy criteria of RWB-AD-002, copied word for word with their origin tag. One Given line is added to AC1: the mocked answer of the reference-data contract (DP-07, the C dependency RWB-P3-E1043-CON) that returns the 14 areas of LOV-CAPABILITY in force, because the completeness rule of AC1 and AC2 is measured against that list. Every legacy value is kept character for character — the file "with every role and area", the missing role, the refusal "in full with the missing role named", the approved version "with a valid from date" and the rule that every endpoint checks against the new version.

AC1 ends where the legacy criterion ends, at "waits for the application owner's approval": the approval is RWB-P4-AD010-APP's (ASM-3728) and this story writes VALIDATED and no further. AC2 is answered by `PermissionMatrixChecks` over the whole file. AC3 is answered by the valid-from date this story stores and by the guard, which resolves the version in force on the day of the request for every endpoint.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | A matrix is one `permission` row per role and area: `role_id` (DF-REF-041), `capability_area` (DF-REF-042, LOV-CAPABILITY), `letters` (DF-REF-043) and `matrix_version` (DF-REF-044). No role code, area, label or date is written in code | Legacy Data table; TSD P4 v3 T3.1; FSD P4 v3 A2.4 |
| BR2 | A complete matrix holds exactly one row for every active `role` row against each of the 14 areas, and a file with any gap is refused in full with the missing role named | Legacy AC1, AC2; FSD P4 v3 AC-EXC-P4-004-02; TSD P4 v3 T3.2; ASM-3729 |
| BR3 | The letters are `C`, `R`, `U`, `D` and `A` in that order or the dash for none, and never anything else | FSD P4 v3 A2.4 field catalog; DF-REF-043 |
| BR4 | A version is a label with a status from LOV-VERSION-STATUS and a valid-from date; an applied version is never edited and a change is a new dated version | Legacy AC3; TSD P4 v3 T3.2, T4; DP-15 |
| BR5 | This story writes a version VALIDATED and stops: it never approves, verifies or rolls back, and the approval of the `permission` table is RWB-P4-AD010-APP's | Legacy AC1; ASM-3728 |
| BR6 | A version answers as the matrix in force only when it is APPROVED and only from its valid-from date; before that date the version in force before it answers for every endpoint | Legacy AC3; TSD P4 v3 T4; ASM-3727 |
| BR7 | The reads need the `R` letter of Platform administration and the load needs `C`; no Workbench role is 401 with MSG-P4-001, a missing letter is 403 with MSG-P4-002, and both refusals are recorded | TSD P4 v3 T6.1; FSD P4 v3 VR-P4-004-1, VR-P4-004-2; DP-08; ASM-1454 |
| BR8 | Every load and every refusal writes one local decision-record entry — `AC-VERS` or `AC-DENY` — and where the entry cannot be written no `permission` row is stored | DP-03; Principle 5; FSD P4 v3 AC-EXC-P4-004-07; MSG-P7-003 |
| BR9 | A matrix load is published as `rwb.access.AccessPolicyChanged.v1` with change kind `MATRIX`, the version, the status, the effective date and the row count, and no personal data; no second event name exists for it | Architecture v5 slides 14, 20, 43; ASM-3730 |
| BR10 | LOV-CAPABILITY is read through the reference-data contract (DP-07) and the approver role through the parameters contract (DP-06); never by SQL and never as a constant | DP-06; DP-07; ownership map |
| BR11 | No statement names a table of another service or a `public` table: `lov_value`, `reference_row`, `reference_version`, `parameter_catalog`, `parameter_value`, `decision_log_entry`, `assignment` and `document` are never read | DP-01; ownership map |
| BR12 | A repeated load with the same `Idempotency-Key` answers the first answer and stores no second version; two loads of one label are one stored version and one 409 | Architecture v5 slide 11; DP-09 idempotency rule |

Where the rules sit: BR1 to BR4 are answered from `permission` and from the reference list of the 14 areas, with the checks before the write. BR5 is the absence of an approve, verify or rollback operation. BR6 is the read predicate — status APPROVED or IN_FORCE and the latest valid-from not after the date asked. BR7 is the guard of DP-08 in one hop. BR8 is the decision-record library and the service-template outbox. BR9 is the publication after commit. BR10 is the two clients. BR11 is enforced by the module map and boundary rule BND-6 of RWB-P4-E1069-APP. BR12 is the stored answer of the load.

##### 9. State transitions

None for a case, a task or a session. The states here are the states of a matrix version (LOV-VERSION-STATUS, TSD P4 v3 T3.2, in the standard `state` column).

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| No version of the environment | a matrix is loaded by this story | Every check passes and the entry is written | The rows are VALIDATED under the label; no version is in force yet |
| No version of the environment | a matrix is loaded and a check fails, or the entry cannot be written | Any failed check, or a 503 from the record library | REFUSED; no row stored and nothing in force |
| VALIDATED | the approval of RWB-P4-AD010-APP | The approver's gate passes and the entry is written | APPROVED with its valid-from date; this story does not make the transition |
| APPROVED | the valid-from date arrives | None | IN_FORCE; the matrix read answers it and every endpoint checks against it |
| IN_FORCE | a later version is approved and its date arrives | None | SUPERSEDED; the later version answers from its date and the old rows stay readable for audit |
| IN_FORCE | a rollback (RWB-P4-AD009-APP, RWB-P4-AD010-APP) | The rollback gate passes | ROLLED_BACK; this story reads it only to refuse it as the matrix in force |

This story writes LOADED inside its transaction and VALIDATED on commit, and reads the later states the approval stories write.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| rwb-access service identity (per-service login, DP-02) | Answers the three reads, writes a matrix version, runs the checks, writes the decision-record entry and publishes the event |
| RW-SECADM, security administrator | CRUDA in Platform administration (TSD P4 v3 T6.1): loads a version and reads every version |
| RW-PLATADM, platform administrator | CRUD in Platform administration: loads a version as the security administrator does, and reads the versions |
| RW-AUDIT, internal audit | `R` in Platform administration: reads the matrix, the versions and the entries; writes nothing |
| RW-COE, center of excellence analyst | CRUD in Rules and parameters and `R` in Platform administration: reads the matrix only, because the matrix is not a rule or a parameter |
| RW-REFADM, reference data administrator | CRUD in Reference data and no right in Platform administration: does not load the matrix, which is not reference data (ASM-1454) |
| The application owner | Approves each version outside this story, on the gate of RWB-P4-AD010-APP (legacy AC1) |
| The guard (RWB-P4-E1037-CON, RWB-PLT-E1037-CON) | Resolves the letters of every caller and checks every endpoint against the version in force (DP-08) |
| Every other role and service identity | Reads the matrix through the guard and no operation of this story |
| Delegation of authority | No level applies: a permission letter is not a credit decision and no `delegation_limit` row is read |

The legacy permission table gives the rule-version approve the `A` letter of Rules and parameters for RW-RISK and the reference-load the `C` letter of Reference data for RW-COE and RW-REFADM. Neither row is kept for the matrix: the rule paths belong to the rule-version stories of this service and P7 rwb-decision (ASM-0040), the reference-load path belongs to P3 rwb-case (ASM-0041), and the matrix is Platform administration in TSD P4 v3 T6.1 (ASM-1454).

##### 11. Data

| BR Field ID | Table | Field | Read or write |
|---|---|---|---|
| DF-REF-040 | `permission` (`rwb_access`) | id | Written, one per row of a new version |
| DF-REF-041 | `permission` | role_id | Written, from the role the file names |
| DF-REF-042 | `permission` | capability_area (LOV-CAPABILITY) | Written, one of the 14 areas |
| DF-REF-043 | `permission` | letters | Written, `C`, `R`, `U`, `D`, `A` in that order or the dash |
| DF-REF-044 | `permission` | matrix_version | Written and read; the label of the row |
| DF-REF-034 to DF-REF-038 | `role` (`rwb_access`) | id, role_code, role_name, role_class, default_scope | Read; the role rows a file is checked against and the scope the matrix answer shows |
| **Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2263; ASM-3727)** | `permission` | the version status, the valid-from and valid-to dates, the approver reference | Written by the load and read by all four operations; the status uses the standard `state` column |
| DF-ACE-301 to DF-ACE-304 | `v_ace_iam_group` (ACE, read-only view) | entra_group, role_code, source_system, data_as_of | Read through the P1 ACE-view contract (DP-05) for the group reference of the loader; never written |
| DF-REF-027 to DF-REF-033 | `lov_value` of `rwb_case` | lov_code, value_code, label_en, sort_order, valid_from | **Never read by SQL**: LOV-CAPABILITY arrives through the reference-data contract (DP-07) |
| DF-WRK-009 to DF-WRK-016 | `assignment` of `rwb_case` | id, case_id, task_id, assignee_user_id, assigned_at, ended_at | Not read and not written; the legacy Data table names it and the ownership map gives it to P3 |
| DF-DOC-001 to DF-DOC-011 | `document` of `rwb_document` | id, case_id, person_key, document_type, source, storage_ref | Not read and not written; the legacy Data table names it and the ownership map gives it to P5 |
| the DP-03 library's table | local decision record | the `AC-VERS` and `AC-DENY` entries of a load and of a refusal | Written through the library; no field invented here |

Two values the sources do not fix are carried as placeholders. The version status, the dates and the approver reference have no column on `permission` in TSD P4 v3 T3.1 while legacy AC3 needs an approved version with a valid-from — **Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2263; ASM-3727)**. The rights of the four operations have no ownership-map row and no T-A row and the legacy rows name other areas — **Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2263; ASM-1454)**. Field IDs are those of the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8; the legacy physical names `role` and `permission` are kept.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner `rwb-access` (P4); base `/api/recovery/access/v1`. The four paths are fixed by RWB-P4-AD002-CON and have no ownership-map row and no T-A row — **Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2263; ASM-1453)**.

| Method | Path | Purpose | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/recovery/access/v1/admin/permission-matrix` | The matrix rows in force on the date asked: role code and name, class, default scope, area, letters, version label. Query `roleCode`, `capabilityArea`, `matrixVersion`, `validOn`, `page`, `size` | Platform administration `R` | Read only |
| POST | `/api/recovery/access/v1/admin/permission-matrix-loads` | Load a matrix file with its label and valid-from; check it whole and store the version VALIDATED | Platform administration `C` | `Idempotency-Key`; the same key returns the first answer |
| GET | `/api/recovery/access/v1/admin/permission-matrix-versions/{matrixVersion}` | One version by label: status, dates, counts, author and approver references, decision-record reference and rows | Platform administration `R` | Read only |
| GET | `/api/recovery/access/v1/admin/permission-matrix-versions` | The versions with status, dates and row counts. Query `status`, `page`, `size` | Platform administration `R` | Read only |

`GET /admin/roles` (API-P4-007) and `GET /me/session` (API-P4-012) are the service's own and are not restated here; the role rows, their scope, their conflicts and the masking policy are RWB-P4-E1019-APP's, RWB-P4-E1037-APP's and RWB-P4-E1037-CON's.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

One hop per call, 2 s timeout and a breaker per downstream (DP-11).

| Method | Path | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/admin/parameters` | P3 `rwb-case`, RWB-P3-E1042-CON (DP-06) | The approver role `rwb.refload.approver.permission`, so the role a version waits for is data (ASM-3728) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/admin/lists/{listCode}` | P3 `rwb-case`, RWB-P3-E1043-CON (DP-07) | LOV-CAPABILITY and its 14 values in force, which a complete matrix must cover |
| POST | `/api/recovery/access/v1/authorise` | P4 `rwb-access` (own), RWB-P4-E1037-CON (DP-08) | The Platform administration `R` or `C` of the caller, with the MSG-P4-002 shape |

`recovery.v_ace_iam_group` (SELECT) is a read-only SQL read and not a call: it is granted and contracted by RWB-P1-E1069-APP (DP-05) and answers the group of the caller, its source system and its `data_as_of`; it is never `public.iam_group`. No other list is resolved, because role class, scope and letters travel as codes in `role` and `permission`.

###### 12.3 Events published

| Event | Topic | Owner | Contract element |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.access.AccessPolicyChanged.v1` | `rwb.access.events.v1` | P4 `rwb-access` | Change kind `MATRIX`, the version label, the status VALIDATED, the effective date, the row count and the time; no letters, no user reference, no personal data |
| `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` | `rwb.decision-record.v1` | PLT library, consumed by P7 | Entry id, decision code (`AC-VERS`, `AC-DENY`), the version label, the row count and the time |

Both use the CloudEvents 1.0 envelope with id, source, type, specversion, time, subject and datacontenttype. `rwb.access.DoaLimitChanged.v1` is not published here and no second access event name exists for a matrix load (ASM-3730). Consumers refresh their cached permission data on `AccessPolicyChanged` and then resolve the version in force on the date asked, so an unapproved version changes no answer.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. rwb-access is a reference-data owner in Architecture v5 slide 14 (events: none), the version in force is read from `rwb_access` on each call, and this story writes no inbox row.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None. The load, the three reads and the publish are synchronous work in the caller's thread. The six-monthly access review (JOB-18, Architecture v5 slide 44) is RWB-P4-AD008-APP's; this story registers no activity on the `rwb-access` queue.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. No Temporal Schedule and no quartz job sits here: the valid-from date is a row value the read resolves.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Schema | Owner | This story |
|---|---|---|---|
| `permission` | `rwb_access` | P4 | Writes the rows of each loaded version and reads them; adds the version dates and approver reference (ASM-3727) |
| `role` | `rwb_access` | P4 | Reads the active role codes a file must cover, the name, the class and the default scope; never writes |
| `outbox_event`, `processed_event`, `idempotency_key` | `rwb_access` | PLT library | Created by the service baseline; the library writes the outbox row and the stored answer |
| `masking_rule`, `role_conflict`, `delegation_limit` | `rwb_access` | P4 | Not read and not written: RWB-P4-AD004-APP's, RWB-P4-E1019-APP's and RWB-P4-E1038-APP's |
| `v_ace_iam_group` | ACE, read-only view | ACE / P1 `rwb-source-data` | Read through the P1 ACE-view contract (DP-05) |
| `lov_value`, `reference_row`, `reference_version` | `rwb_case` | P3 | **Never read by SQL**; LOV-CAPABILITY arrives through the contract (DP-07) |
| `parameter_catalog`, `parameter_value` | `rwb_case` | P3 | **Never read by SQL**; the approver role arrives through the contract (DP-06) |
| `decision_log_entry`, `approval` | `rwb_decision` | P7 | Not read and not written; the local entry is the library's |

No foreign key crosses a schema and no statement names a table outside `rwb_access` except the read-only ACE view of the P1 contract.

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.access.permissionmatrix`, in the service root `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.access`; base `/api/recovery/access/v1`, schema `rwb_access`, topic `rwb.access.events.v1`, queue `rwb-access` (unused here).

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-08 | RecoveryAccessGuard | Authorise contract of rwb-access and the guard library | H RWB-PLT-E1037-CON; C RWB-P4-E1037-CON |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-03 is the entry of every load and refusal with its outbox row. DP-05 is the read-only view that answers the group of the loader; the view and its grant come from RWB-P1-E1069-APP and add no dependency here. DP-06 is the approver role as data. DP-07 is the 14 areas as data. DP-08 is the guard that resolves the letters and checks every endpoint against the version in force. DP-13 is the base of the four operations. DP-19 is the composite route of SCR-43. The outbox relay and the inbox are the service template's objects and add no dependency.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| `V4001_2__permission_matrix_version.sql` | Migration | Adds the valid-from, valid-to and approver-reference columns of a version to `permission`, a unique key on (matrix_version, role_id, capability_area) and an index for the version-in-force read |
| `PermissionMatrixChecks` | Service | The whole-file checks of BR2 and BR3: one row per active role per area, letters, duplicates, unknown role codes, label, valid-from, required fields |
| `PermissionMatrixRepository` | Repository | Reads the rows in force on a date, one version by label and the versions; writes the rows of a new version in one transaction |
| `PermissionMatrixService` | Service | Assembles the three answers, resolves the version in force, computes the expected row count from `role` and LOV-CAPABILITY and writes the version VALIDATED |
| `CapabilityAreaReader` | Client | LOV-CAPABILITY through DP-07 with the 2 s budget and the 503 with MSG-GEN-006 |
| `ApproverParameterClient` | Client | `rwb.refload.approver.permission` through DP-06; no approver role in code |
| `MatrixVersionRecorder` | Service | Writes the `AC-VERS` and `AC-DENY` entries through DP-03 and the outbox row of the event |
| `AceGroupReader` | Client | Reads `v_ace_iam_group` read-only through the P1 contract with `data_as_of` |

**Database and migrations**

- Writes `permission` in `rwb_access` only: the rows of a version and its dates and approver reference; it changes no column of `role`.
- `V4001_2__permission_matrix_version.sql` sits on the per-service Flyway sequence after the V0001 baseline (DP-15); it drops nothing and copies no ACE value.
- The read predicate is the version whose valid-from is the latest not after the day asked and whose state is APPROVED or IN_FORCE; the version is a value, never a date in code.
- A new version is written by insert only; no update rewrites the rows of a stored version. The approval and the rollback are RWB-P4-AD010-APP's writes.
- DB access uses the per-service login (DP-02); no grant on `rwb_case`, on `recovery` or on `public` is added beyond the SELECT on the ACE view that RWB-P1-E1069-APP grants.

**Configuration and reference data**

- Labels, dates, letters and role codes are rows of the file and of `permission`; none is a constant (BR1).
- The approver role arrives as `rwb.refload.approver.permission` (DP-06) and the 14 areas as LOV-CAPABILITY (DP-07).
- `PM-2026.11`, `PM-2026.12` with 756 rows and the refused `PM-2026.13` are the values of the criteria and the tests (ASM-3729).
- No feature switch: a matrix changes by rows and dates, not by a flag.

**Build steps**

1. The migration with the date and approver columns, the unique key and the index, plus a fixture that applies it twice; test AC1.
2. `CapabilityAreaReader` and `ApproverParameterClient` over their fakes; test AC1.
3. `PermissionMatrixChecks` with one failing fixture per rule — a missing role, a duplicated pair, an invalid letter string, an unknown role code, an empty label, a label over 20 characters, a valid-from in the past; test AC2.
4. `PermissionMatrixRepository` and `PermissionMatrixService` with the version written VALIDATED, the version-in-force resolution on a fixed clock and the computed row count; tests AC1 and AC3.
5. `MatrixVersionRecorder` with the `AC-VERS` entry, the outbox row and the forced failure answering 503 with MSG-P7-003; tests AC1 and the NFR case.
6. The four operations with the `R` and `C` letters through the guard, and the `AC-DENY` entry of a refusal; test AC1.
7. The publication with change kind `MATRIX` after commit, and the assertion that nothing is published when the transaction fails; test AC1.
8. `AceGroupReader` over the ACE-view fake with `data_as_of`, and the 503 when the view cannot be read.
9. The boundary check: no statement names a `public` table, a `v_ace_*` view other than `v_ace_iam_group` or a table of another service; BND-6 of RWB-P4-E1069-APP stays green.

**Done when.** The tests of section 16 pass; `permission` holds `PM-2026.11` in force and `PM-2026.12` VALIDATED with its valid-from; a file with a role missing is refused in full with the role named; a caller without the letter is refused with MSG-P4-002 and one `AC-DENY` entry is written; a forced record failure leaves nothing stored and answers 503 with MSG-P7-003; the load publishes `rwb.access.AccessPolicyChanged.v1` with change kind `MATRIX`; on its valid-from date the approved version is the one the matrix read and the guard answer; and no statement names a table outside `rwb_access` or a `public` table.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message | Where it is produced |
|---|---|---|---|
| MSG-P4-001 | The caller holds no Recovery Workbench role | You have no Recovery Workbench role. Ask your team manager to request one. | The guard, on all four operations |
| MSG-P4-002 | No Platform administration `R` for a read, or no `C` for the load | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. | The guard, on all four operations |
| MSG-GEN-001 | A required field is empty, the label is too long or the valid-from is in the past | Enter {field}. | The checks, as a 422 with the field |
| MSG-P1-002 | A role is missing, a pair is repeated, a letter is outside the vocabulary or a role code is unknown | The {source} load for {date} was refused: {check}. The previous load is still in use. | The checks, as a 422 naming the gap |
| MSG-GEN-004 | The label already exists, or the version asked for does not exist | Someone else changed this record. Reload it to see their change. | The load and the reads |
| MSG-GEN-006 | LOV-CAPABILITY cannot be read through DP-07 | The reference data is not available. Try again later. | The load, on the reference read |
| MSG-P7-003 | The decision-record entry cannot be written | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. | The load and the refusals, through DP-03 |

Every error is an RFC 9457 problem response with `messageId` set and `detail` carrying the filled text. For MSG-P4-002 the {action} value names the action tried — "load the permission matrix", "read the permission matrix", "read a matrix version", "list the matrix versions" — never a case fact or another person's entitlement. For MSG-P1-002 the {check} value names the failed check, the missing role or the duplicate pair, and {source} and {date} are the label and its valid-from date.

**Note on the legacy message table, carried once.** Legacy RWB-AD-002 lists MSG-P4-004, the break-glass warning "Emergency access is on until {time}. Every action is recorded." No operation of this story produces it: the break-glass grant and its warning are RWB-P4-AD006-APP's and RWB-P4-E1039-APP's. MSG-P4-001, MSG-P4-002, MSG-GEN-001 and MSG-P7-003 are kept as the legacy story has them, MSG-P1-002 keeps its text, and MSG-GEN-004 and MSG-GEN-006 are the service's existing messages for an existing label and an unavailable reference answer.

##### 15. Screens and states

No screen is built by this story. SCR-43 Roles and access shows the roles, their permissions, the scope and the group mapping with the access log, and the security administrator, the platform administrator and internal audit read it there; it is served by the gateway-bff composite route of DP-19, which calls the matrix read (or the versions list) and the access-log read in parallel, one hop each. The screen field list, the column order and the merge are the screen owner's, and this story returns the rows and the versions only. Where the load form sits is **Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2263; ASM-3731)**.

| Screen | State | What the operator sees |
|---|---|---|
| SCR-43 Roles and access | List | The matrix rows in force: role code and name, area, letters and the version label |
| SCR-43 Roles and access | Versions | The labels with their status (VALIDATED, APPROVED, IN_FORCE, SUPERSEDED), their dates and row counts |
| SCR-43 Roles and access | Load | The load form: file, version label and valid-from, with the checks answered field by field |
| SCR-43 Roles and access | Loaded | The new version with status VALIDATED, its row count, commit time, decision-record reference and the role it waits for |
| SCR-43 Roles and access | Refused | MSG-P1-002 with the missing role or duplicate pair, or MSG-GEN-001 with the field |
| SCR-43 Roles and access | Refused, no right | MSG-P4-002 or MSG-P4-001, with no row and no version |
| SCR-43 Roles and access | Not available | MSG-GEN-006 for the reference list and MSG-P7-003 for the record, each with its retry advice |

The legacy pair SCR-39 Rules and parameters ("versions; load; approval") and SCR-40 Reference data ("versions; load") is not served by this story: the rule versions are RWB-P4-AD011-APP's and the reference lists are RWB-P4-AD009-APP's and RWB-P4-AD010-APP's.
