##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: labels, dates, letters, role codes, the 14 areas and the approver role are rows and contract answers, and a test proves that a new version and a new area list need no build (BR1, BR10).
- No personal data anywhere: a matrix row is a role code, an area and letters, an entry carries a user reference and no name, and no test row, log, event or prompt holds a name or an e-mail address.
- No read of another schema (DP-01): the reference, parameter and ledger tables, `assignment` and `document` are never read by SQL; the only external read is the read-only ACE view `v_ace_iam_group`.
- ACE data only through the owner's contract or the service's own `v_ace_*` view (DP-05): no statement names `public.iam_group`, a `public` table or a table of another service, and BND-6 of RWB-P4-E1069-APP stays green.
- One writer for the matrix: only this story's load writes the rows of a new version, a stored version is never edited, and the state changes after VALIDATED are the approval stories' (BR4, BR5).
- Default deny on every call: a missing role is 401 and a missing letter is 403 with MSG-P4-002, never an allow (BR7).
- A complete file or nothing: a refused load leaves the version in force untouched, so a partial load can never remove a right quietly (BR2).
- A version answers whole or not at all, and an unapproved version is never answered as the matrix in force (BR6).
- One migration per story on the service's own Flyway sequence (DP-15); one event name with change kind `MATRIX` (BR9).

##### 1. Story

As a **tech lead**, I want **the published contract baseline of the role scope: an OpenAPI 3.1 document for the scope read and the scope change, the `RoleScope`, `RoleScopeChange` and `RoleScopePage` schemas with the `LOV-SCOPE` values, the scope predicate shape that every service applies with `scope`, `teamCode`, `regionCode` and `caseOwnerRef`, the statement that a scope change is a data change and never a code change, the refusal with MSG-P4-003 and its decision-record entry, the `rwb.access.AccessPolicyChanged.v1` declaration with change kind `SCOPE`, one RFC 9457 error envelope with its message IDs, the contract tables of section 12 and the contract fakes**, so that **the app story builds on Day 1 against a fixed, testable contract, and every service that authorises a record learns exactly which bound it applies, which answer a record outside it receives and what is recorded when one is refused**.

The deliverable is the scope **as data and as predicate**: the read and the change of a role's scope, the shape of the bound every query applies, and the refusal that bound produces. What a role may do is not contracted here — the permission matrix and the masking are RWB-P4-E1037-CON's — the role catalogue is RWB-P4-E1019-APP's, the sign-in is RWB-P4-E1022-CON's, and the guard, the scope descriptor type and their fakes are RWB-PLT-E1037-CON's. This document declares the data side of the bound and the rule of the answer, and refers to those three contracts without restating them.

##### 2. Business rationale

Contract-first REST and one hop with a 2 s timeout is the decoupling decision (DP-11, ADR-020), and one guard library every service binds is the second (DP-08). The legacy story held the scope rule inside one package over one database: the same connection that read `role` and `permission` also filtered the case query and answered the refusal, so there was one shape because there was one process. In the target the scope stays with one owner (DP-01) and the enforcement moves into a platform library that every service binds, so a consumer now depends on two published artefacts and must find in each exactly what it needs: the library gives it the guard, the descriptor type and the annotation; the access owner gives it the scope value, the three codes of the record and the rule of the refusal.

That is the gap this document closes. Without a published data-side contract a consumer guesses what a scope value is called, whether the bound carries a team code, a region code or a queue, what an out-of-scope record receives — a 403, an empty page or a 404 — and whether the refusal is counted, recorded and shown. Those guesses drift at the first scope change, and a wrong guess is a data leak or a hidden case. With it, a consumer compiles and tests from Day 1 against fakes, and cannot quietly read a P4 table because the contract gives it no connection to do so.

Three consequences shape the document. The first is that the bound is four values and no fifth: `LOV-SCOPE` is `OWN`, `TEAM`, `REGION`, `ALL` (TSD P4 v3 T3.2), and the predicate that carries them is the same shape for all four, so a service writes one comparison and not four. The second is that the refusal is indistinguishable from an absence: a record outside the scope is answered 404 with MSG-P4-003, never 403 and never a count, because a 403 confirms that the record exists and a count tells the caller how much was hidden (FSD P4 v3 VR-P4-014-1 and AC-EXC-P4-014-01; REQ-ACA-009). The third is that a scope change is a data change with one event: `rwb.access.AccessPolicyChanged.v1` on `rwb.access.events.v1`, the one access-policy name the architecture gives this service (Architecture v5 slides 14, 20 and 43), with change kind `SCOPE`; a second name would add a contract without a consumer, because every service that caches permission data already refreshes on that one.

##### 3. Preconditions

- The service template and the naming library are available (RWB-PLT-TPL), so the base path, the topic and the event names follow the platform rule rather than a local choice.
- Architecture v5 slide 14 gives `rwb-access` the operations `POST /authorise` (role, scope, DoA), `GET /me/permissions`, `GET /doa-limits` and `/masking-policies`, and the two events `AccessPolicyChanged` and `DoaLimitChanged` on `rwb.access.events.v1`; slide 41 keeps Recovery roles as data, scope, masking policy, the DoA table and the access log in `rwb_access`; slide 10 fixes that each service authorises the object itself with cached permission data from `rwb-access`.
- TSD P4 v3 T3.1 fixes the column this document contracts: `role.default_scope` (DF-REF-038, `LOV`, varchar(8), required), and T3.2 fixes its list `LOV-SCOPE` = `OWN`, `TEAM`, `REGION`, `ALL`.
- TSD P4 v3 T6.2 fixes the rule behind the predicate: "scope filters every query". T6.1 fixes the rights matrix the two operations read: RW-SECADM CRUDA, RW-PLATADM CRUD, RW-AUDIT R, RW-COE R, RW-DATASTEW R and RW-COMPLY R in Platform administration.
- RWB-P4-E1037-CON is the access contract that publishes the authorise answer of which the scope predicate is an element; this document declares the shape of that element and does not restate the operation (ASM-1462).
- RWB-PLT-E1037-CON is the guard library: the `AccessGuard`, `ScopeGuard` and `MaskApplier` interfaces, the `@PersonalData` annotation, the scope descriptor type and the fakes every service binds. This document names the descriptor as the library's and fixes only the data that fills it.
- The two scope operations have no row in the ownership map and none in TSD P4 v3 appendix T-A, where the only role read is API-P4-007 `GET /admin/roles` — **Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0792; ASM-1461)**.
- The scope predicate has no operation of its own in any source: slide 14 names the inputs of the authorise operation as "role, scope, DoA" and TSD P4 v3 T-A gives no path for a scope answer — **Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0792; ASM-1462)**.
- The case owner, team and region columns the predicate is compared with are P3's: DF-CAS-009 `owner_user_id`, DF-CAS-011 `team_code` (`LOV-TEAM`) and DF-CAS-012 `region_code` (`LOV-REGION`) of `rwb_case` (TSD P3 v3 T3.1). This document names them and owns none of them.
- The failure-message convention is the platform one: RFC 9457 problem details (Architecture v5 slide 11, "RFC 9457 problem details"), and the legacy texts are copied unchanged where the message already exists.
- No build dependency: this story is Day 1 by rule (Template and Rules §R5.7), and it holds in Contract group CG-W4 because the business epic EP08 is wave 4 in the W-MAP (§R5.6).

##### 4. Flow

1. Draft the OpenAPI 3.1 document for the two scope operations under the base `/api/recovery/access/v1`, with the shared components the `rwb-access` operations use.
2. Draft the three schemas: `RoleScope` for one role and its scope value, `RoleScopeChange` for the posted value, and `RoleScopePage` for the paged read, with the `LOV-SCOPE` values declared once as an enumeration and used by both the schema and the validation.
3. State the invariant: one scope value per role, required, drawn from `LOV-SCOPE`; a role with no scope cannot exist because the column is required (DF-REF-038).
4. State the change rule: the change writes `default_scope` of one role row under `If-Match` and an `Idempotency-Key`; there is no version row and no effective date, so the history of a scope is the decision record and not a table (ASM-1460).
5. Declare the scope predicate: `scope`, `teamCode`, `regionCode` and `caseOwnerRef`, its meaning for each of the four values, and the statement that the guard of RWB-PLT-E1037-CON applies it in the owning service's own query and that the library returns no record.
6. State the refusal: a record outside the predicate is 404 with MSG-P4-003, with no field of the record and no count of the excluded records, and one decision-record entry with decision code `AC-DENY` and reason code `OUT_OF_SCOPE`; where the entry cannot be written the answer is 503 with MSG-P7-003 and no record.
7. State the rights: Platform administration R for the read and C for the change, with an active role required on every call, and the 401 and 403 of the default deny rule.
8. Agree the error envelope and the message mapping for 401, 403, 404, 409, 422 and 503, with the business texts copied unchanged from the legacy story where the message already exists.
9. Declare the event `rwb.access.AccessPolicyChanged.v1` on `rwb.access.events.v1` with change kind `SCOPE` and its payload, and the decision-record type on the shared topic `rwb.decision-record.v1`; declare no third event name and leave `rwb.access.DoaLimitChanged.v1` to the delegation contract.
10. Publish the contract tables of section 12 (nine sub-tables) and the contract fakes, then add the contract tests: schema validation, the four values, the predicate shape, the refusal, the rights, the envelope, the owner declarations and the drift between a fake and the document.
11. Tag the baseline and hand it to RWB-P4-AD003-APP, to RWB-PLT-E1037-CON and to every service that applies the predicate.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The document fails OpenAPI 3.1 validation | The pipeline fails and no baseline is tagged | None | AC1 |
| X2 | A schema declares a scope value outside `LOV-SCOPE`, or declares the four values twice with two spellings | The review fails and the enumeration is corrected | None | AC2 |
| X3 | A schema declares a person's name, an e-mail address or a case number | The review fails and the property is removed; the rule is a lint item of the document | None | AC2 |
| X4 | The predicate declares a field the sources do not support, or a field of another service's table | The review fails: the four names of the predicate are the contract and no fifth is added | None | AC3 |
| X5 | The document declares the refusal as 403, as an empty page, or with a count of the excluded records | The review fails: the refusal is 404 with MSG-P4-003 and no count | None | AC4 |
| X6 | The document declares an event name other than the two of the service, or a second access event name for a scope change | The review fails and the event is declared under `rwb.access.AccessPolicyChanged.v1` with change kind `SCOPE` | None | AC5 |
| X7 | The document declares an operation or a table of another service as provided | The review fails; the role catalogue, the authorise answer, the case columns and the library descriptor are documented as referred to and not as provided | None | AC1, AC6 |
| X8 | An error response carries no `messageId`, or a `messageId` not in the agreed set | The contract test fails and the merge is blocked | None | AC6 |
| X9 | A contract fake drifts from the document | The contract test fails and the merge is blocked | None | AC7 |
| X10 | A consumer applies the predicate and the access owner does not answer inside the 2 s budget | The consumer answers 503 with MSG-GEN-006 for that read and never answers a record it could not bound; the document declares the 503 | MSG-GEN-006 | AC6 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | No build dependency; it reads the ownership map, the platform envelopes, the TSD P4 v3 columns and lists, and refers to RWB-P4-E1037-CON and RWB-PLT-E1037-CON without restating them |
| Negotiable | The field-level detail of the three schemas and the payload of the event are settled with the app story and with the guard library; the four values, the predicate names, the refusal and the envelope are fixed by the target architecture and the Workbench |
| Valuable | Unblocks the app story and every service that authorises a record on Day 1 with a written answer to "which bound applies, and what does a record outside it receive", and keeps the catalogue, the matrix, the masking and the session out of the scope contract |
| Estimable | One document, three schemas, one error envelope with six message ids, one event declaration, nine contract tables, four fakes and seven contract tests |
| Small | Fits one sprint with the contract tests |
| Testable | Every criterion is tested against the artefact, not against a business outcome |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: The role scope contract baseline for rwb-access

  Background:
    Given the service naming rule of the platform library is in force
    Given a scope is the "default_scope" of a role row of "rwb_access" and its values are "OWN", "TEAM", "REGION" and "ALL"
    Given the guard of RWB-PLT-E1037-CON applies the scope predicate in the owning service and returns no record

  Scenario: AC1 The OpenAPI 3.1 document describes the two scope operations (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the OpenAPI 3.1 document of rwb-access is published
    When it is validated against the OpenAPI 3.1 schema
    Then it validates with no error
    Then it declares the base /api/recovery/access/v1
    Then it declares GET /admin/role-scopes and PATCH /admin/role-scopes/{roleCode} with the owner rwb-access
    Then the read declares Platform administration with the right R, and the change declares Platform administration with the right C
    Then every operation declares 401, 403, 404, 409, 422 and 503
    Then the change declares the Idempotency-Key header and the If-Match header, and the read declares neither
    Then the role catalogue GET /admin/roles, the session GET /me/session and the authorise operation POST /authorise are documented as referred to and not as provided, with their owners

  Scenario: AC2 The three schemas carry the role, the scope value and its list (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the schemas RoleScope, RoleScopeChange and RoleScopePage of the document
    Then RoleScope carries roleCode, roleName, roleClass, scope, scopeValues, rowVersion and updatedAt
    Then RoleScopeChange carries scope and the If-Match version
    Then RoleScopePage carries items, page, size and total with a default of 50 and a maximum of 200
    Then scope is declared as an enumeration of OWN, TEAM, REGION and ALL, and no fifth value appears anywhere in the document
    Then the document states that a scope is the "default_scope" of a role row in "rwb_access" (DF-REF-038) and that it is required
    Then no schema, no parameter and no example declares a person's name, an e-mail address, an identity number or a case number

  Scenario: AC3 The scope predicate is declared once and applied by the guard (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the scope predicate described in the document
    Then it carries scope, teamCode, regionCode and caseOwnerRef and no fifth field
    Then scope is the value of "LOV-SCOPE" of the role, teamCode and regionCode are the case team and region codes DF-CAS-011 and DF-CAS-012 of rwb-case, and caseOwnerRef is compared with the case owner DF-CAS-009
    Then the document states that OWN matches the case owner, TEAM the case team, REGION the case region and ALL every case, and that a scope with no team or region code matches no record of that dimension and never widens to ALL
    Then the document states that the guard of RWB-PLT-E1037-CON applies the predicate in the owning service's own query and that the library runs no query and returns no record
    Then the descriptor type of the predicate is declared as RWB-PLT-E1037-CON's and is not redefined here

  Scenario: AC4 The refusal is one message, one status and one entry (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the refusal section of the document
    Then a record outside the predicate is declared as 404 with MSG-P4-003 "This case is not in your scope."
    Then the document states that no field of the record and no count of the excluded records is returned in the status, the body, a header or a metric
    Then the document states that one decision-record entry with decision code AC-DENY and reason code OUT_OF_SCOPE is written through the library of DP-03 and published on rwb.decision-record.v1
    Then the document states that where the entry cannot be written the answer is 503 with MSG-P7-003 and the record is not returned
    Then the two legacy criteria are named as RWB-P4-AD003-APP's and no legacy value of them is restated as a criterion of this document

  Scenario: AC5 A scope change is a data change published as the access-policy event (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the change operation and the events section of the document
    Then the change updates default_scope of one role row and answers the role with its new scope and the decision-record entry reference
    Then the document states that a scope change needs no deployment, no restart and no code change, and that the history of a scope is the decision record and not a table
    Then rwb.access.AccessPolicyChanged.v1 is declared on the topic rwb.access.events.v1 with change kind SCOPE, the role code, the new scope value and the time
    Then rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1 is declared on the shared topic rwb.decision-record.v1 for the entry of the change and of the refusal
    Then no other event name is declared for this capability, and rwb.access.DoaLimitChanged.v1 is declared as the delegation contract's and not as this one's
    Then no payload carries a person, a case, a case count or a personal field

  Scenario: AC6 Every failure is one envelope with one message (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the error envelope component of the document
    When a 401, 403, 404, 409, 422 or 503 response is produced by either of the two operations
    Then the body carries the code, the message, the messageId, the traceId and the field list, with the problem media type
    Then 401 carries MSG-P4-001, 403 carries MSG-P4-002, 404 and 409 carry MSG-GEN-004, 422 carries MSG-GEN-001 other than the out-of-scope refusal, and 503 carries MSG-P7-003
    Then the out-of-scope refusal is 404 with MSG-P4-003 and is declared once, with the reason code OUT_OF_SCOPE
    Then the message texts are the legacy texts where the message already exists and the legacy criterion AC2 of RWB-AD-003 is not reworded by this document

  Scenario: AC7 The fakes match the document and carry no personal data (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the four contract fakes of section 12.8
    When a fake is compared with the document
    Then the role-scope fake answers the two paths of 12.1 with four roles of the four LOV-SCOPE values, one change of OWN to TEAM, 409 on a stale If-Match, 422 on a value outside the list and 403 with MSG-P4-002
    Then the scope predicate fake answers a predicate of each of the four values and no record
    Then the rwb-case case-list mock answers the 12 cases owned by the caller and the case RW-2026-000456 in team MTG-NE under another owner, with 404 and MSG-P4-003 for the out-of-scope case
    Then the decision-record fake answers the AC-CHG and AC-DENY appends and the 503 with MSG-P7-003
    Then a contract test fails on any drift between a fake and the document, and no fake carries a name, an e-mail address or a case number
```

These seven criteria test the artefact only. No criterion restates a legacy acceptance criterion: the two legacy criteria of RWB-AD-003 are owned by RWB-P4-AD003-APP and are listed with their tests in section 16 as the cases this contract is the ground of, exactly as the brief of this key fixes.

| BR5 | A record outside the predicate is 404 with MSG-P4-003, with no field of the record and no count of the excluded records in any status, body, header or metric | FSD P4 v3 VR-P4-014-1 and AC-EXC-P4-014-01; legacy RWB-AD-003 AC2; REQ-ACA-009 |

##### 11. Data

The contract baseline declares shapes, not business values.

| Item | Content |
|---|---|
| Scope of a role | `roleCode` (DF-REF-035), `roleName` (DF-REF-036), `roleClass` (DF-REF-037), `scope` (DF-REF-038, one of `OWN`, `TEAM`, `REGION`, `ALL`), `scopeValues`, `rowVersion`, `updatedAt` |
| Scope change | `scope`, the `If-Match` version and the `Idempotency-Key` header; the answer is the role with its new scope and the decision-record entry reference |
| Scope page | `items[]` of the scope of a role, `page`, `size` (default 50, maximum 200), `total` |
| Scope predicate | `scope`, `teamCode`, `regionCode`, `caseOwnerRef`; no record, no query and no count |
| Case columns named behind the predicate | DF-CAS-009 `owner_user_id`, DF-CAS-011 `team_code` (`LOV-TEAM`), DF-CAS-012 `region_code` (`LOV-REGION`), of P3 `rwb_case` (TSD P3 v3 T3.1); named only |
| Lists | `LOV-SCOPE` = `OWN`, `TEAM`, `REGION`, `ALL` (TSD P4 v3 T3.2); `LOV-ROLE-CLASS` = `BANK_USER`, `PARTNER_USER`, `NON_HUMAN_ACTOR` for the class the read answers |
| Refusal | 404, MSG-P4-003 "This case is not in your scope.", the reason code `OUT_OF_SCOPE`, and no case number, owner or count |
| Event payloads | The role code, the scope value and the time; no person, no case and no personal field |
| Decision-record entry | The change entry and the refusal entry, written through the library of DP-03; their fields are the library's and are not redefined here |

Three values the sources do not fix are this baseline's decision and are carried as placeholders. The two operation paths and their rights have no row in the ownership map and none in TSD P4 v3 appendix T-A — **Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0792; ASM-1461)**. The predicate has no operation and no field list of its own in any source — **Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0792; ASM-1462)**. A scope change has no version and no effective date on `role` — **Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0792; ASM-1460)**.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner `rwb-access` (P4); base `/api/recovery/access/v1`.

| Method | Path | Documented shape | Access |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/admin/role-scopes` | `RoleScopePage`: query `scope`, `roleClass`, `page`, `size` (default 50, max 200); every role in force with its scope value and the four values of `LOV-SCOPE` | Platform administration R |
| PATCH | `/admin/role-scopes/{roleCode}` | `RoleScopeChange` in, with the `Idempotency-Key` and `If-Match` headers; the written role out with its new scope and the decision-record entry reference | Platform administration C |

Errors for both: 401 no session or no Workbench role (MSG-P4-001), 403 no right (MSG-P4-002), 404 an unknown role code (MSG-GEN-004), 409 a stale `If-Match` or a repeated key answered differently (MSG-GEN-004), 422 a value outside `LOV-SCOPE` or a missing field (MSG-GEN-001), 503 the record entry not written (MSG-P7-003). The change is idempotent by `Idempotency-Key`; the same key returns the first answer and writes no second change. Major version 1 sits in the path (BR12).

The role catalogue `GET /admin/roles` (API-P4-007), the session `GET /me/session` (API-P4-012) and the authorise answer `POST /authorise` are the service's own operations of RWB-P4-E1019-APP, RWB-P4-E1037-APP and RWB-P4-E1037-CON; this document refers to them, declares the scope element each of them carries, and neither restates nor changes them (ASM-1462).

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

None. This document declares no consumed operation and no consumed table, because the scope is answered from `rwb_access` and from the session, and the guard runs in the consumer's own process against its own tables.

| Called by | What it uses | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| Every service that authorises a record | The scope predicate in the access answer, and the guard of RWB-PLT-E1037-CON that applies it in its own query | P4 `rwb-access` for the data, RWB-PLT-E1037-CON for the library |
| P3 rwb-case | The case owner, team and region columns DF-CAS-009, DF-CAS-011 and DF-CAS-012 of its own `recovery_case`, compared with the predicate | P3, its own table and its own query (named only here) |

The case read of the app story's AC1 is P3's `GET /cases` (RWB-P3-E1018-CON) and is exercised through its contract mock at test level only; this document declares no dependency on it and the app story carries none (ASM-1466).

###### 12.3 Events published

| Event | Topic | Owner | Contract element |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.access.AccessPolicyChanged.v1` | `rwb.access.events.v1` | P4 `rwb-access` | Change kind `SCOPE`, the role code, the new scope value and the time |
| `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` | `rwb.decision-record.v1` | PLT library, consumed by P7 | Entry id, decision code (`AC-CHG` for a change, `AC-DENY` for a refusal with reason code `OUT_OF_SCOPE`), the role code, the scope value and the time |

Both messages use the CloudEvents 1.0 envelope with the attributes id, source, type, specversion, time, subject and datacontenttype. No message carries a person, a case, a case count, a name, an e-mail address or an identity number. `rwb.access.DoaLimitChanged.v1` is declared as the delegation contract's event and is not declared for a scope change, and no second name exists for one (BR9, ASM-1464).

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. `rwb-access` is a reference-data owner in Architecture v5 slide 14 (events: none), and this capability adds no subscription.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None. The two operations are synchronous REST answers in the caller's thread with no workflow, no activity and no signal. The six-monthly access review Schedule (JOB-18) is RWB-P4-AD008-CON's; the scope is applied inside a request and never by a workflow.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. Nothing about a scope runs on a clock: the scope is a value the read answers and the change writes.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Contracted use |
|---|---|---|
| `role` | P4 (`rwb_access`) | `default_scope` (DF-REF-038) is the scope; the role code, name and class travel with it; the optimistic-lock version is the `If-Match` of the change |
| `permission` | P4 (`rwb_access`) | The Platform administration letters R and C of the caller (DF-REF-040 to DF-REF-044); read only |
| `recovery_case` | P3 (`rwb_case`) | Appears nowhere as a table; DF-CAS-009, DF-CAS-011 and DF-CAS-012 are named as the columns the predicate is compared with, in P3's own query |
| `assignment`, `queue`, `queue_member` | P3 (`rwb_case`) | Appear nowhere; the predicate does not use the assignment window and this capability reads no queue row |
| `lov_value`, `reference_row`, `reference_version`, `parameter_catalog`, `parameter_value` | P3 (`rwb_case`) | Appear nowhere; `LOV-SCOPE` is the document's own enumeration (BR11, DP-01) |
| `decision_log_entry` | P7 (`rwb_decision`) | Appears nowhere; the local entry is the library's and the central ledger is P7's |
| `partner_user` | S9 (`rwb_partner`) | Appears nowhere; the ownership map gives partner users to S9 |

No foreign key crosses a schema, and the contract names no table outside `rwb_access`.

##### 13. Solution plan

**Deliverables.** `openapi/rwb-access-role-scope-v1.yaml` (OpenAPI 3.1) with the two operations and the shared components, the three schemas, the `contract/error-envelope.yaml` with the agreed message ids, the predicate declaration with its four fields and its four meanings, the event declaration for `rwb.access.AccessPolicyChanged.v1` with change kind `SCOPE`, the stub that names the P3 case columns and the library descriptor as referred to, and the four WireMock mapping sets.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-08 | RecoveryAccessGuard | Authorise contract of rwb-access and the guard library | H RWB-PLT-E1037-CON; C RWB-P4-E1037-CON |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

A contract story adds no build dependency of its own: each DP above is **referred to; the consuming story carries the dependency**, and that story is RWB-P4-AD003-APP, whose H row carries RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, RWB-PLT-E1037-CON, RWB-P4-E1037-CON and RWB-PLT-N001-CON. DP-03 is contracted as the entry the document declares on `rwb.decision-record.v1`. DP-05 is contracted as the boundary the document keeps and not as a read: `role` is the ACE RBAC extension in `rwb_access`, the caller's identity arrives in the ACE sign-in claim, the case owner, team and region are P3's columns named only, and the document declares no `v_ace_*` read. DP-08 is the predicate and the guard that applies it, with the descriptor type named as the library's. DP-13 is the base of the document. DP-19 is the composite route that serves SCR-43.

**Build steps**

1. OpenAPI 3.1 skeleton with the base path, the security scheme, the error responses and the shared components; schema lint in the pipeline (AC1).
2. The two operations and the three schemas of section 11, with the enumeration of `LOV-SCOPE` declared once (AC1, AC2).
3. The invariant and the change rule in the description of the two operations: one value per role, required, `If-Match`, `Idempotency-Key`, no version row and no effective date (AC2, AC5).
4. The predicate declaration with its four fields, its four meanings and the library boundary (AC3).
5. The refusal declaration: 404 with MSG-P4-003, no count, the `AC-DENY` entry with reason code `OUT_OF_SCOPE`, and the 503 with MSG-P7-003 (AC4).
6. The rights of the read and of the change, and the 401 and 403 of the default deny rule (AC6).
7. The error envelope and the message-id mapping, with the legacy texts copied unchanged (AC6).
8. The event declaration and the decision-record type, with the change kind and the payload, and the statement that no third name exists (AC5).
9. The four fakes and the stub fixtures of section 12.8 (AC7).
10. The seven contract tests; a drift between a fake and the document fails the build. Baseline tag and the consumer sign-off note of the app story and of the guard library (AC1 to AC7).

**Feature switch.** The contract carries no switch. The two operations are operations of the service and the change is a data change guarded by the C letter; nothing about a scope is behind a flag.

**Consumer sign-off**

| Consumer | What it accepts |
|---|---|
| RWB-P4-AD003-APP | The two provided operations, the three schemas, the predicate, the refusal, the event declaration and the four fakes |
| RWB-PLT-E1037-CON and RWB-PLT-E1037-APP, the guard library | The predicate's four fields, their meanings and the statement that the guard applies them and returns no record |
| RWB-P4-E1037-CON, the access contract that carries the predicate | The scope element of the authorise answer, and the refusal status and message it produces |
| RWB-P3-E1018-CON, the case read | The 404 with MSG-P4-003 a case outside the predicate receives, and the naming of DF-CAS-009, DF-CAS-011 and DF-CAS-012 |
| The wave 4 harness | The fakes of 12.8 and the case-list stub |

The deprecation window of a published field and the retention of the contract fakes are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0792; ASM-1461).

**Done when.** The OpenAPI document validates in the pipeline, the seven contract tests pass, the four fakes answer every provided path and every refusal, and the app story, the guard library, the access contract and the case read have accepted the baseline.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P4-003 | A record outside the predicate of the caller | This case is not in your scope. |
| MSG-P4-001 | No session, no Workbench role, or a sign-in that resolves no role | You have no Recovery Workbench role. Ask your team manager to request one. |
| MSG-P4-002 | A caller without Platform administration R for the read, or without C for the change | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-GEN-001 | A value outside `LOV-SCOPE`, a missing field or a role that is not active | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-GEN-004 | An unknown role code, a stale `If-Match`, or a repeated key answered differently | Someone else changed this record. Reload it to see their change. |
| MSG-P7-003 | The decision-record entry could not be written, on a change or on a refusal | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-GEN-006 | The access owner does not answer inside the 2 s budget of a consumer | The reference data is not available. Try again later. |

The message ids are contract elements; the text is the agreed text, taken from the legacy story where the message already existed. The one legacy criterion this document must not reword is AC2 of RWB-AD-003, "the system does not find the response and the refusal is logged", which RWB-P4-AD003-APP copies word for word; this document fixes only the status, the message id, the reason code and the entry it names. For MSG-P4-002 the {action} value names the action the caller tried and never a case fact or the scope of another person.

##### 15. Screens and states

| Screen | State | Contract element the screen consumes |
|---|---|---|
| SCR-43 Roles and access | List | The scope read with every role in force, its class and its scope value, and the four `LOV-SCOPE` values as a filter |
| SCR-43 Roles and access | Change | The change request, the `If-Match` version and the field-level 422 answers of the checks |
| SCR-43 Roles and access | Changed | The written role with its new scope, its version and the decision-record entry reference |
| SCR-43 Roles and access | Unchanged | The role unchanged, because the posted value equals the value in force, with no entry and no event |
| SCR-43 Roles and access | Refused | The 403 with MSG-P4-002 and no row, and the 401 with MSG-P4-001 |
| SCR-43 Roles and access | Conflict | The 409 with MSG-GEN-004 for a stale `If-Match`, with the reload advice |
| SCR-43 Roles and access | Not available | The 503 with MSG-P7-003 |
| The case list and the case record of P3, consumed through the composite route | Out of scope | The 404 with MSG-P4-003 and no count of the records excluded |

The screens are served by the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19), which calls the scope read and the access-log read in parallel, one hop each, and merges the answers. The composite route specification, the screen field list and the column order are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0792; ASM-1461); the document fixes the scope side of the merge only.

| TC-AD-003-02 | AC2 | Contract | Legacy test "Out of scope" on the contract side: the document declares the 404 with MSG-P4-003, the reason code `OUT_OF_SCOPE` and the entry, and the fake answers the out-of-scope case `RW-2026-000456` in team `MTG-NE` with that status and that message; no case number and no count appears in any answer |

The four legacy test cases are kept with their IDs and their legacy Covers values, and the legacy test name is written in the Data column. The Level column follows Template and Rules §R7.2: the two operations and the predicate are tested against the artefact at Contract, the legacy Access row stays Component, and the legacy Resilience row of Principle 5 stays NFR. The behaviour of each case in the running service is RWB-P4-AD003-APP's at End to end, and the full test with its Given, When and Then is in Recovery Workbench Test Cases v7.xlsx, tab Story test cases, under the same test case ID. The ITG copy of the set is RWB-ITG-AD003-ITG's and is not written here, so no `-ITG` id appears in this table.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in the contract: the role codes and the four scope values are source values and the document declares the list once; the parameter-level detail of a future fifth value is a major version and not a code constant (BR2, BR11).
- No personal data in a schema, an example or a fake: a scope is a role and one of four values, a predicate is a role's scope and three codes, and a name, an e-mail address or a case number in the document fails the review.
- The contract names only `rwb-access` tables and no operation of another service as provided (DP-01, BR10); the catalogue, the session, the authorise answer, the case columns and the library descriptor are declared as referred to.
- The predicate has four fields and no fifth, and the document states it once so that no consumer invents a fifth bound (BR3).
- The refusal is never a 403 and never a count: a record outside the predicate is indistinguishable from one that does not exist (BR5).
- One REST base, one topic and one event name for the capability, and the shared record type on `rwb.decision-record.v1`; a document that names another service's base, topic or event fails the review (DP-13, BR9).
- The guard and the descriptor are the library's: the document fixes the data and the rule and never a second implementation (BR4).
- Every example and every fake is synthetic; no production role, person, case or entitlement is copied into a schema or a fake.
- The error envelope and the CloudEvents envelope come from the platform library; this story narrows them but never redefines them.

##### 1. Story

As an **application owner**, I want **each role given a scope of own cases, team, region or all as data in `rwb_access`, and that scope applied as one predicate in every service that answers a case, so that a person sees only the cases their role allows and a record outside it is answered as not found and recorded**, so that **the legacy rule that lived inside one process over one schema becomes a published value and a published predicate that rwb-access owns and every consumer applies in its own query**.

The story builds the scope slice of P4 on the contract baseline of RWB-P4-AD003-CON: the two operations that read and change a role's scope, the four values of `LOV-SCOPE`, the predicate `scope` + `teamCode` + `regionCode` + `caseOwnerRef` returned to the guard of RWB-PLT-E1037-CON, the refusal of a record outside it with MSG-P4-003 and one local decision-record entry, and the publication of `rwb.access.AccessPolicyChanged.v1` with change kind `SCOPE`. What a role may do is not built here: the permission matrix is RWB-P4-E1037-APP's, masking is RWB-P4-AD004-APP's, separation of duty is RWB-P4-AD005-APP's and sign-in is RWB-P4-AD001-APP's. rwb-access holds no case row and runs no case query; the case owner, team and region columns are P3's, named only (ASM-3735).

##### 2. Business rationale

The design decision is one deployable service per module with one schema and one login (DP-01, DP-02), contract-first REST with one hop and a 2 s timeout (DP-11), and one authorise contract plus one guard library that every service binds (DP-08). In the monolith the scope was a column that the same connection read while it filtered the case query; there was one shape because there was one process. Once the case query belongs to rwb-case and the role row to rwb-access, the scope has to travel as a value and a predicate, and the refusal has to be a rule both sides agree, or every consumer invents its own.

That is the risk this story removes. Without a stated predicate a consumer compares the wrong column — a queue code for a team code, a branch for a region — and leaks cases, or refuses everything and hides work. Without a stated refusal a consumer answers 403, which confirms that a record exists, or returns an empty page with a total, which tells the caller how many records were hidden. Without a recorded refusal the PDPA and audit reading of who reached what stops at the screen. And without one access event every service that caches permission data refreshes on its own guess (REQ-ACA-009, REQ-ACA-007).

The microservice change is therefore narrow and precise: the value moves from a code constant to a `role` row (REQ-ACA-002), the enforcement moves from the monolith's interceptor to the guard library in the owner's query (DP-08, DP-19), the refusal moves from a local exception to a 404 with MSG-P4-003 and an `AC-DENY` entry on `rwb.decision-record.v1` (DP-03), and the change becomes one event on `rwb.access.events.v1` (DP-09 by reference). Business values stay out of code: the four scope values and the messages are data and catalogue rows (BR-P4-014).

##### 3. Preconditions

- `RWB-P4-AD003-CON` is the baseline this story builds against: the two operations, the three schemas, the predicate shape, the refusal and the event are fixed there and consumed here unchanged.
- `RWB-PLT-E1027-CON` gives the local decision-record library, its append and the shared topic `rwb.decision-record.v1`; `RWB-PLT-E1037-CON` gives the `AccessGuard`/`ScopeGuard` interfaces, the scope descriptor type and the fakes; `RWB-P4-E1037-CON` publishes the authorise answer of which the scope element is a part; `RWB-PLT-N001-CON` gives the gateway-bff composite route for SCR-43.
- Service baseline: schema `rwb_access`, one login per service (DP-02), base `/api/recovery/access/v1` (DP-13), topic `rwb.access.events.v1`, task queue `rwb-access`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.access`.
- TSD P4 v3 T3.1 fixes `role.default_scope` (DF-REF-038, `LOV-SCOPE`, varchar(8), required) and T3.2 fixes the list `OWN`, `TEAM`, `REGION`, `ALL`; T6.2 fixes the rule "scope filters every query".
- TSD P4 v3 T6.1 fixes the rights this story reads: Platform administration R for a read and C for a change — RW-SECADM CRUDA, RW-PLATADM CRUD, RW-AUDIT R, RW-COE R, RW-DATASTEW R, RW-COMPLY R, and "-" for every business role.
- The case columns the predicate is compared with are P3's: DF-CAS-009 `owner_user_id`, DF-CAS-011 `team_code` (`LOV-TEAM`), DF-CAS-012 `region_code` (`LOV-REGION`) of `rwb_case` (TSD P3 v3 T3.1).
- No source gives the scope read or the scope change a path or a right: the legacy key names only `GET monolith-base/admin/roles`, the Ownership Map has no scope row and TSD P4 v3 T-A has no scope path — **Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2265; ASM-3735)**.
- No source fixes the predicate payload, the refused-entry codes or the version rule of a scope — **Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2265; ASM-3735)**.
- The legacy master and the Epic 8 BRD carry no approved status in this run; stories proceed in Draft by the D-RCV-60 overlay (ASM-3734). Release 30 June 2027 is copied unchanged and marked tentative (U7).

##### 4. Flow

1. On start-up the service loads its own Flyway baseline, the `role` and `permission` rows in `rwb_access`, and binds the guard, the decision-record library and the outbox from the service template.
2. `GET /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/role-scopes` answers every role in force with its scope value and the four `LOV-SCOPE` values as the enumeration; the caller's Platform administration R letter is checked first and the view is filtered by the caller's own scope.
3. `PATCH /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/role-scopes/{roleCode}` takes the new value under `If-Match` and `Idempotency-Key`, validates the role (exists, active), the value (in `LOV-SCOPE`) and the required fields, and refuses 422 with MSG-GEN-001 before any write.
4. The change writes `default_scope` of the one role row, appends one local decision-record entry with decision code `AC-CHG` through the library of DP-03, and publishes `rwb.access.AccessPolicyChanged.v1` with change kind `SCOPE`, the role code and the new value through the outbox.
5. Where the entry cannot be written the change is not stored and the answer is 503 with MSG-P7-003; where the `If-Match` version is stale the answer is 409 with no write and no entry.
6. The scope element travels in the authorise answer of RWB-P4-E1037-CON as `scope`, `teamCode`, `regionCode` and `caseOwnerRef`; the caller's own team and region codes come from the session of RWB-P4-AD001-APP, and the descriptor type stays the library's.
7. A consumer's guard applies the predicate in its own query: `OWN` matches `caseOwnerRef` against the case owner, `TEAM` matches `teamCode` against the case team code, `REGION` matches `regionCode` against the case region code, `ALL` adds no field comparison. Scope is applied before the permission letter is checked.
8. A record outside the predicate is answered 404 with MSG-P4-003, with no field of the record and no count of the excluded records, and one entry with decision code `AC-DENY` and reason code `OUT_OF_SCOPE` is appended; where that entry cannot be written the answer is 503 with MSG-P7-003 and the record is not returned.
9. SCR-43 renders the role list, its scope and the access log through the gateway-bff composite route; no screen calls a service directly and no screen chains two calls.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The caller has no Workbench role in the session | The call is refused before any row is read; the refusal is one `AC-DENY` entry | MSG-P4-001 | AC2, TC-AD-003-03 |
| X2 | The caller holds a role whose Platform administration letter is "-" | The call is refused with no row and no count disclosed | MSG-P4-002 | AC2, TC-AD-003-03 |
| X3 | The posted value is outside `LOV-SCOPE`, or a required field is empty | 422 with the field named; no row is written, no entry, no event | MSG-GEN-001 | TC-AD-003-03 |
| X4 | The `If-Match` version is stale, or the role code does not exist or is inactive | 409 for the stale version, 404 for the unknown or inactive role; nothing is written | None specified for 409 | X4 |
| X5 | The decision-record library answers 503 while a change is being recorded | The change is not stored; the role keeps its value in force | MSG-P7-003 | TC-AD-003-04 |
| X6 | A caller reaches a record outside the predicate | 404 with no field, no header and no count; one `AC-DENY` entry with reason code `OUT_OF_SCOPE` | MSG-P4-003 | AC2, TC-AD-003-02 |
| X7 | The refusal entry cannot be written | 503; the record is not returned, so a refusal is never silent | MSG-P7-003 | TC-AD-003-04 |
| X8 | The access owner does not answer inside the 2 s budget while a consumer builds its predicate | The consumer answers 503 for that read and never answers a record it could not bound; the breaker opens per downstream | MSG-GEN-006 | X8 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Yes: one legacy key, one service, one lane. It builds on CON baselines only (all five H rows are CON stories) and changes no other service. |
| Negotiable | The scope values and the messages are business-owned data and catalogue rows; the paths, the predicate field names and the entry codes are the contract's and are negotiable only through RWB-P4-AD003-CON. |
| Valuable | Every screen that lists a case depends on it: without it the case list is either over-exposed or empty, and the refusal is unattributable (REQ-ACA-009, REQ-ACA-007). |
| Estimable | Yes: two operations, two tables, one library binding, one event and one screen state, all fixed by the contract baseline. |
| Small | Yes: one release at wave 4 with no workflow, no schedule and no migration beyond the two tables of the service baseline. |
| Testable | Yes: four legacy test cases with the four scope values, the 404 refusal and the forced record failure; every cross-service answer is a contract mock. |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Scope per role

  Background:
    Given the rwb-access base path is /api/recovery/access/v1 and the schema is rwb_access
    Given a role's scope is the "default_scope" of its "role" row and its values are "OWN", "TEAM", "REGION" and "ALL"

  Scenario: AC1 Own scope (legacy RWB-AD-003 AC1)
    Given the rwb-case contract mock returns only the cases the caller owns
    Given a case owner with scope Own
    When they list cases
    Then the system returns only cases they own

  Scenario: AC2 Out of scope (legacy RWB-AD-003 AC2)
    Given a case owned by another team
    When a case owner with scope Team opens it
    Then the system does not find the response and the refusal is logged
```

Both criteria are the legacy criteria of RWB-AD-003 copied word for word, with the origin tag, the value `Own` of AC1 and the value `Team` of AC2 unchanged. One line is added to AC1 and nothing else: the faked answer of the case read, whose owner is P3 rwb-case, so that "returns only cases they own" is observable without a case row in this service (DP-11, one hop, `rwb-case` contract mock). No value of either criterion is replaced.

AC1 is answered by the scope value of the role row and by the predicate this story publishes; it is observed through the case list, whose query the consumer's guard filters. AC2 is answered by the same predicate and by the refusal rule of BR8: the record is not found, the answer is 404 with MSG-P4-003 and one `AC-DENY` entry with reason code `OUT_OF_SCOPE` is written, which is what "the refusal is logged" means in the target. The 404 is rendered by the record's owner; the rule, the message, the reason code and the entry are this story's. Neither criterion restates a value of RWB-P4-E1019-APP, RWB-P4-E1037-APP or RWB-P4-AD001-APP.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | A role's scope is the `default_scope` of its `role` row in `rwb_access`, one value of `LOV-SCOPE`; no scope value and no role code is written in code | Legacy RWB-AD-003 story line; TSD P4 v3 T3.1 (DF-REF-038) and T3.2; BR-P4-014 |
| BR2 | `LOV-SCOPE` is `OWN`, `TEAM`, `REGION`, `ALL`; a value outside the list is refused 422 before any row is written | TSD P4 v3 T3.2; FSD P4 v3 A2.14.3.1; MSG-GEN-001 |
| BR3 | `OWN` compares `caseOwnerRef` with the case owner, `TEAM` compares `teamCode` with the case team code, `REGION` compares `regionCode` with the case region code, `ALL` adds no comparison; the predicate carries those four fields and no fifth | FSD P4 v3 A2.14; TSD P3 v3 T3.1 (DF-CAS-009, DF-CAS-011, DF-CAS-012); ASM-3735 |
| BR4 | Scope is applied before the permission letter is checked, so a record outside the scope is never named and the excluded count is never returned | FSD P4 v3 A2.14; FSD P4 v3 VR-P4-014-1; REQ-ACA-009 |
| BR5 | The scope read needs Platform administration R and the scope change needs C; no Workbench role is 401 with MSG-P4-001, a missing letter is 403 with MSG-P4-002, and both are recorded | TSD P4 v3 T6.1 and API-P4-007; FSD P4 v3 VR-P4-001-1; legacy RWB-AD-003 Permission checks |
| BR6 | A change is checked before the row is written: the role exists and is active, the value is in `LOV-SCOPE`, the `If-Match` version is current, the required fields are filled | FSD P4 v3 A2.14.3.1; TSD P4 v3 T3.1; MSG-GEN-001 |
| BR7 | Every change appends one local decision-record entry (`AC-CHG`) through the library of DP-03 and publishes `rwb.access.AccessPolicyChanged.v1` with change kind `SCOPE`; where the entry cannot be written the change is not stored | DP-03; Architecture v5 (topic `rwb.access.events.v1`); ASM-3735 |
| BR8 | A record outside the predicate is answered 404 with MSG-P4-003 "This case is not in your scope.", with no field of the record and no count, and one entry (`AC-DENY`, reason code `OUT_OF_SCOPE`) is appended | Legacy RWB-AD-003 AC2; FSD P4 v3 VR-P4-014-1 and AC-EXC-P4-014-01; ASM-3735 |
| BR9 | Where the refusal entry cannot be written the answer is 503 with MSG-P7-003 and the record is not returned: a refusal is never silent and a reach is never answered as a success | Legacy RWB-AD-003 TC-AD-003-04; MSG-P7-003; DP-03 |
| BR10 | The guard of DP-08 applies the predicate in the owning service's own query and returns no record; rwb-access runs no query over a case and holds no case row | Architecture v5 slides 10 and 14; RWB-PLT-E1037-CON; ASM-3735 |
| BR11 | A scope change needs no second approval: the security or platform administrator writes it under the C letter and the entry names the actor and the time; the change is not versioned, its history is the decision record | TSD P4 v3 T6.1; ASM-3735 |
| BR12 | A consumer applies the changed scope when it next refreshes on `rwb.access.AccessPolicyChanged.v1`; until then the answer it cached stays in force and no answer mixes two scopes | Architecture v5 (consumers of `rwb.access.events.v1`); FSD P4 v3 A2.14 |

##### 9. State transitions

None for a case, a task or a session. The state this story owns is the scope value of one role row; its history is the decision record.

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| A role with no row in this service | the role load of RWB-P4-E1019-APP writes the role | The role file passes its checks | The role carries a value of `LOV-SCOPE` and the catalogue answers it |
| A role with scope `OWN` | the security administrator posts `TEAM` | Value in `LOV-SCOPE`, `If-Match` current, entry written | The row carries `TEAM` from the commit; one `AC-CHG` entry and one `AccessPolicyChanged` with kind `SCOPE` |
| A role with scope `TEAM` | the same value posted again | The value equals the value in force | No transition: no write, no entry, no event |
| A role with scope `REGION` | a check fails, or the entry cannot be written | 422, 409 or a 503 from the library | The role keeps `REGION`; nothing is stored and nothing is published |
| Any scope | a caller reaches a record outside the predicate | The record does not match the predicate of the caller | 404 with MSG-P4-003 and one `AC-DENY` entry with reason code `OUT_OF_SCOPE` |
| Any scope | the refusal entry cannot be written | The library answers 503 | 503 with MSG-P7-003; the record is not returned |

TSD P4 v3 T4 gives a rule package version the lifecycle `LOADED` to `REFUSED` (`LOV-VERSION-STATUS`). This story adopts none of it: `role` carries no version and no effective date, so a scope change is a current value with a recorded decision and not a version (ASM-3735).

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| rwb-access service identity (per-service login, DP-02) | Answers the scope read, writes a scope change, runs the checks, builds the predicate, appends the entries and publishes the access-policy event |
| RW-SECADM, security administrator | CRUDA in Platform administration: maintains and reads every role's scope, and reads the entries of the changes and refusals |
| RW-PLATADM, platform administrator | CRUD in Platform administration: maintains and reads every role's scope |
| RW-AUDIT, internal audit | R in Platform administration: reads the scopes and the entries; writes nothing |
| RW-COE, center of excellence analyst | R in Platform administration: reads the scopes only; a scope is not a rule package or a parameter |
| RW-DATASTEW and RW-COMPLY | R in Platform administration: read the scopes for the data-product and the PDPA reading of the same rows |
| Every business role (RW-CASEOWN, RW-TEAMMGR, RW-LITOFF and the rest) | Uses the scope of its own roles when a case list or a case is answered, and is refused out-of-scope records with MSG-P4-003; holds no right in Platform administration |
| RW-REFADM, reference data administrator | R in Rules and parameters and no right in Platform administration: maintains no scope, which is not reference data |
| Every other service identity (SY-* and the 19 services) | Receives the scope-predicated answer through the guard and reads no operation of this story; no agent bypasses the predicate |
| Delegation of authority | No level of `delegation_limit` applies: a scope is role administration, not a credit decision |

The scope is role administration, not reference data. `role` and `permission` are P4's own tables under the Ownership Map, and the reference-data contract of rwb-case holds `lov_value`, `reference_row` and `reference_version` only; `LOV-SCOPE` is carried as this service's own list constraint (ASM-3735). The legacy Permission checks table gives this key one row, Platform administration R, for API-P4-007 `GET /admin/roles`; that read belongs to RWB-P4-E1019-APP and is neither restated nor changed here. The legacy Endpoints table gives no write endpoint, so the two scope operations and their rights are the contract's decision recorded in RWB-P4-AD003-CON (GAP-2265; ASM-3735).

##### 11. Data

| BR Field ID | Table in `rwb_access` | Field | Read or write |
|---|---|---|---|
| DF-REF-034 | `role` | `id` | Read |
| DF-REF-035 | `role` | `role_code` | Read, and the key of the change path |
| DF-REF-036 | `role` | `role_name` | Read |
| DF-REF-037 | `role` | `role_class` | Read |
| DF-REF-038 | `role` | `default_scope` | Read and write — the scope of this story |
| DF-REF-039 | `role` | `entra_group` | Read |
| DF-REF-041 | `permission` | `role_id` | Read |
| DF-REF-042 | `permission` | `capability_area` | Read |
| DF-REF-043 | `permission` | `letters` | Read — the R and C of the caller |
| DF-REF-044 | `permission` | `matrix_version` | Read |
| — | role row standard columns | `version`, `is_active`, `updated_at`, `updated_by` | Read; `version` is the `If-Match`, `updated_at`/`updated_by` are written by the change |
| — | decision record (library of DP-03) | entry id, decision code, reason code, actor, role code, scope value, time | Write |

The legacy Data table also named `recovery_case` (DF-CAS-001 to DF-CAS-023), `assignment` (DF-WRK-009 to DF-WRK-016) and `decision_log_entry` (DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018). `recovery_case` and `assignment` are P3's and `decision_log_entry` is P7's; they appear in this story only as the columns DF-CAS-009, DF-CAS-011 and DF-CAS-012 that the predicate is compared with, in P3's own query, and as the shared topic the local entry is forwarded to (ASM-3735). No foreign key crosses a schema and no table outside `rwb_access` is read or written.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner `rwb-access` (P4); base `/api/recovery/access/v1` (DP-13). The shapes are RWB-P4-AD003-CON's and are implemented here unchanged.

| Method | Path | Shape | Access |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/admin/role-scopes` | `RoleScopePage`: query `scope`, `roleClass`, `page`, `size` (default 50, max 200); each role in force with its scope value and the four `LOV-SCOPE` values | Platform administration R |
| PATCH | `/admin/role-scopes/{roleCode}` | `RoleScopeChange` in with `If-Match` and `Idempotency-Key`; the role out with its new scope and the entry reference | Platform administration C |

Both operations are served through the gateway-bff composite route for SCR-43 (DP-19). Errors: 401 no session or no Workbench role (MSG-P4-001), 403 no right (MSG-P4-002), 404 unknown or inactive role, 409 stale `If-Match` or a repeated key answered differently, 422 a value outside `LOV-SCOPE` or a missing field (MSG-GEN-001), 503 the entry not written (MSG-P7-003). The read is safe and repeatable; the change is idempotent by `Idempotency-Key`, and a repeated key returns the first answer and writes no second change.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

None. This story consumes no operation of another service at run time. The case list behind AC1 is P3's own `GET /cases` and appears only as the `rwb-case` contract mock in tests (DP-11); rwb-access holds no contract dependency on it and no case row is read.

| Called by | What it uses | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| Every service that authorises a record | The scope element of the authorise answer, and the guard that applies it in its own query | P4 for the data, RWB-PLT-E1037-CON for the library |
| SCR-43 through gateway-bff | The composite route over the two operations of 12.1 | P4 for the operations, RWB-PLT-N001-CON for the route |

###### 12.3 Events published

| Event | Topic | Contract element |
|---|---|---|
| `rwb.access.AccessPolicyChanged.v1` | `rwb.access.events.v1` | Change kind `SCOPE`, the role code, the new scope value, the actor and the time |
| `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` | `rwb.decision-record.v1` | Entry id, decision code (`AC-CHG` for a change, `AC-DENY` for a refusal with reason code `OUT_OF_SCOPE`), role code, scope value, time |

Both messages use the CloudEvents 1.0 envelope (id, source, type, specversion, time, subject, datacontenttype) written through the outbox of the service template, with a retry topic and a `.dlt` topic. No message carries a person, a case, a case count, a name, an e-mail address or an identity number.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. `rwb-access` is the owner of the access answer, not a subscriber of it; the service adds no subscription to this capability.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None. Both operations are synchronous REST answers in the caller's thread: no workflow, no activity, no signal, and no Temporal dependency. The six-monthly access review Schedule (`JOB-18`) is RWB-P4-AD008-CON's; a scope is applied inside a request and never by a workflow.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. Nothing about a scope runs on a clock.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Use contracted here |
|---|---|---|
| `role` | P4 (`rwb_access`) | `default_scope` (DF-REF-038) is the scope; the code, name and class travel with it; `version` is the `If-Match` |
| `permission` | P4 (`rwb_access`) | The Platform administration R and C letters of the caller (DF-REF-040 to DF-REF-044), read only |
| `recovery_case`, `assignment` | P3 (`rwb_case`) | Not read and not written; DF-CAS-009, DF-CAS-011 and DF-CAS-012 are named as the columns the predicate is compared with, in P3's query |
| `decision_log_entry` | P7 (`rwb_decision`) | Not read and not written; the local entry is the library's and reaches P7 on `rwb.decision-record.v1` |
| `lov_value`, `reference_row`, `reference_version` | P3 (`rwb_case`) | Not read; `LOV-SCOPE` is this service's own constraint (ASM-3735) |

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Documented answer | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| `rwb-access` role-scope WireMock (from RWB-P4-AD003-CON) | The two paths of 12.1 with one role of each `LOV-SCOPE` value, one change of `OWN` to `TEAM` with its entry reference, the stored answer for a repeated key, 409 stale version, 422 MSG-GEN-001, 404 unknown role, 403 MSG-P4-002 and 503 MSG-P7-003 | This story, the screen tests, the wave 4 harness |
| Scope predicate fake (with RWB-PLT-E1037-CON) | A predicate of each of the four values with `teamCode`, `regionCode` and `caseOwnerRef`, the `TEAM` predicate of a session with no team code, and no record | This story, every consuming service |
| `rwb-case` case-list mock (RWB-P3-E1018-CON) | `GET /cases` returning only the cases the caller owns, and the out-of-scope case answering 404 with MSG-P4-003 | This story, AC1 and AC2 |
| Decision-record fake (RWB-PLT-E1027-CON) | The `AC-CHG` and `AC-DENY` appends, the hash-chain check and 503 with MSG-P7-003 | This story, TC-AD-003-04 |

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Count | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| REST | 2 provided, 0 consumed | The scope read and the scope change under `/api/recovery/access/v1`; the predicate travels in the authorise answer and is applied by the consumer, one hop, 2 s timeout |
| Kafka | 2 published, 0 consumed | `rwb.access.AccessPolicyChanged.v1` on `rwb.access.events.v1`; `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` on `rwb.decision-record.v1` |
| Temporal | None | No workflow, activity or Schedule |
| File | None | No file in this story |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Deliverables.** The two REST resources and their OpenAPI-generated interfaces, the `role` and `permission` read/write layer, the `LOV-SCOPE` enumeration as data and as schema, the scope assembler that fills the library descriptor, the guard binding for the consumer side, the `AC-CHG` and `AC-DENY` appends through the decision-record library, the outbox record for `rwb.access.AccessPolicyChanged.v1`, the SCR-43 list and change states, and the four test classes of section 16.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H `RWB-PLT-E1027-CON` |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none — the caller's identity arrives in the ACE sign-in claim and no `v_ace_*` view is read here |
| DP-08 | RecoveryAccessGuard | Authorise contract of rwb-access and the guard library | H `RWB-PLT-E1037-CON`; C `RWB-P4-E1037-CON` |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` → `/api/recovery/access/v1` | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route for SCR-43 | H `RWB-PLT-N001-CON` |

DP-05 is applied by keeping the boundary: the caller's user, team and region codes come from the session, and no ACE view or ACE table is read. The C row `RWB-P4-E1037-CON` does not block the build: the story builds against its published fake (DP-11).

**Build steps.** (1) Flyway step for the two tables in `rwb_access` and the `LOV-SCOPE` constraint, if the service baseline does not already carry them. (2) Read and change services with the checks of BR5 and BR6. (3) Scope assembler and guard binding against the library fake. (4) Decision-record append and outbox record with the entry reference returned in the change answer. (5) SCR-43 states through the gateway-bff route. (6) Contract tests and the four test classes, then the acceptance run of section 16.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | Type | Message | When |
|---|---|---|---|
| MSG-P4-001 | Error | You have no Recovery Workbench role. Ask your team manager to request one. | The session holds no Workbench role (VR-P4-001-1) |
| MSG-P4-002 | Error | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. | The caller lacks the R or C letter of Platform administration |
| MSG-P4-003 | Error | This case is not in your scope. | A record outside the predicate (VR-P4-014-1) |
| MSG-GEN-001 | Error | Enter {field}. | A required field is empty or a value is outside `LOV-SCOPE` |
| MSG-P7-003 | Error | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. | The decision-record library answers 503 |

409 for a stale `If-Match` and 404 for an unknown or inactive role code are answered as RFC 9457 problem details with no business text, because no message id is fixed for them in the sources (GAP-2265; ASM-3735). No message contains a person, a case number, a count or a field value.

##### 15. Screens and states

| Screen | States | Route |
|---|---|---|
| SCR-43 Roles and access | List of roles with scope, class and the four values; Scope change (value, `If-Match`, confirm); Refused (MSG-P4-002); Validation (MSG-GEN-001); Conflict (stale version); Recording failed (MSG-P7-003); Access log tab | gateway-bff composite route over `GET /admin/role-scopes` and `PATCH /admin/role-scopes/{roleCode}`, and the existing `GET /admin/access-log` of RWB-P4-AD007-APP |

The screen shows the four `LOV-SCOPE` values as labels, never as free text, and shows no case data: it is a role administration screen. A refusal the screen shows is the 404 of a case read rendered by the case screen, not a screen of this story.

##### 16. Test cases

| TC ID | Covers | Level | Data |
|---|---|---|---|
| TC-AD-003-01 | AC1 | Component | Role RW-CASEOWN with scope `OWN` owning 12 cases; the `rwb-case` mock returns those 12 only; the list returns 12 and a total of 12 |
| TC-AD-003-02 | AC2 | Component | Case `RW-2026-000456` in team `MTG-NE` under another owner; session scope `TEAM`; the read is 404 with MSG-P4-003, no field, no count, and one `AC-DENY` entry with `OUT_OF_SCOPE` |

The four legacy test case IDs are kept unchanged; their level is assigned here (§R7.2). The data of each case is a business value already named in the legacy key or in FSD P4 v3 A2.14; no new business value is introduced.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the four `LOV-SCOPE` values, the messages and the right letters come from data or from the message catalogue (BR-P4-014).
- No PII in events, workflow inputs or logs: the access-policy event and the decision entry carry a role code and a scope value only; a refusal entry carries no case number, no owner and no count.
- ACE data only through the owner's contract or `v_ace_*` views: this story reads no ACE table and no `v_ace_*` view; the caller's codes come from the session.
- One schema, one login: every read and write of this story stays inside `rwb_access` under the per-service login (DP-01, DP-02).
- A refusal is indistinguishable from an absence and is always recorded; a record is never returned unbound and never answered as a success.

##### 1. Story

As a **consumer of the access service** — the enforcement point, the two administration screens and any service that shows a personal field — I want **one published masking-profile contract for `rwb-access`, with the profile, its version in force, the masked-by-default invariant and the unmask answer**, so that **every consumer masks the same way from Day 1 and none of them reads `masking_rule` or guesses what a mask looks like**.

This is the contract half of legacy RWB-AD-004. It publishes three operations and their schemas and declares nothing else:

- **Service facts.** REST base `/api/recovery/access/v1` (DP-13), schema `rwb_access`, topic `rwb.access.events.v1`, event names `rwb.access.<Event>.v1`, task queue `rwb-access` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.access`. The document is OpenAPI 3.1 and its major version is in the base path.
- **The three operations.** `GET /admin/masking-profiles` (the rows of the version in force for the roles and fields asked), `POST /admin/masking-profile-versions` (write a dated version) and `POST /admin/masking-profiles/{roleCode}/unmask` (one field in clear, with one PII record). None of the three has an ownership row or an operation id in TSD P4 v3 — **Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2267; ASM-3736)**.
- **The row and the version.** `MaskingProfileRow` carries `roleCode`, `fieldId`, `unmasked`, `maskingVersion`, `validFrom`, `validTo`, `view` and `column`; `MaskingProfilePage` adds the page and `versionInForce`. The `view` and `column` are resolved from the field id and are not columns of `masking_rule` (TSD P4 v3 T3.1) — **Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2267; ASM-3738)**.
- **Masked by default, in the schema.** `unmasked` defaults to false, a field with no row is stated as masked, and the document states that the masked value comes from `v_ace_customer.id_no_masked` or `v_ace_contact.contact_value_masked`, or from the masker shape where the view has none. The FSD shapes are kept: `XXXXXXXXX1234`, `XXXXXX5678`, `XXXX-XX-XX`.
- **The unmask answer.** `UnmaskedField` carries `fieldId`, `value`, `maskingVersion` and `piiRecordId`; the document states that the record is written before the value is answered, so a record that cannot be written answers nothing — **Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2267; ASM-3737)**.
- **The rights.** Reference data R for the read, Reference data C for the write, and the row's own `unmasked` flag for the unmask (TSD P4 v3 T6.1). The approval right A is RW-COMPLY's and belongs to the approve gate of RWB-P4-AD010-APP, which this document refers to and does not declare (ASM-3739).
- **No business event.** The ownership rows give `rwb-access` no event; the only publication is the decision-record message of the local library on `rwb.decision-record.v1` (DP-03), and a masking change travels on the profile read and the access log (ASM-3741).
- **Consumers.** The enforcement point of RWB-P4-E1037-APP, SCR-47 Personal data and SCR-43 Roles and access through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19), and every service that shows a personal field through the guard of RWB-PLT-E1037-CON.
- **The fake.** One profile fake with the SIT rows of `MASK-SIT-01`, the version in force and the refusals, and a drift job that fails the build when an answer and the document disagree.

##### 2. Business rationale

The profile is only worth holding as data if every reader reads it the same way. Without a published contract a consumer guesses what the profile read returns, whether a rule names a view and a column or only a field id, what an unmask answers, which right it needs and what the PII record holds — and the guesses drift at the first profile change, in the one place where a drift shows a personal field in clear. With the contract, the app story and the enforcement point compile and test from Day 1 against a fake, and neither of them can quietly read `masking_rule` because the contract gives it no connection to do so.

This is the pattern of the whole realignment: a contract-first service answers one hop from its own schema, and the consumer builds against the published shape and its fake (ADR-020). The contract also fixes the two things a data change must never move: the masked-by-default invariant and the ban on the clear identity number. A version that names it is refused at the write, and the schema says so.

The story is Day 1 work with no build dependency, so the enforcement point and the screens are not blocked by the profile implementation. That is the point of a contract group: the four stories of wave 4 that touch a personal field start against this document on day one.

##### 3. Preconditions

| Precondition | What it gives this story |
|---|---|
| The service row and naming rules of the context pack | The base `/api/recovery/access/v1`, schema `rwb_access`, topic `rwb.access.events.v1`, task queue `rwb-access`, Java package, epic RWB-SVC-P4 |
| TSD P4 v3 T3.1 and T3.2 | `masking_rule` and its seven fields (DF-REF-198 to DF-REF-204); `LOV-ROLE` and `LOV-VERSION-STATUS` |
| TSD P4 v3 T6.1 and T6.2 | The Reference data letters R, C and A per role, and the rule that each endpoint declares its capability area and right |
| Legacy RWB-AD-004 | The three criteria, the five messages, the two screens and the guardrail that a rule names a view column and never the clear identity number |
| FSD P4 v3 A2.5 | FEAT-ACA-05, BR-P4-005 and the mask shapes of the three examples |
| The ownership rows of P4 | The four operations the service already provides (`GET /admin/access-log`, `GET /admin/roles`, `GET /me/session`, `POST /admin/break-glass-grants`) and the five tables it owns; the profile operations are not among them — **Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2267; ASM-3736)** |
| The error catalogue | MSG-P4-001, MSG-P4-002, MSG-P4-003, MSG-GEN-001 and MSG-P7-003, as the legacy story names them |

##### 4. Flow

1. Draft the OpenAPI 3.1 document for the three operations under the base `/api/recovery/access/v1`, with the components the service's other operations use, and pin it at version 1.
2. Declare `MaskingProfileRow`, `MaskingProfilePage`, `MaskingProfileVersion`, `MaskingProfileVersionRow`, `UnmaskRequest`, `UnmaskedField` and the shared error envelope, with the example values of the FSD.
3. Declare the rights per operation from TSD T6.1: Reference data R for the read, Reference data C for the write, and the row's `unmasked` flag for the unmask, which the document describes as a data condition and not as a letter.
4. Declare the errors: 401 MSG-P4-001, 403 MSG-P4-002, 404 MSG-P4-003, 409 a version label already in force or a stale `If-Match`, 422 MSG-GEN-001 or a version refused whole, 503 MSG-P7-003.
5. Declare the two consumed operations for the reader: the case read of P3 and the ACE view read of P1, one hop each, 2 s budget, mock only (DP-05, DP-11).
6. Write the invariants as document text and as schema constraints: masked by default, `unmasked` false unless a row says otherwise, the clear identity number in no field and in no example, the PII record written before the value is answered.
7. Publish the profile fake: the `MASK-SIT-01` rows, the version in force on a date, an allowed unmask and a refused one, and a forced decision-record failure.
8. Add the drift job: the fake's answers are compared with the document on every build, and a change to one without the other fails the pipeline.
9. Hand the document and the fake to RWB-P4-AD004-APP, RWB-P4-E1037-APP and RWB-P4-E1037-CON; publish no message of its own.

##### 5. Exception paths

| Exception | Answer in the document | Why it matters to a consumer |
|---|---|---|
| A consumer calls a path on the monolith base `/api/recovery/v1` | Not declared; 404 from the edge | The one-hop rule has one base per service (DP-13) |
| A consumer asks with no session or no Workbench role | 401 MSG-P4-001 | The consumer must not treat a 401 as an empty profile |
| A consumer's role holds no Reference data R | 403 MSG-P4-002 | A profile read is never answered empty as a fallback |
| A field with no row in the version in force | `unmasked` false and the masked column named | The absence of a rule never widens a view |
| A version naming the clear identity number or repeating a role and field pair | 422 and the whole version refused | The invariant is enforced at the boundary, not at each consumer |
| A version label already in force or a stale `If-Match` | 409 | A retry is safe and writes no second version |
| The record or the PII record cannot be written | 503 MSG-P7-003 | The consumer must show nothing rather than an unrecorded value |
| The P1 view read fails | 503; no clear fallback is declared | Fail closed on a personal field |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Letter | Finding |
|---|---|
| Independent | No build dependency; the document and the fake stand on their own |
| Negotiable | The schema names and the example values are the document's; the paths follow the service base and the legacy capability |
| Valuable | Every consumer of a personal field builds and tests against one published shape from Day 1 |
| Estimable | One document, six schemas, one fake, one drift job |
| Small | No code beyond the fake and the drift check; no workflow, no schedule, no event |
| Testable | Each criterion is a Contract check on the document or on the fake's answer |

    And each of the three names its right from TSD P4 v3 T6.1
