```gherkin
    Given the contract fake is started with the rows of MASK-SIT-01
    When a consumer calls GET /admin/masking-profiles with roleCode RW-CASEOWN and validOn 2026-12-03
    Then the answer is a MaskingProfilePage whose versionInForce is MASK-SIT-01
    And every row carries roleCode, fieldId, unmasked, maskingVersion, validFrom, validTo, view and column
    And the row of the identity number names the column id_no_masked of the view v_ace_customer

  Scenario: AC3 The unmask answer carries the value and the record reference (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the contract fake is started with a row of RW-CASEOWN whose unmasked is true for the contact value
    When a consumer calls POST /admin/masking-profiles/RW-CASEOWN/unmask with case RW-2026-000123 and that field id
    Then the answer is an UnmaskedField with that fieldId, the value from v_ace_contact.contact_value, the maskingVersion and a piiRecordId
    And the document states that no value is answered when the PII record cannot be written

  Scenario: AC4 Masked by default and the clear identity number are declared as invariants (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the published document and its examples
    When the schemas and the examples are scanned
    Then a row with unmasked false, and a field with no row, are declared masked with the column named
    And no schema, field or example carries the clear identity number
    And the document states the mask shapes XXXXXXXX1234 for an identity number, XXXXXX5678 for a phone and XXXX-XX-XX for a date

  Scenario: AC5 Every failure is one envelope with one message (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given a caller whose role holds no Reference data R
    When it calls the profile read on the fake
    Then the answer is 403 with MSG-P4-002 in the one error envelope
    And the document declares 401 with MSG-P4-001, 404 with MSG-P4-003, 422 with MSG-GEN-001 and 503 with MSG-P7-003 on the operations where each can occur

  Scenario: AC6 The fake matches the document and carries no personal data (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the fake and the drift job of the build
    When the fake's answers are compared with the document
    Then every declared operation, status and message id is answered as declared
    And a change to one side without the other fails the build
    And no personal value, and no case number beyond the example, appears in the fake or in the examples
```

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | One base per service: `/api/recovery/access/v1`, with the major version in the path | DP-13; ADR-020 |
| BR2 | A personal field is masked unless a row of the version in force says `unmasked` true for a role the caller holds | Legacy AC1 |
| BR3 | A masking rule names the view column the masked value comes from, and no rule returns the clear identity number | Legacy guardrail; ADR-010 |
| BR4 | The version in force on a date is the latest `valid_from` not after it; an applied version is never edited | TSD T4 |
| BR5 | The PII record is written before the value is answered; a record that cannot be written answers nothing | Legacy AC2; ASM-3737 |
| BR6 | An error is one envelope with one message id from the catalogue, and a refusal changes nothing | FSD VR-P4-005-1 |
| BR7 | No personal data in an example, a fake, a schema or a message | Legacy guardrail; NFR-040 |

##### 9. State transitions

| From | Trigger | To | What the document must say |
|---|---|---|---|
| (none) | `POST /admin/masking-profile-versions` passes every check | LOADED | The answer carries the version, its status and its id; 409 if the label is already in force |
| LOADED | the approve gate of RWB-P4-AD010-APP | APPROVED | Declared by that contract, referred to here and not declared |
| APPROVED | `valid_from` arrives | IN_FORCE | `versionInForce` of the read changes on that date with no deployment |
| IN_FORCE | a later version reaches IN_FORCE | SUPERSEDED | `validTo` of the earlier version is the day before the later `validFrom` |
| IN_FORCE | a rollback of the reference version | ROLLED_BACK | Declared by the rollback operation of AD010, and the earlier version is answered again |
| LOADED | a check fails | REFUSED | 422 and no row of the version stored |

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner `rwb-access` (P4); base `/api/recovery/access/v1`.

| Method | Path | Schemas | Right |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/admin/masking-profiles` | query `roleCode`, `fieldId`, `validOn`, `page`, `size`; answer `MaskingProfilePage` of `MaskingProfileRow` | Reference data R |
| POST | `/admin/masking-profile-versions` | `MaskingProfileVersion` in, with `Idempotency-Key`; answer the written version with status and id | Reference data C |
| POST | `/admin/masking-profiles/{roleCode}/unmask` | `UnmaskRequest` in, with `Idempotency-Key`; answer `UnmaskedField` | the row's `unmasked` flag |

Errors: 401 MSG-P4-001, 403 MSG-P4-002, 404 MSG-P4-003, 409 a version label already in force or a stale `If-Match`, 422 MSG-GEN-001 or a version refused whole, 503 MSG-P7-003. Schemas: `MaskingProfileRow` (`roleCode`, `fieldId`, `unmasked`, `maskingVersion`, `validFrom`, `validTo`, `view`, `column`), `MaskingProfilePage` (items, page, size, total, `versionInForce`), `MaskingProfileVersion` (`maskingVersion`, `validFrom`, rows of `roleCode`, `fieldId`, `unmasked`), `MaskingProfileVersionRow`, `UnmaskRequest` (`caseId`, `fieldId`), `UnmaskedField` (`fieldId`, `value`, `maskingVersion`, `piiRecordId`) and the shared error envelope. The three paths are fixed here because no source names them — **Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2267; ASM-3736)**.

The session read `GET /me/session` and the role catalogue `GET /admin/roles` are the service's own operations of RWB-P4-E1037-CON and RWB-P4-E1019-APP; this document neither restates nor changes them.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in the document as a constant: role codes, field ids, versions and mask shapes are data, and the examples are marked as examples.
- No PII in an example, a fake, a log or a message; the identity number is masked before the service and no schema carries it clear.
- ACE data only through the P1 contract or a `v_ace_*` view; the document declares no `public` table and no other service's table.
- One base per service and one hop per call, 2 s timeout; no consumer is invited to chain two calls.
- The contract declares no message id that is not in the catalogue, and no event name the ownership rows do not support.
- Secrets never in the document, the fake or the examples.

##### 1. Story

As a **Compliance and PDPA officer**, I want **a masking profile per role and per personal field held as data, naming the view column the masked value comes from**, so that **personal data is shown only to the roles allowed to see it and the clear identity number never leaves ACE**.

This is the rwb-access slice of legacy RWB-AD-004, and the profile half of that legacy key: the `masking_rule` rows as a dated version per role and per field, masked by default, the unmask path that fills one field from the ACE view and records the read, and the version in force carried on the read record of the access log.

- **Service facts.** REST base `/api/recovery/access/v1` (DP-13), schema `rwb_access`, topic `rwb.access.events.v1`, event names `rwb.access.<Event>.v1`, task queue `rwb-access` in namespace `rwb-recovery` (not used here — this story starts no workflow), Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.access`.
- **The profile row.** One `masking_rule` row is one role and one personal field in one masking version (TSD P4 v3 T3.1): `id` (DF-REF-198), `role_code` (DF-REF-199, LOV-ROLE), `field_id` (DF-REF-200), `unmasked` (DF-REF-201), `masking_version` (DF-REF-202), `valid_from` (DF-REF-203) and `valid_to` (DF-REF-204). `unmasked` says whether that role sees that field in clear in that version; a false value, or no row at all, means masked.
- **The naming rule.** The legacy guardrail is that a masking rule names the view column the masked value comes from, and `masking_rule` carries the field id only. The field id is resolved to its view and column through the P1 field registry, and no view-name column is added to `masking_rule` — **Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2266; ASM-3738)**. What a rule reports is the view and the column: `v_ace_customer.id_no_masked` and `id_no_last4`, `v_ace_contact.contact_value` and `contact_value_masked`.
- **The views.** `v_ace_customer` (DF-ACE-055 to DF-ACE-074) and `v_ace_contact` (DF-ACE-075 to DF-ACE-083) are read read-only through the P1 ACE-view contract (DP-05): the clear contact value only on the unmask path, the masked identity number and the masked contact value everywhere else. Neither view exposes the clear identity number and no rule may name it.
- **Masked by default.** A field with no rule in the version in force, or with a rule whose `unmasked` is false for every role the caller holds, is answered from the masked view column named by its field id; where the view holds no masked column, the value is masked by the masker of RWB-PLT-E1037-CON. The FSD fixes the shapes: `XXXXXXXXX1234` for the identity number, `XXXXXX5678` for the phone and `XXXX-XX-XX` for a date (FSD P4 v3 AC-ALT-P4-004-01, AC-EXC-P4-004-05).
- **The three operations of this story** are the profile read by role and by field with the version in force, the profile version write, and the unmask request and its record, at the paths the contract baseline RWB-P4-AD004-CON fixes on the service base. None of the three has a row in the ownership map and none has an operation id in TSD P4 v3 — **Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2266; ASM-3736)**.
- **The version.** A profile is written as a new dated version with its `masking_version` label and its `valid_from`; the version in force on a date is the one whose `valid_from` is the latest not after that date; the `valid_to` of the earlier version closes on the day before a later `valid_from`; a version in force is never edited (DP-15; ASM-3741).
- **The unmask record.** An unmask fills one field from `v_ace_contact.contact_value` for a role whose rule has `unmasked` true, and writes the read to the PII log. The PII log is the ACE Common audit and PII Kafka path to the SOC (TSD P4 v3 T5.1 INT-22) and not a table of `rwb_access`; its producer, record name and field list are **Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2266; ASM-3737)**.
- **The version on the record.** Every read of a personal field carries the masking version in force, the field ids and their masked flags on the read record; the access-entry writer of RWB-P4-E1039-APP writes the entry and this story supplies the version and the flags, so a profile change is visible in the access log from its `valid_from` date (ASM-3740).
- **The boundary, once.** This story owns the masking-profile version and the unmask record; RWB-P4-E1037-APP owns the enforcement point that reads the profile, the permission matrix that decides who may unmask, and the endpoint enforcement of masking. Neither story redefines the other's shape.
- **Not this story.** The reference-load path (load, approve, verify, rollback) is RWB-P4-AD010-APP's and RWB-P4-E1037-APP's; the role catalogue is RWB-P4-E1019-APP's; the access-log search, the export and the break-glass grant are RWB-P4-AD007-APP's and RWB-P4-E1039-APP's; `lov_value`, `reference_row` and `reference_version` are P3's (DP-07); `decision_log_entry` is P7's (DP-03); `partner_user` is S9's. This story writes no row of any of them.
- **Screens.** SCR-47 Personal data (loading; list; masked and unmasked states) and SCR-43 Roles and access (list; access log) are served by the gateway-bff composite route of DP-19 (RWB-PLT-N001-CON), which reads the profile and the logged reads in parallel.

##### 2. Business rationale

PDPA and the bank's own data controls say that a personal field is shown to a person only when their role needs it. The monolith answered that with one masker, one set of rules and the identity number masked inside ACE. The realignment keeps the answer and gives the rule a home: the profile is `masking_rule` rows of `rwb_access`, one row per role and per personal field, written as a dated version, so an audit can say which role could see which field on a given date and a change of masking is a data change with a Compliance approval and not a release. That is FEAT-ACA-05 of FSD P4 v3, measured by rule and limit changes made without a code release.

Masking by default is the rule, not the exception. A field with no rule is masked, and a rule that is absent, false or not in the version in force never widens what a person sees. The profile therefore only ever grants; it never leaves a field open by omission. The values come from the columns ACE already masks — `id_no_masked` and `contact_value_masked` — so the identity number is masked before the Workbench comes into it, and `id_no_last4` is the clearest identity value any rule can reach. The clear contact value is the one exception the notices and the calls need, and it is reached only through the unmask path, with the read recorded.

The boundary with the enforcement point is the profile read. RWB-P4-E1037-APP asks this story for the rows of a session's roles in the version in force and applies them on every screen, every API answer and every agent call; this story answers the version, the fields and the columns, and applies nothing. A profile version that names the clear identity number, a field id that is not a personal field, or a role code the role table does not hold is refused whole, so a mistake in one row never half-applies.

|---|---|
| RWB-P4-AD004-CON (same service, its own contract story) | The published profile contract: the three operations, `MaskingProfile`, `MaskingProfileRow`, `MaskingProfileVersion`, `MaskingProfilePage` and `UnmaskedField`, the naming rule, the masked-by-default invariant, the error envelope and the contract fakes this story builds against from Day 1 |
| RWB-PLT-E1037-CON and RWB-P4-E1037-CON | The guard and masker library and this service's own access contract (DP-08): the masker for a field with no masked view column and the permission answer that resolves the caller's roles and their Reference data letters. The DP row's C for the guard is carried as H because E1037 is a contract of this same service |
| RWB-P4-E1037-APP | The enforcement point that reads the profile; the consumer of the profile read, and the owner of the permission matrix and of the endpoint enforcement of masking |
| RWB-PLT-E1043-CON and RWB-P3-E1043-CON | The reference-data client library and the reference-data contract of rwb-case (DP-07): `LOV-ROLE` and `LOV-VERSION-STATUS` at the version in force. This story builds against the fake and never against the rwb-case build |
| RWB-PLT-E1027-CON | The local decision-record library and the shared topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` (DP-03): the entry of a profile version write and of every refusal |
| RWB-PLT-N001-CON | The gateway-bff composite route (DP-19) that serves SCR-47 and SCR-43 and merges the profile read with the logged reads |
| The `masking_rule`, `role` and `permission` tables of `rwb_access` | The profile rows (DF-REF-198 to DF-REF-204), the active role codes (DF-REF-034 to DF-REF-038) and the caller's Reference data letters, from the service baseline. This story adds no table; its migration adds the version index and the SIT seed only |
| The two ACE views and their SELECT grants | `v_ace_customer` and `v_ace_contact`, read read-only through the P1 ACE-view contract (DP-05) with their masked columns. The views are never written and never joined to a `public` table |
| The profile versions of the environment | `MASK-SIT-01` in SIT, in which only RW-CASEOWN may see the contact value in clear, and `MASK-2026.11` in production with no unmasked row until Compliance supplies the rules |
| The profile operations | The three paths and their rights, fixed on `/api/recovery/access/v1` — **Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2266; ASM-3736)** |
| The PII log | The ACE Common audit and PII Kafka path to the SOC. Its producer, record name and field list are **Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2266; ASM-3737)** |
| The Compliance approval of a version | The approve gate of RWB-P4-AD010-APP on the reference-load path, with the approver role RW-COMPLY. This story writes the version and never approves it (ASM-3739) |

##### 4. Flow

1. A reader's session arrives at the Workbench with its roles from the session answer of RWB-P4-E1037-APP; the Workbench knows the case that is on screen.
2. The enforcement point calls `GET /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/masking-profiles` with the caller's role codes, the field ids of the personal fields on the screen and `validOn` set to the business date. The answer is the rows of the version in force on that date.
3. For each personal field the answer decides one of two outcomes: a row with `unmasked` true for one of the caller's roles means the field may be unmasked on request; anything else means masked.
4. A masked field is answered from the masked view column its field id resolves to — `v_ace_customer.id_no_masked`, `v_ace_contact.contact_value_masked` — read read-only through the P1 ACE-view contract. Where the view holds no masked column, the PLT masker's shape answers (`XXXX-XX-XX` for a date).
5. A caller whose rule allows the unmask calls `POST /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/masking-profiles/{roleCode}/unmask` with the case reference and the field id. The rule is re-read for that role, that field and the date; a role with no such rule is refused before any value is read.
6. On an allowed unmask the one field is filled from `v_ace_contact.contact_value`, one PII record is written with the actor, the role code, the field id, the case reference, the masking version and the time, and the answer carries the field with its value and the record reference.
7. A profile change is written with `POST /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/masking-profile-versions`: the version label, the `valid_from` and the rows of role code, field id and `unmasked`. The version is validated whole, written with status LOADED, and the version it closes takes its `valid_to` as the day before the new `valid_from`.
8. From the `valid_from` date every read answers the new version, and every read record carries `maskingVersion` — so AC3 holds with no deployment: the responses use the new version and the access log carries the version in force.
9. Each write and each refusal writes one decision-record entry through the local library (DP-03), and the entry and the PII record are written in the same transaction window as the change they describe.

##### 5. Exception paths

| Exception | Answer | What is left unchanged |
|---|---|---|
| A caller with no Workbench role | 401 with MSG-P4-001 (session refused upstream) | Nothing is read, nothing is written |
| A caller whose roles hold no Reference data R | 403 with MSG-P4-002 naming the action, before any row is read | The profile and the case are untouched |
| An unmask for a role whose rule is absent or false in the version in force | 403 with MSG-P4-002; no value is fetched and no PII record is written | The clear value never leaves ACE |
| A case outside the caller's scope | 404 with MSG-P4-003 | No field, no count and no case number in the answer |
| A field id that is not a personal field, a role code not in the role table, or a missing field | 422 with MSG-GEN-001 | Nothing is written |
| A version whose rows name the clear identity number or repeat a role and field pair | 422; the whole version is refused and no row of it is stored | The version in force stays in force |
| A version label already in force, or a stale `If-Match` | 409 (the envelope of the contract baseline) | The version in force stays in force |
| The decision record cannot be written | 503 with MSG-P7-003 and an incident to the platform administrator queue | The version is not written and the unmask answers nothing (FSD AC-EXC-P4-007-03 pattern) |
| The PII record cannot be written | 503 with MSG-P7-003; the field value is not answered | The read is not recorded, so the value is not shown (ASM-3737) |
| The masked view read is unavailable | 503; the field is not answered in clear as a fallback | Fail closed: no unmasked value |

| Letter | Finding |
|---|---|
| Independent | Buildable against the published contract of RWB-P4-AD004-CON and the fakes of every H dependency; no other story must ship first |
| Negotiable | The version labels, the SIT seed and the mask shapes are configuration and data; the paths are the contract baseline's |
| Valuable | FEAT-ACA-05 and NFR-039: personal fields are shown by role, and the identity number is never in clear |
| Estimable | Three operations, one table, one version rule, one unmask path; the sources fix the rows and the messages |
| Small | No workflow, no schedule, no event of its own, no screen of its own; one package |
| Testable | Every criterion is a Component or Contract check on a case, a role and a version with fixed values |

```gherkin
Feature: Masking profiles per role

  Scenario: AC1 Masked by default (legacy RWB-AD-004 AC1)
    Given the rwb-case contract mock returns the case read for case RW-2026-000123
    And a role with no unmasked rule in the version in force
    When it reads a case
    Then the identity number shows from v_ace_customer.id_no_masked
    And the phone number shows from v_ace_contact.contact_value_masked

  Scenario: AC2 Unmask is logged (legacy RWB-AD-004 AC2)
    Given the rwb-source-data contract mock returns contact_value and contact_value_masked for the phone number
    And a role allowed to unmask the contact value
    When it unmasks the phone number on a case
    Then the system fills the field from v_ace_contact.contact_value and writes the read to the PII log
    And the identity number is still shown from id_no_masked, never in clear

  Scenario: AC3 Profile change (legacy RWB-AD-004 AC3)
    Given a new masking_rule version approved by Compliance
    When its valid from date arrives
    Then responses use the new version and the access log carries the version in force
```

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | A personal field is masked unless a row of the version in force says `unmasked` true for a role the caller holds | Legacy AC1; FSD A2.5 |
| BR2 | A masking rule names the view column the masked value comes from, and no rule returns the clear identity number | Legacy guardrail; ADR-010 |
| BR3 | `unmasked` true is granted per role and per field, and every unmask writes one PII record | Legacy AC2 |
| BR4 | A version applies from its `valid_from`; the version in force on a date is the latest `valid_from` not after it; an applied version is never edited | TSD T4; LOV-VERSION-STATUS |
| BR5 | Every read record carries `maskingVersion`, so the access log shows the version in force at the read | Legacy AC3; RWB-P4-E1039-APP |
| BR6 | No value a business person may change is written in code; it is a versioned data row | FSD BR-P4-005; VR-P4-005-1 |
| BR7 | An action outside the caller's rights is refused with MSG-P4-002 and nothing changes | FSD VR-P4-005-1, VR-P4-005-3 |
| BR8 | A version, a refusal or an unmask that cannot be recorded does not take effect | FSD AC-EXC-P4-005-07; MSG-P7-003 |

##### 9. State transitions

| From | Trigger | To | Side effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| (none) | `POST /admin/masking-profile-versions` passes every check | LOADED | Rows written; decision-record entry; one PII-free version summary |
| LOADED | Compliance approves through the gate of RWB-P4-AD010-APP | APPROVED | Approver and time recorded by AD010, not here |
| APPROVED | `valid_from` arrives | IN_FORCE | The read answers these rows from this date; `maskingVersion` on every read record |
| IN_FORCE | a later version reaches IN_FORCE | SUPERSEDED | `valid_to` set to the day before the later `valid_from` |
| IN_FORCE | a rollback of the reference version (AD010's operation) | ROLLED_BACK | The earlier version is in force again; recorded by AD010 |
| LOADED | a check fails | REFUSED | No row stored; the version in force unchanged; one entry |
| any | a read of a field | any | Masked or unmaskable, decided per role and field; nothing else changes |

##### 10. Authority

| Capability area | Right | Roles | Where used in this story |
|---|---|---|---|
| Reference data | R | every role of TSD P4 v3 T6.1 (RW-CASEOWN, RW-PHONECOL, RW-TEAMMGR and the rest) | the profile read |
| Reference data | C | RW-COE, RW-REFADM | the profile version write |
| Reference data | A | RW-COMPLY | the approval, held by RWB-P4-AD010-APP and not by this story |
| the row's own `unmasked` flag | — | the roles a row names with `unmasked` true | the unmask request |
| Platform administration | R | RW-COE, RW-DATASTEW, RW-AUDIT, RW-COMPLY, RW-PLATADM, RW-SECADM | the access-log panel of SCR-43, served by RWB-P4-AD007-APP |

A caller holding no right in Reference data is refused with MSG-P4-002 before any row is read; a service identity (SY-AGENT, SY-CASEWF) is subject to the same rows as a person (NFR-051).

##### 11. Data

| Table or view | Schema | Fields (BR Field IDs) | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| `masking_rule` | `rwb_access` | `id` DF-REF-198, `role_code` DF-REF-199, `field_id` DF-REF-200, `unmasked` DF-REF-201, `masking_version` DF-REF-202, `valid_from` DF-REF-203, `valid_to` DF-REF-204 | Owned: the profile row and its version |
| `role` | `rwb_access` | `role_code` DF-REF-034 to `default_scope` DF-REF-038 | Read only: the role codes a row may name |
| `permission` | `rwb_access` | `role_id`, `capability_area`, `letters` | Read only: the caller's Reference data letters (TSD T6.1) |
| `v_ace_customer` | ACE, read-only view | `cif_no`, `person_key`, `first_name`, `last_name`, `id_no_masked`, `id_no_last4` and 14 more — DF-ACE-055 to DF-ACE-074 | Read through P1: the masked identity number |
| `v_ace_contact` | ACE, read-only view | `contact_type`, `contact_key`, `person_key`, `contact_value`, `contact_value_masked` and 4 more — DF-ACE-075 to DF-ACE-083 | Read through P1: the masked contact value everywhere, the clear value on the unmask path only |

The story writes `masking_rule` and nothing else. `decision_log_entry` is P7's, written through the local library (DP-03). `lov_value`, `reference_row` and `reference_version` are P3's (DP-07). The field-to-view-and-column map is not a column of `masking_rule` — **Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2266; ASM-3738)**.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner `rwb-access` (P4); base `/api/recovery/access/v1`.

| Method | Path | Request and answer | Right | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/admin/masking-profiles` | Query `roleCode`, `fieldId`, `validOn`, `page` (default 50, max 200), `size`; answer `MaskingProfilePage` — items of `MaskingProfileRow` with `roleCode`, `fieldId`, `unmasked`, `maskingVersion`, `validFrom`, `validTo`, `view`, `column`, and the page's `versionInForce` | Reference data R | Read only |
| POST | `/admin/masking-profile-versions` | `MaskingProfileVersion` in (`maskingVersion`, `validFrom`, rows of role code, field id and `unmasked`); answer the written version with its status and its id | Reference data C | `Idempotency-Key`; the same key returns the first answer and writes no second version |
| POST | `/admin/masking-profiles/{roleCode}/unmask` | `UnmaskRequest` in (`caseId`, `fieldId`); answer `UnmaskedField` (`fieldId`, `value`, `maskingVersion`, `piiRecordId`) | the `unmasked` rule of the version in force for that role and that field | `Idempotency-Key`; the same key answers the first call and writes no second PII record |

Errors for all three: 401 no session or no Workbench role (MSG-P4-001), 403 no right (MSG-P4-002), 404 case out of scope (MSG-P4-003), 409 a version label already in force or a stale `If-Match`, 422 a missing field (MSG-GEN-001) or a version refused whole, 503 the record entry or the PII record not written (MSG-P7-003). Major version 1 sits in the base. The three paths have no ownership row and no operation id in TSD P4 v3 — **Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2266; ASM-3736)**.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Operation | Owner | What it gives | Class |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` | P3 `rwb-case` | The case and its person keys, whose personal fields are masked by this profile | Mock at test level only; the story declares no C for it |
| the ACE-view read of `rwb-source-data` for `v_ace_customer` and `v_ace_contact` (P1) | P1 `rwb-source-data` | The masked identity number, the masked contact value, and the clear contact value on the unmask path (DP-05) | Mock at test level only |

The P1 operation path is not named in the source documents — **Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2266; ASM-3736)**; the mock answers it on the P1 base `/api/recovery/source-data/v1`.

###### 12.3 Events published

| Event | Topic | Owner | Content |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` | `rwb.decision-record.v1` | PLT library (DP-03), ledger consumer P7 `rwb-decision` | Entry id, decision code (`AC-UNMSK` for an unmask, `AC-DENY` for a refusal), role code, field ids and their masked flags, masking version, case reference, time |

`rwb-access` declares no business event of its own: the ownership rows give the service no event, and a masking change travels on the profile read and on the access log rather than on a topic (ASM-3741). Every message uses the CloudEvents 1.0 envelope and carries no person, name, e-mail address, case number or identity number.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. The service holds the profile and reads it locally; it subscribes to nothing to answer a masking question.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None. All three operations are synchronous REST answers in the caller's thread: no workflow, no activity, no signal, no child.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. Nothing about a profile runs on a clock: `valid_from` and `valid_to` are dates the read compares with.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Contracted use |
|---|---|---|
| `masking_rule` | P4 (`rwb_access`) | The profile row and its version (DF-REF-198 to DF-REF-204) |
| `role` | P4 (`rwb_access`) | Read only; the active role codes a row may name |
| `permission` | P4 (`rwb_access`) | Read only; the caller's Reference data letters |
| `decision_log_entry` | P7 (`rwb_decision`) | Appears nowhere; the local entry is the library's and the ledger is P7's |
| `v_ace_customer`, `v_ace_contact` | ACE, read-only views | Named, never written and never joined to a `public` table |

No foreign key crosses a schema.

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.access.masking`, module `masking`, under the service root `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.access`.

| DP | Legacy marker | What this story does | Dependency |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Writes the local entry through the library and the shared topic, with the profile version on it | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*` | Reads the two views through the P1 contract; the clear contact value only on the unmask path | none |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | `LOV-ROLE` and `LOV-VERSION-STATUS` through the reference-data contract and its library | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-08 | RecoveryAccessGuard | The caller's roles, letters and the masker come from the guard contract of this service | H RWB-PLT-E1037-CON; C RWB-P4-E1037-CON |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | Every path sits on `/api/recovery/access/v1` | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | SCR-47 and SCR-43 are served by the gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

1. Flyway in `rwb_access`: the version index on `masking_rule` (`role_code`, `field_id`, `masking_version`, `valid_from`) and the SIT seed `MASK-SIT-01`; no new table.
2. Domain: `MaskingProfile` (rows of a version), `MaskingPolicy` (the version in force on a date), `resolveViewColumn(fieldId)` through the P1 field registry, `Masked`/`Unmaskable` value objects.
3. Read service: `GET /admin/masking-profiles` — rights from the guard, rows in force for the role codes asked, `view` and `column` resolved per row.
4. Write service: `POST /admin/masking-profile-versions` — validate the whole version (role codes exist, field ids are personal fields, no row names the clear identity number, no repeated role and field pair), close the earlier version, write LOADED, one decision-record entry.
5. Unmask service: `POST /admin/masking-profiles/{roleCode}/unmask` — re-read the rule for the role, field and date; refuse without a rule; fetch the clear value through P1; write the PII record; answer the field.
6. Wire the profile read into the enforcement point of RWB-P4-E1037-APP through the masker interface; the mask shapes of a field with no masked column come from the PLT masker.
7. Tests: unit for the version-in-force rule and for the resolution; component for the three operations with the fakes; contract drift for the answers against RWB-P4-AD004-CON; an NFR check that no personal value appears in a log, an event or a workflow input.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | Type | Message | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| MSG-P4-001 | Error | You have no Recovery Workbench role. Ask your team manager to request one. | 401 on all three operations |
| MSG-P4-002 | Error | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. | 403 no right; 403 an unmask for a role with no rule |
| MSG-P4-003 | Error | This case is not in your scope. | 404 the case of an unmask request is out of the caller's scope |
| MSG-GEN-001 | Error | Enter {field}. | 422 a missing `maskingVersion`, `validFrom`, `roleCode`, `fieldId` or `caseId` |
| MSG-P7-003 | Error | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. | 503 record entry or PII record not written |

Field validation: `unmasked` is boolean; `valid_from` and `valid_to` are dates with `valid_to` after `valid_from`; `masking_version` is a label of at most 20 characters; `field_id` is a BR Field ID of a personal field; `role_code` is one of `LOV-ROLE` in force. A version that fails one row fails whole.

##### 15. Screens and states

| Screen | States | What this story gives it |
|---|---|---|
| SCR-47 Personal data | Loading; list; masked; unmasked by the row's rule; refused | The profile rows of a role and a field with their version, and the unmask answer with its version |
| SCR-43 Roles and access | List; access log; masked by role | The `maskingVersion` and the field flags that the access-log row carries |

Both screens are gateway-bff composite routes (DP-19): the profile read and the logged reads load in parallel and no screen chains a call.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: role codes, field ids, versions and mask shapes are data rows.
- No PII in events, workflow inputs, logs or test data: the identity number is masked before the service, and `id_no_last4` is the clearest identity value reachable.
- ACE data only through the P1 contract or a `v_ace_*` view; no `public` table is read and no service reads another's tables.
- The clear contact value is fetched only on the unmask path, for a role with an `unmasked` true row, and only with a PII record written; a failure to record answers nothing.
- No rule, schema or example names the clear identity number.
- Secrets in the key store only; no secret in configuration, code or prompt.
- The service owns one schema, one login and one Flyway sequence (DP-01, DP-02, DP-15).

- The role catalogue, roles classes and scopes — RWB-P4-E1019-APP.
- The access-log search, the export and the break-glass grant — RWB-P4-AD007-APP and RWB-P4-E1039-APP.
- The separation-of-duty table and the sign-in refusal — RWB-P4-AD005.
- The delegation of authority table — RWB-P4-AD016 and RWB-P4-E1038-APP.
- ACE ingestion and the views themselves — P1 rwb-source-data.
- The ledger, its hash chain and its query — P7 rwb-decision.
- The PII log implementation in ACE Common — the shared audit and PII path (INT-22).

##### 1. Story

As a **tech lead**, I want **the published contract baseline of the separation-of-duty rule: an OpenAPI 3.1 document for the check that the sign-in calls, the conflict-table read and the conflict-version read, the `RoleConflict`, `RoleConflictVersion`, `SodCheckRequest` and `SodCheckResult` schemas, the statement that a resolved role set holding both halves of a pair refuses the whole session and records the refusal, the `conflictVersion` field the session read carries, the decision-record type with its reason code, one RFC 9457 error envelope with its message IDs, the consumed parameters read and the read-only ACE group view with their owner and one-hop budget, the contract tables of section 12 and the contract fakes**, so that **the app story builds on Day 1 against a fixed, testable contract, and the sign-in of RWB-P4-E1022-APP learns exactly what to ask, what a refusal looks like and which version of the rule it was checked against**.

The deliverable is the rule **as data plus one call**: the check, the read of the pairs of a version, the read of one version with its effective dates, the refusal rule and the field the session answers. What a role may do is not contracted here — the permission matrix is RWB-P4-E1037-CON's — and how the sign-in resolves a person's groups into role codes is RWB-P4-E1022-CON's.

##### 2. Business rationale

Contract-first REST and one hop with a 2 s timeout is the decoupling decision (DP-11, ADR-020). In the monolith the separation-of-duty table was read in the same transaction as the session and the refusal was a line of code in the resolver; nobody outside the team could say which pairs were in force, which message a refused person saw or what was recorded. In the target the check is one published operation of rwb-access and the pairs are rows of `rwb_access` with a conflict version and effective dates, so the answer the sign-in needs — may this set of role codes hold together on this date — must be written down once, with its fields, its negative answer, its record and its version.

The split of this legacy key is fixed and this contract is the rule half of it. **RWB-P4-E1022-CON and RWB-P4-E1022-APP own the sign-in, the token, the group claim and the resolution of a person's roles; this story owns the rule, the version in force, the refusal of the whole session, the refusal record and the `conflictVersion` the session answers.** The sign-in story calls this contract between the resolution and the session answer, and the two meet at one operation, which is what lets each be built and tested against the other's fake from Day 1.

Two consequences shape the document. The first is that the refusal is total and it is written down: a session is refused whole and never in part, the answer names the two role codes and the conflict version, and the same refusal becomes one decision-record entry with reason `ROLE_CONFLICT`, so the security administrator acts on a record and not on a rumour. The second is that the version is part of the answer: a session states the conflict version it was checked against, because a pair that was in force at 09:00 may not be in force at 17:00 and the audit must be able to say which rule governed one sign-in.

The document also has to be honest about what does not exist. The criterion requires an incident to the security administrator and the functional specification requires a refusal event; no source names an incident queue, an incident operation or a target service, and Architecture v5 slide 14 gives rwb-access no such event, so the refusal record is the channel and no queue, event name or operation is invented for it (GAP-0796; ASM-1479, ASM-1482).

##### 3. Preconditions

- The service template and the naming library are available (RWB-PLT-TPL), so the base path, the topic and the event names follow the platform rule rather than a local choice.
- RWB-PLT-E1027-CON is published: the decision-record library and the shared topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` (DP-03), whose entry is the refusal record this document declares. The dependency is carried by the app story, RWB-P4-AD005-APP (ASM-1486).
- RWB-PLT-E1042-CON and RWB-P3-E1042-CON are published: the parameters client library and the parameters contract of rwb-case (DP-06), through which the environment code of the deployment is read. The dependencies are carried by the app story (ASM-1485).
- RWB-PLT-N001-CON is published: the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19) that serves SCR-43 and merges the conflict-table read with the access-log read of RWB-P4-AD007-APP. The dependency is carried by the app story.
- The ACE view `v_ace_iam_group` (DF-ACE-301 to DF-ACE-304) is granted and contracted by RWB-P1-E1069-APP (DP-05); this document declares it as a read-only consumed read with its `data_as_of`.
- `role_conflict` exists with its seven fields (DF-REF-205 to DF-REF-211) in TSD P4 v3 T3.1, including `conflict_version`, `valid_from` and `valid_to`, so this key needs no invented column, unlike the mapping of RWB-P4-AD001-CON.
- The check operation has no row in the ownership map and none in TSD P4 v3 appendix T-A, where the P4 inventory holds `GET /admin/roles` (API-P4-007) and `GET /me/session` (API-P4-012) and no separation-of-duty path: the path, the request and the answer are this document's own decision on the base of §R4 and DP-13, under the operation Architecture v5 slide 14 names as `POST /authorise` — **Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0796; ASM-1478)**.
- The two administrative reads of the pairs have no row in the ownership map either; they sit on the `/admin` family TSD P4 v3 gives this service and take the Platform administration R letter of TSD P4 v3 T6.1 — **Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0796; ASM-1481)**.
- The session read `GET /me/session` (API-P4-012) belongs to RWB-P4-E1037-CON; this document adds one field to that answer and restates no operation (ASM-1480).
- No build dependency: this story is Day 1 by rule (Template and Rules §R5.7), and it holds in Contract group CG-W4 because the business epic EP08 is wave 4 in the W-MAP (§R5.6).

##### 4. Flow

1. Draft the OpenAPI 3.1 document for the three separation-of-duty operations under the base `/api/recovery/access/v1`, with the shared components the `rwb-access` operations use.
2. Fix the check operation `POST /authorise/separation-of-duty`: the request is the resolved role codes, the subject reference and the time of the sign-in; the answer is `ALLOWED` with the conflict version applied, or `REFUSED` with the two role codes, the conflict version and the reason of the pair.
3. Fix the rule of the answer: the version in force is the one whose `valid_from` is the latest not after the date of the sign-in, one version answers whole, a pair is read both ways, and the whole set is refused and never a part of it.
4. Fix the refusal statement: a refused session answers no role, no scope and no token, the sign-in answers the person MSG-P4-006 naming both role codes, and the refusal is one decision-record entry with reason `ROLE_CONFLICT` addressed to the security administrator.
5. Draft the schemas `RoleConflict` (the seven dictionary fields), `RoleConflictVersion` (the version with its effective dates, its row count, its author reference and the reference of the decision-record entry of its load), `SodCheckRequest` and `SodCheckResult`.
6. Fix the two administrative reads: the pairs in force on a date asked, and one version by its label, both with the Platform administration R letter and the 401 and 403 of the default deny rule.
7. Declare the `conflictVersion` field the session read of RWB-P4-E1037-CON carries, name API-P4-012 as the operation, and state that this document restates no operation of that contract.
8. Declare the record type `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` on `rwb.decision-record.v1` with decision code `AC-DENY` and reason code `ROLE_CONFLICT`, and declare no access event and no incident operation for the refusal.
9. Agree the error envelope and the message mapping for 401, 403, 404, 409, 422 and 503, with the business texts copied unchanged from the legacy story where the message already exists and the text of MSG-P4-006 left open.
10. Declare the consumed parameters read and the read-only ACE group view with their owners and the one-hop budget, declare no operation of another service as provided, and carry the absence of the incident channel and of the load path as the open points of this key.
11. Publish the contract tables of section 12 (nine sub-tables) and the contract fakes, then add the contract tests: schema validation, the version rule, the refusal rule, the rights, the envelope, the owner declarations and the drift between a fake and the document.
12. Tag the baseline and hand it to RWB-P4-AD005-APP and to the sign-in of RWB-P4-E1022-CON and RWB-P4-E1022-APP, which calls the check.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The document fails OpenAPI 3.1 validation | The pipeline fails and no baseline is tagged | None | AC1 |
| X2 | The document publishes a separation-of-duty path other than the three of 12.1, or an incident operation nobody owns | The review fails; the three operations are the document's and the incident is not an operation | None | AC1, AC5 |
| X3 | A schema declares a person's name, an e-mail address, a group membership of an individual or a case fact | The review fails and the property is removed; the rule is a lint item of the document | None | AC2 |
| X4 | The check answer declares a partial refusal, or a refusal with one role code only | The review fails: the whole set is refused and both role codes are named | None | AC3 |
| X5 | The document states a version rule other than the valid-from rule, or lets two versions answer at once | The review fails; the version in force is the one whose `valid_from` is the latest not after the date of the sign-in | None | AC3 |
| X6 | The document restates `GET /me/session` or declares a second session operation, or names a session field other than `conflictVersion` | The review fails; the session read is RWB-P4-E1037-CON's and this document adds one field | None | AC4 |
| X7 | The document declares an access event or a second name for the refusal, or a second topic | The review fails; the refusal is the decision record and no access event exists for it | None | AC5 |
| X8 | The document declares an operation or a table of another service as provided | The review fails; the parameters contract and the ACE view are documented as consumed | None | AC6 |
| X9 | An error response carries no `messageId`, or a `messageId` not in the agreed set | The contract test fails and the merge is blocked | None | AC7 |
| X10 | A contract fake drifts from the document | The contract test fails and the merge is blocked | None | AC8 |
| X11 | The parameters contract or the ACE view does not answer inside the 2 s budget | The call answers 503 for that read and the document declares the 503 | MSG-GEN-006 | AC6, AC7 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | No build dependency; it reads the ownership map, the platform envelopes, the parameters contract of RWB-P3-E1042-CON, the ACE-view contract of RWB-P1-E1069-APP and the session contract of RWB-P4-E1037-CON only |
| Negotiable | The field-level detail of the four schemas and the shape of the check answer are settled with the app story and the sign-in story; the base, the rights, the reason code and the envelope are fixed by the target architecture and this revision |
| Valuable | Unblocks the app story and the sign-in story on Day 1 with a written answer to "may these role codes hold together on this date, and what does a refusal record", and keeps the permission matrix, the role catalogue and the central ledger out of this contract |
| Estimable | One document, three operations, four schemas, one error envelope with eight message IDs, one record declaration, nine contract tables, four fakes and eight contract tests |
| Small | Fits one sprint with the contract tests |
| Testable | Every criterion is tested against the artefact, not against a business outcome |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: The separation-of-duty contract baseline for rwb-access

  Background:
    Given the service naming rule of the platform library is in force
    Given a pair is a "role_conflict" row of one conflict version in "rwb_access"
    Given the check is one operation of "rwb-access" on the base "/api/recovery/access/v1"

  Scenario: AC1 The document describes the check and the two reads (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the OpenAPI 3.1 document of rwb-access is published
    When it is validated against the OpenAPI 3.1 schema
    Then it validates with no error
    Then it declares the base /api/recovery/access/v1
    Then it declares POST /authorise/separation-of-duty, GET /admin/role-conflicts and GET /admin/role-conflict-versions/{versionId} with the owner rwb-access
    Then the check declares no capability letter and requires a subject reference, and the two reads declare Platform administration with the right R
    Then every operation declares 401, 403, 404, 422 and 503, and the two reads declare 409
    Then the document declares no incident operation, no incident queue and no session operation of its own

  Scenario: AC2 The four schemas carry the pair, the version and the check (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the schemas RoleConflict, RoleConflictVersion, SodCheckRequest and SodCheckResult of the document
    Then RoleConflict carries id, roleCode, conflictsWith, reason, conflictVersion, validFrom and validTo as DF-REF-205 to DF-REF-211
    Then RoleConflictVersion carries conflictVersion, validFrom, validTo, rowCount, authorReference, decisionRecordEntryRef and the rows
    Then SodCheckRequest carries the resolved role codes, the subject reference and the time of the sign-in
    Then SodCheckResult carries the decision ALLOWED or REFUSED, the conflictVersion applied and, on a refusal, roleCode, conflictsWith and reason
    Then no schema, no parameter and no example declares a person's name, an e-mail address, an identity number, a group membership or a case fact

  Scenario: AC3 A refused set refuses the whole session and the refusal is recorded (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the description of the check operation
    Then the document states that the version in force is the one whose validFrom is the latest not after the date of the sign-in, and that one version answers whole
    Then it states that a pair is read in both orders and that a set holding both halves is REFUSED
    Then a refused answer names roleCode, conflictsWith, conflictVersion and reason, and carries no role list, no scope and no token
    Then the document states that the refusal is one decision-record entry with decision code AC-DENY and reason code ROLE_CONFLICT, addressed to the security administrator
    Then the document states that where the entry cannot be written the session is not answered, and that no pair, reason or version is a constant in code

  Scenario: AC4 The session read carries the conflict version it was checked against (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the session section of the document
    Then GET /me/session (API-P4-012) is named as the operation of RWB-P4-E1037-CON and is not restated
    Then the document declares exactly one field it adds to that answer: conflictVersion
    Then the document states that a session keeps the conflictVersion it was checked against until it ends
    Then no other field of the session answer is declared, removed or retyped by this document

  Scenario: AC5 The refusal is one record and no new event (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the events section of the document
    Then rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1 is declared on the shared topic rwb.decision-record.v1 with decision code AC-DENY and reason code ROLE_CONFLICT
    Then no access event is declared for the refusal, and no second name and no second topic appear anywhere in the document
    Then the loading of a new conflict version is declared as the load path of RWB-P4-E1037-CON and not as an operation of this document
    Then no payload carries a group membership, a user reference, a name or a case fact

  Scenario: AC6 The consumed reads are declared as consumed (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the consumed section of the document
    Then GET /api/recovery/case/v1/admin/parameters is declared with the owner rwb-case and the parameters contract RWB-P3-E1042-CON, for the environment code only
    Then the read-only ACE group view v_ace_iam_group is declared with the owner of RWB-P1-E1069-APP, its fields DF-ACE-301 to DF-ACE-304 and its data_as_of
    Then both are declared one hop, with the 2 s client budget and the 503 when the read does not answer in time
    Then no operation, table or list owned by another service is declared as provided, and no rule package table appears in the document

  Scenario: AC7 Every failure is one envelope with one message (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the error envelope component of the document
    When a 401, 403, 404, 409, 422 or 503 response is produced by any of the three operations
    Then the body carries the code, the message, the messageId, the traceId and the field list, with the problem media type
    Then 401 carries MSG-P4-001, 403 carries MSG-P4-002, 404 carries MSG-P4-003 or MSG-GEN-004, 409 carries MSG-GEN-004, 422 carries MSG-GEN-001 and 503 carries MSG-P7-003 or MSG-GEN-006
    Then MSG-P4-006 is declared for the refusal of a session and its text is left open, and the message texts are the legacy texts where the message already exists

  Scenario: AC8 The fakes match the document and carry no personal data (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the four contract fakes of section 12.8
    When a fake is compared with the document
    Then the separation-of-duty fake answers the three paths of 12.1: a version in force with the pair RW-WRITEOFF and RW-WOCOMM, a set with one of the two, and a next version with a later validFrom
    Then the sign-in fake answers a resolved role set and no session
    Then the parameters fake answers the environment code of the deployment
    Then the ACE group fake answers the group of each role code with its data_as_of, and the decision-record fake answers the entry append and the 503 with MSG-P7-003
    Then a contract test fails on any drift between a fake and the document, and no fake carries a name or an e-mail address
```

These eight criteria test the artefact only. No criterion restates a legacy acceptance criterion: the two legacy criteria of RWB-AD-005 are owned by RWB-P4-AD005-APP and are listed with their tests in section 16 as the cases this contract is the ground of. Every value they use is the legacy or the functional-specification value unchanged: the role codes `RW-WRITEOFF` and `RW-WOCOMM`, the message IDs, and the conflict version fields DF-REF-205 to DF-REF-211.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | One REST base per service: `/api/recovery/access/v1`; the document never declares another service's path, table or event | DP-13; Architecture v5 slides 14 and 41 |
| BR2 | A consumed read is described as consumed, never as provided; its owner comes from the ownership map | DP-11; Ownership Map v1 |
| BR3 | Events are named `rwb.<short>.<Event>.v1` on the topic `rwb.<short>.events.v1`, the shared record type stays on `rwb.decision-record.v1`, and the envelope is CloudEvents 1.0 | Architecture v5 slides 14, 20 and 43; Template and Rules §R4 |
| BR4 | This capability publishes no access event for a refusal and declares no incident operation: the refusal is one decision-record entry with reason `ROLE_CONFLICT`, and the access-policy event belongs to the load path of RWB-P4-E1037-CON | Architecture v5 slide 14; ASM-1479, ASM-1482 |
| BR5 | The contract declares no table of another service: `lov_value`, `reference_row` and `reference_version` are P3's, `parameter_catalog` and `parameter_value` are P3's, `decision_log_entry` and the rule package tables are P7's, and `partner_user` is S9's | DP-01; ownership map |
| BR6 | A pair is two role codes of one conflict version, read in both orders; a pair that forbids one role with any business role is one row per business role | TSD P4 v3 T3.1 (DF-REF-206, DF-REF-207); FSD P4 v3 AC-EXC-P4-001-03; ASM-1490 |
| BR7 | The version in force is the one whose `valid_from` is the latest not after the date of the sign-in, one version answers whole, and a session keeps the version it was checked against until it ends | Legacy RWB-AD-005 AC2; TSD P4 v3 T3.2 (LOV-VERSION-STATUS); ASM-1484 |
| BR8 | A resolved set holding both halves of a pair is refused whole: the answer carries no role list, no scope and no token, and the person receives MSG-P4-006 naming both role codes | Legacy RWB-AD-005 AC1; FSD P4 v3 AC-EXC-P4-001-03 |
| BR9 | The refusal is one decision-record entry through the library of DP-03 with decision code `AC-DENY` and reason code `ROLE_CONFLICT`, and where it cannot be written the session is not answered | DP-03; FSD P4 v3 AC-EXC-P4-001-03 and AC-EXC-P4-001-06; MSG-P7-003 |
| BR10 | The check is called by the sign-in of this service with a subject reference and declares no capability letter; the two administrative reads need Platform administration R, and the default deny rule answers 401 and 403 | TSD P4 v3 T6.1, API-P4-007 and API-P4-012; FSD P4 v3 VR-P4-004-1; ASM-1481 |
| BR11 | The environment code is read as a parameter and never declared as a constant or an enumerated list in the document | DP-06; ASM-1485 |
| BR12 | No schema, parameter, example or fake declares a name, an e-mail address, an identity number, a group membership of an individual or a case fact | REQ-ACA-005; guardrails |
| BR13 | The `conflictVersion` field is the only element this document adds to the session read of RWB-P4-E1037-CON, and that operation is named and not restated | TSD P4 v3 API-P4-012; ASM-1480 |
| BR14 | A schema change is additive within major version 1; a removed, renamed or retyped field is a new major version | Architecture v5 slide 42 |

A conflict version has its own states — loaded, approved, in force, superseded, refused — and they are the data states of the load path of RWB-P4-E1037-CON and of the app story, not states of this document.

##### 11. Data

The contract baseline declares shapes, not business values.

| Item | Content |
|---|---|
| Pair | `id` (DF-REF-205), `roleCode` (DF-REF-206, LOV-ROLE), `conflictsWith` (DF-REF-207, varchar(30)), `reason` (DF-REF-208, varchar(200)), `conflictVersion` (DF-REF-209, varchar(20)), `validFrom` (DF-REF-210, date), `validTo` (DF-REF-211, date, optional) |
| Conflict version | `conflictVersion`, `validFrom`, `validTo`, `rowCount`, `authorReference`, `decisionRecordEntryRef`, `rows[]` |
| Check request | The resolved role codes, the subject reference and the time of the sign-in; no name, no group and no case |
| Check answer | The decision `ALLOWED` or `REFUSED`, the `conflictVersion` applied and, on a refusal, `roleCode`, `conflictsWith` and `reason` |
| Session field | `conflictVersion`, added to the answer of `GET /me/session` (API-P4-012), which is declared by RWB-P4-E1037-CON (ASM-1480) |
| Environment | The code of this deployment, read as a parameter through the parameters contract of rwb-case; the parameter code is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0796; ASM-1485) |
| Record payload | Entry id, decision code `AC-DENY`, reason code `ROLE_CONFLICT`, the two role codes, the conflict version, the environment and the time; no name, no e-mail address and no group membership |
| Refused person | The subject reference and the pair, carried by the record; MSG-P4-006 to the person |

Three values the sources do not fix are this baseline's decision and are carried as placeholders. The path and the payloads of the check have no row in the ownership map or in TSD P4 v3 appendix T-A — **Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0796; ASM-1478)**. The field name `conflictVersion` of the session answer is this document's choice, because API-P4-012 names "conflict versions" in its purpose and declares no field — **Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0796; ASM-1480)**. The text of MSG-P4-006 is declared by no source — **Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0796; ASM-1479)**.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner `rwb-access` (P4); base `/api/recovery/access/v1`.

| Method | Path | Documented shape | Access |
|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/authorise/separation-of-duty` | `SodCheckRequest` in — the resolved role codes, the subject reference and the time; `SodCheckResult` out — `ALLOWED` with the conflict version, or `REFUSED` with `roleCode`, `conflictsWith`, `conflictVersion` and `reason` | The sign-in of this service with a subject reference; no capability letter |
| GET | `/admin/role-conflicts` | The pairs in force on the date asked: `roleCode`, `conflictsWith`, `reason`, `conflictVersion`, `validFrom`, `validTo`. Query `roleCode`, `validOn`, `conflictVersion`, `page`, `size` (default 50, max 200) | Platform administration R |
| GET | `/admin/role-conflict-versions/{versionId}` | `RoleConflictVersion`: the effective dates, the row count, the author reference, the decision-record entry reference and the rows | Platform administration R |

Errors for all three: 401 no subject or no Workbench role (MSG-P4-001), 403 no right (MSG-P4-002), 404 a path this service does not publish or an unknown version, role or pair (MSG-P4-003, MSG-GEN-004), 409 a version label that does not exist or two versions in force on the date asked (MSG-GEN-004), 422 a missing or invalid field (MSG-GEN-001), 503 the record entry not written (MSG-P7-003) or the group reference not readable (MSG-GEN-006). No operation of 12.1 writes a row: the check answers, and the only write of the call is the refusal entry of the library. Major version 1 sits in the path (BR14).

The session read `GET /me/session` (API-P4-012) belongs to RWB-P4-E1037-CON and appears in this document as one declared field of its answer, `conflictVersion` (AC4); the contract declares no second session operation and no other session field.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

One hop per call, 2 s timeout and a breaker per downstream (DP-11).

| Method | Path | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/admin/parameters` | P3 `rwb-case`, published by RWB-P3-E1042-CON (DP-06) | The environment code of the deployment; the parameter code is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0796; ASM-1485) |

The ACE group reference is a read-only SQL read and not a REST call: `recovery.v_ace_iam_group` (DF-ACE-301 to DF-ACE-304), owner RWB-P1-E1069-APP (DP-05), one hop in the same database, declared with its `data_as_of` and its 503. Nothing else is consumed: the reference-data contract of rwb-case is not declared, because this capability reads no list of values, and the load path of RWB-P4-E1037-CON is named as the route of a new version and not declared as an operation here.

###### 12.3 Events published

| Event | Topic | Owner | Contract element |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` | `rwb.decision-record.v1` | PLT library, consumed by P7 | Entry id, decision code `AC-DENY`, reason code `ROLE_CONFLICT`, the two role codes, the conflict version, the environment and the time |

The message uses the CloudEvents 1.0 envelope with the attributes id, source, type, specversion, time, subject and datacontenttype. No message carries a group membership, a user reference, a name, an e-mail address or a case fact. No access event of `rwb.access.events.v1` is declared for a refusal: `rwb.access.AccessPolicyChanged.v1` belongs to the load of a matrix, a masking row or a mapping, `rwb.access.DoaLimitChanged.v1` to the delegation table, and the refusal is a decision record (BR4, ASM-1479, ASM-1482).

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. `rwb-access` is a reference-data owner in Architecture v5 slide 14 (events: none), and this capability adds no subscription.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None. The check and the two reads are synchronous REST answers in the caller's thread with no workflow, no activity and no signal. The six-monthly access review Schedule (JOB-18) is RWB-P4-AD008-CON's.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. Nothing about a pair runs on a clock: the `validFrom` date is a row value the check resolves.

No foreign key crosses a schema, and the contract names no table outside `rwb_access` except the read-only ACE view it consumes.

##### 13. Solution plan

**Deliverables.** `openapi/rwb-access-separation-of-duty-v1.yaml` (OpenAPI 3.1) with the three operations and the shared components, the four schemas, the `contract/error-envelope.yaml` with the agreed message IDs, the record declaration for `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` with its reason code, the declared `conflictVersion` field of the session answer of RWB-P4-E1037-CON, the parameters stub with its owner, the ACE-view stub with its `data_as_of`, and the five WireMock mapping sets.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

A contract story adds no build dependency of its own: each DP above is **referred to; the consuming story carries the dependency**, and that story is RWB-P4-AD005-APP, whose H row carries RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, RWB-PLT-E1042-CON and RWB-PLT-N001-CON and whose C row carries RWB-P3-E1042-CON. DP-03 is contracted as the entry the document declares on `rwb.decision-record.v1`; DP-05 as the statement that the group of a role code is read read-only through the P1 contract and never through a `public` table; DP-06 as the consumed parameters read that answers the environment code; DP-13 as the base of the document; DP-19 as the composite route that serves SCR-43.

**Build steps**

1. OpenAPI 3.1 skeleton with the base path, the security scheme, the error responses and the shared components; schema lint in the pipeline.
2. The three operations and the four schemas of section 11, with the page, the version and the dates.
3. The rule of the answer in the description of the check: the version in force, one version whole, a pair read both ways, the whole set refused and never a part (BR6 to BR8).
4. The refusal statement: no role, no scope and no token on a refusal, MSG-P4-006 to the person, one entry with reason `ROLE_CONFLICT` and its addressee (BR8, BR9).
5. The rights of the check and of the two reads, and the 401 and 403 of the default deny rule (BR10).
6. The one `conflictVersion` field of the session answer, with API-P4-012 named and no operation restated (BR13).
7. The record declaration with its decision code and reason code, and the statement that no access event exists for a refusal (BR4).
8. The error envelope and the message-ID mapping, with the legacy texts copied unchanged and the text of MSG-P4-006 left open.
9. The consumed parameters read and the read-only ACE view with their owners, the one-hop rule, the 2 s budget and the 503 (BR2).
10. The five fakes and the stub fixtures of section 12.8.
11. The eight contract tests; a drift between a fake and the document fails the build.
12. Baseline tag and the consumer sign-off note of the app story and of the sign-in story.

**Feature switch.** The contract carries no switch. The check is an operation of the service and a pair is data with a version; nothing about a refusal is behind a flag.

**Consumer sign-off**

| Consumer | What it accepts |
|---|---|
| RWB-P4-AD005-APP | The three provided operations, the four schemas, the refusal rule, the record type and the five fakes |
| RWB-P4-E1022-CON and RWB-P4-E1022-APP, the sign-in | The check request, the refusal answer and the `conflictVersion` field it answers |
| RWB-P4-E1037-CON, the session read | The one field this document adds to its answer, and the statement that it restates no operation |
| The wave 4 harness | The fakes of 12.8 and the parameters and ACE-view stubs |

The load and the approval route of a new conflict version, and the deprecation window of a published field, are the load path of RWB-P4-E1037-CON and are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0796; ASM-1482).

**Done when.** The OpenAPI document validates in the pipeline, the eight contract tests pass, the five fakes answer every consumed and every provided path, and the app story, the sign-in story and the session contract have accepted the baseline.

| ID | When | Message |

| MSG-P4-001 | No subject reference on the check, no session, or no Workbench role | You have no Recovery Workbench role. Ask your team manager to request one. |
| MSG-P4-002 | A caller without Platform administration R on a read | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P4-003 | A path the document does not publish, or a record outside the caller's scope | This case is not in your scope. |
| MSG-P4-006 | The resolved role set holds both halves of a pair at the conflict version in force | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0796; ASM-1479); the message ID and the two role codes are fixed, the text is not |
| MSG-GEN-001 | A required field of a read is empty or invalid, or a role code of a pair is not an active role row | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-GEN-004 | The version label, the role code or the pair asked for does not exist, or no version or two versions are in force on the date asked | Someone else changed this record. Reload it to see their change. |
| MSG-GEN-006 | The ACE group reference cannot be read | The reference data is not available. Try again later. |
| MSG-P7-003 | The decision-record entry of a refusal could not be written | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |

The message IDs are contract elements; the text is the agreed text, taken from the legacy story where the message already existed. MSG-P4-006 is named by FSD P4 v3 AC-EXC-P4-001-03 and has no text in any source, so this document declares the ID, the pair it names and the refusal it carries, and leaves the text to the business decision: the sibling story RWB-P4-E1022-APP declares a text for the same ID in this run, and the two must agree before the freeze (GAP-0796; ASM-1479).

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in the contract: the pairs, the reasons and the version labels are data rows, the environment is a parameter, and the document fixes names and types only.
- No personal data in a schema, an example or a fake: a pair is two role codes, a refusal carries a subject reference and no name, and a name or an e-mail address in the document fails the review (BR12).
- The contract names only `rwb-access` tables, the read-only ACE view it consumes and operations owned by `rwb-access` or declared as consumed (DP-01, BR5).
- One REST base and one record topic, and no access event and no incident operation invented for a refusal (DP-13, BR3, BR4).
- The refusal is whole and it is recorded: a consumer that reads a partial refusal or a refusal with no entry fails the contract test (BR8, BR9).
- The session answer is touched once: one field, `conflictVersion`, and no operation of RWB-P4-E1037-CON restated (BR13).
- Every example and every fake is synthetic; no production group, person or entitlement is copied into a schema or a fake.
- The error envelope and the CloudEvents envelope come from the platform library; this story narrows them but never redefines them.
