**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: the firm-and-user slice of RWB-AD-022 in rwb-partner. AC2 is kept word for word with its origin tag; the firm is the `partner` row of DF-PRT-001 to DF-PRT-007 and its users are the `partner_user` rows of DF-REF-212 to DF-REF-217, and the day the contract ends a dated pass ends the validity of every live user, so the partner portal refuses them, and sends the `contractEnd` command that closes the panel and recalls the open instructions at `RECALLED` through the branch RWB-S9-E7015-APP owns. No source gives `partner_user` a catalogue entry in TSD S9 T3.1, names the date trigger or a Schedule, or names an event that announces a recall (GAP-3103; ASM-5329, ASM-5330, ASM-5331). Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **partner and agency manager**, I want **every firm held as a panel record with its users and the period each user may sign in, so that the day its contract ends its accounts stop working and the work placed with it is recalled**, so that **partners see only the work placed with their firm and a firm with no contract holds no live work and no live user**.

This story owns:

- the one legacy criterion of RWB-AD-022 that the plan gives it, AC2, copied verbatim with its origin tag;
- the firm as master data: `partner` over DF-PRT-001 to DF-PRT-007, kept by SCR-34 Partner list;
- the firm's users: `partner_user` over DF-REF-212 to DF-REF-217 (`identity_ref`, `partner_id`, `role_code`, `valid_from`, `valid_to`), and the mapping of a partner's sign-in to that row and its firm;
- the dated pass that finds a firm whose `contract_end` has arrived, ends the validity of its live users in one transaction and sends the recall command for the firm;
- the two reads its screens use, SCR-34 Partner list and PRT-01 Partner home, behind the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19) on base `/api/recovery/partner/v1` (DP-13).

It does not own: the exit itself, that is the close of the panel at `EXITED`, the recall of the open instructions, the exit's decision record, the request to rwb-case to re-select and the service-level clock, which are the `contractEnd` branch of RWB-S9-E7015-APP on the same workflow (ASM-5331); the published shapes, the six operations, the rights, the error set and the fakes, which are RWB-S9-AD022-CON; the criterion that a partner sees only its own firm (AC1), which belongs to the partner-portal read story although the scope filter is built here (ASM-5333); issuing, accepting, declining, recording a result and invoicing an instruction; the notice on a missed target; the scorecard and the allocation; the case of record, which is rwb-case; the roles and rights, which are rwb-access; and the deployment, which is the operations story of this key.

##### 2. Business rationale

The objective, the problem and the metric are unchanged from the legacy story and the module FSD: partners were instructed and paid by email and spreadsheet, and a firm whose contract ended left its users able to sign in and its work stranded (FSD S9 A1.3, A2.12.1). The target holds the firm and its users as rows of one service and lets the end of the contract act on both, measured on the decision log and the Workbench records at the monthly target of A2.12.1. What D-RCV-60 changes is who owns the firm, the user, the trigger and the record.

- **The firm is this service's.** `partner`, `partner_instruction` and `partner_user` are S9's three tables in `rwb_partner` (context pack ownership rows), and the panel status, the contract end and the users live in them and nowhere else.
- **A partner user is a period, not a flag.** The module's rows give `partner_user` a `valid_from`, a `valid_to` and a `role_code` (DF-REF-212 to DF-REF-217), so an account is disabled by ending its validity at the contract end and no new status column is invented (ASM-5329).
- **The exit is already one branch.** The close of the panel, the recall to `RECALLED`, the exit record and the case request are the `contractEnd` branch of RWB-S9-E7015-APP under R-UNI-26 and R-UNI-45; this story adds the date trigger and the account effect and duplicates neither (ASM-5331).
- **The end of the contract is a dated rule.** AC2 reads "when the day ends", so the trigger is a date check on `contract_end` and no officer has to remember it; the pass is a Schedule of the service (ASM-5330).
- **Two facts have no source.** `partner_user` has no entry in the TSD S9 T3.1 catalogue (GAP-3103; ASM-5329), and the service's event pair EV-20 `InstructionIssued` and EV-21 `PartnerResultSubmitted` carries neither a recall nor an account change, so nothing is announced (GAP-3103; ASM-5337).

No business value moves: the panel states, the instruction states, the contract date, the right and the target are reference data and rule values, read with their version and never written in code.

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-S9-AD022-CON is published: the `partner` and `partner_instruction` elements, the four lists, the six operations on `/api/recovery/partner/v1`, the rights and the error set.
- `partner` and `partner_user` exist in `rwb_partner` from the DB story of this service, with DF-PRT-001 to DF-PRT-007, the user fields of DF-REF-212 to DF-REF-217 and the standard columns of TSD S9 T3.0. The user fields are not catalogued in TSD S9 T3.1 and are taken from the Logical Data Model (GAP-3103; ASM-5329).
- RWB-P4-E1022-CON is published with its fake: the partner-portal right of the caller and the status of a partner's sign-in, one hop, 2 s (ASM-5332).
- RWB-PLT-N001-CON is published: SCR-34 and PRT-01 reach this service through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19).
- The `contractEnd` branch of RWB-S9-E7015-APP is available on `InstructionWorkflow` and accepts the firm reference and the end date as a command; the branch owns the panel, the recall, the record, the case request and the clock.
- A firm is on the panel at `ACTIVE` or `ON_NOTICE` with a `contract_end` of today and live users whose `valid_to` is open.
- The service runs as its own login on `rwb_partner`, holds no grant on another `rwb_*` schema and no `v_ace_*` grant, so a statement on `rwb_case` or an ACE view is refused and fails the boundary test.
- No approval is needed to build against a Draft contract baseline.

##### 4. Flow

1. The firm is kept as master data on SCR-34: code, registered name, type, panel status, contract end and latest score (DF-PRT-001 to DF-PRT-007); the panel, the fees and the service levels are reference data with their version (FEAT-PRM-02, BR-S9-012).
2. Each user of a firm is a `partner_user` row with its `identity_ref`, its `partner_id`, its `role_code` and the `valid_from` and `valid_to` of the period it may sign in (DF-REF-212 to DF-REF-217); the manager sets the period and a partner never extends its own.
3. A partner signs in through the partner gateway, the service maps the token subject to its `partner_user` row, and the request is refused at 403 with MSG-P4-002 when the row is unknown or its validity has ended (X3).
4. The dated pass runs daily at 00:05 on the Temporal Schedule `rwb-partner-contract-end` on task queue `rwb-partner` in namespace `rwb-recovery` (target design; ASM-5330).
5. The pass selects every firm whose `contract_end` is today or earlier and that still holds a user whose `valid_to` is open or null; a firm already wholly closed is skipped, so a second run of the same day changes nothing.
6. `AccountEndDecisionRecordWriter` writes one record per firm before any change: the firm, the contract end, the users whose validity ends, the rule version in force and the trigger (ASM-5331; R-UNI-39).
7. `endAccountValidity` writes in one transaction, per firm: `valid_to` of every live user set to the contract end, and the audit columns; no other column of `partner_user` moves and no row is deleted.
8. The pass then sends the `contractEnd` command for the firm on `InstructionWorkflow`: the same command the manager's act sends, which closes `panel_status` at `EXITED`, recalls the open instructions at `RECALLED`, records the exit, asks rwb-case to re-select each case and starts the service-level clock, all of it RWB-S9-E7015-APP's.
9. After the commit SCR-34 shows the firm at `EXITED` with its users closed, PRT-01 shows the recalled instructions and a partner call with an ended validity is refused (X3).
10. No event is published and no second topic is used: the account change and the recall are rows and records, and the owning services read them on the read surfaces (GAP-3103; ASM-5337).

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The account record cannot be written for a firm | That firm's users keep their validity and the command is not sent; nothing else changes | MSG-P7-003 | AC2, TC-AD-022-02 |
| X2 | The caller does not hold the partner-portal right of the operation | 403 before any read or write | MSG-P4-002 | TC-AD-022-03 |
| X3 | The partner account is unknown, or its `valid_to` has passed | 403; no firm, instruction or fee is returned | MSG-P4-002 | TC-S9-AD022-APP-03 |
| X4 | An instruction is asked for by a caller of another firm | 404; the scope comes from the user's row, never from a parameter | None | §17, BR7 |
| X5 | The Schedule fires twice, overlaps or re-runs after a failure | One pass per firm per day: a closed firm is skipped and a half-written firm is retried whole | None | AC2, TC-S9-AD022-APP-01 |
| X6 | The rwb-access read or the command to the exit branch does not answer inside 2 s | The account rows stand as committed, the command is retried on the workflow's own schedule, and the caller sees 503 | None | §13 |
| X7 | The firm has live users and no open instruction, or the reverse | Each side acts on what exists and no error is raised | None | AC2 |
| X8 | A statement reaches a `v_ace_*` view, a `recovery_case` row or another schema | The grant refuses it and the boundary test fails the build | None (pipeline log) | §17, BR9 |

X1 is the legacy exception flow of FSD S9 A2.12.4.3 and X2 the legacy right check; X3 to X8 are the paths the portal, the Schedule, the shared branch and the schema boundary add.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Starts on Day 1 against RWB-S9-AD022-CON, the rwb-access fake, the decision-record stub and the exit branch's command surface, on its own schema, with no live P3 or P4 |
| Negotiable | The clock time, the activity names and the pass's internal shape are this story's design; the criterion, the base, the lists, the rights and the screens are fixed |
| Valuable | A firm whose contract ends has no user able to sign in the next morning and its work is recalled, with the change on the record |
| Estimable | One scheduled pass, one transaction over the users, one record write, one command and two read surfaces |
| Small | Finished inside two weeks with its tests on the fakes |
| Testable | Each path runs on a synthetic firm with a contract end of today, on the fakes, with the clock controlled |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Partner firms and partner users

  Scenario: AC2 Contract ends (legacy RWB-AD-022 AC2)
    Given the rwb-access contract mock returns the partner portal right R
    Given a firm whose contract ends today
    When the day ends
    Then the system disables its user accounts and open instructions are recalled
```

AC2 is the legacy criterion word for word, with its origin tag added and nothing else changed: "a firm whose contract ends today", "the day ends" and "the system disables its user accounts and open instructions are recalled" all stand. Its cross-service part is the caller's right, so AC2 carries the one `Given the rwb-access contract mock returns the partner portal right R` line and that is the only addition. The outcome is the same as FSD S9 AC-S9-012-01, written one epic ahead: the accounts are disabled by ending their validity, and the recall is the `RECALLED` status the exit branch writes on the instructions of that firm (ASM-5331).

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The firm and its users are `rwb_partner`'s rows and no statement leaves the schema; `partner_id` and `case_id` are identifiers of another row or another service's fact, not foreign keys across schemas | DP-01; TSD S9 T3.3 |
| BR2 | No value a business person may change is written in code: the panel states, the instruction states, the types, the contract end and the right are read with their version | BR-S9-012; FSD S9 A2.12.3.1; legacy Guardrails |
| BR3 | An account is disabled by ending its validity: `valid_to` is set to the firm's `contract_end`, and no row is deleted and no status column is invented | AC2; DF-REF-217; ASM-5329 |
| BR4 | The pass acts on the firm whose `contract_end` is today or earlier and skips a firm already closed; a second run of the same day changes nothing | AC2; X5 |
| BR5 | The record is written before the change, one per firm per pass, with the rule version in force; a failed write leaves the users as they were and sends no command | DP-03; R-UNI-39; FSD S9 A2.12.4.3 |
| BR6 | The exit is the branch of RWB-S9-E7015-APP: this pass sends the `contractEnd` command and writes no `panel_status`, no instruction status and no case request of its own | ASM-5331; R-UNI-26, R-UNI-45 |
| BR7 | The scope of every portal read is the firm of the caller's `partner_user` row; a request parameter never widens it | AC1 read surface; ASM-5333 |
| BR8 | No personal data in a row, a log or a workflow input: the user is an `identity_ref`, a firm and a role, and no name, e-mail, phone number or identity number is copied from the partner | Template and Rules §R7.2 (s17); TSD S9 T6.2 |
| BR9 | One base, one topic, one queue, one schema and one login per service; no `v_ace_*` grant and no grant on another `rwb_*` schema | DP-13, DP-14; Template and Rules §R4; ASM-5332 |
| BR10 | No event is published by this pass: neither a recall nor an account change is in the service's event pair | TSD S9 T5.3; GAP-3103; ASM-5337 |

The lists this story reads, copied from TSD S9 T3.2 and published unchanged:

| List | Values | Use here |
|---|---|---|
| LOV-PANEL | `ACTIVE`, `ON_NOTICE`, `SUSPENDED`, `EXITED` | The panel status shown on SCR-34 and read by the pass |
| LOV-INSTR-STATUS | `SENT`, `ACCEPTED`, `DECLINED`, `IN_PROGRESS`, `DONE`, `RECALLED` | Read only, to show on PRT-01 which instruction is recalled |
| LOV-INSTRUCTION | `COLLECT`, `FILE_SUIT`, `ENFORCE`, `APPRAISE`, `REPOSSESS`, `LIST`, `SELL` | Read only, to show the instruction as placed |
| LOV-PARTNER-TYPE | `AGENCY`, `LAW_FIRM`, `VALUER`, `AUCTION_VENDOR`, `BROKER`, `DEBT_BUYER`, `AMC`, `RAMC` | Read only, to show the firm and its users |

##### 9. State transitions

The account, as this story writes it:

| From | Event | Condition | To | Written by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `valid_to` open or null | The contract-end pass | The firm's `contract_end` is today or earlier | `valid_to` = the contract end | rwb-partner, this story |
| `valid_to` = the contract end | The pass again on the same or a later day | Any | Unchanged | none; the firm is skipped (X5) |
| `valid_to` in the future | A new contract or an extension | The manager sets a new period | A new `valid_to` | the manager's edit on SCR-34, not this pass |
| `valid_to` passed | A sign-in | Any | Refused at 403 with MSG-P4-002 | the portal check (X3) |

The firm and the instruction, as the pass reads them and the exit branch writes them:

| From (`panel_status`) | Event | Condition | To | Written by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ACTIVE`, `ON_NOTICE`, `SUSPENDED` | The `contractEnd` command | The end date has arrived | `EXITED` | RWB-S9-E7015-APP's branch, on R-UNI-26 |
| `SENT`, `ACCEPTED`, `IN_PROGRESS` | The `contractEnd` command | The firm exits | `RECALLED` | RWB-S9-E7015-APP's branch |
| `DECLINED`, `DONE`, `RECALLED` | The `contractEnd` command | The firm exits | Unchanged | none |

The panel and instruction states are the lists of TSD S9 T3.2 and this story moves none of them: it moves the validity of the accounts and sends the one command that moves the other two.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| RW-AGENCYMG, partner and agency manager | CRUDA: the primary role of FSD S9 A2.12.3.3, keeping the firm, setting the users' periods and reading the recall |
| RW-HEADLIT, RW-HEADNPA, RW-HEADASL | RA: the also-uses roles of FSD S9 A2.12.3.3 |
| RW-LITOFF, RW-ENFORCE, RW-SALEOFF, RW-NPAMGR, RW-DEBTSALE, RW-GUARANT | CRU: read the firm and its instructions and hold the work they placed |
| RW-CASEOWN, RW-TEAMMGR, RW-LEGAL, RW-CONDUCT, RW-CAPACITY, RW-PRODHEAD, RW-RISK, RW-COE, RW-AUDIT, RW-COMPLY, RW-PLATADM, RW-BIANAL, RW-TRIBE | R: read only, in scope, refused the user edit |
| PT-AGENCY, PT-LAWFIRM, PT-VALUER, PT-AUCTION, PT-BUYER, PT-RAMC | RU: partner users, scoped to their own firm, refused the user edit and the pass |
| rwb-partner service identity | Runs the pass, reads the right, writes the record and the validity, sends the command and serves the two reads; no grant on another schema and no `v_ace_*` grant |

The rights are the rows of TSD S9 T6.1 and nothing wider: the legacy table names eight roles and "21 more", and T6.1 resolves them to the 23 `RW-*` and 6 `PT-*` identities above, which are 29 and agree with the legacy count. DP-08 is not in the pattern set: the right is declared per operation and arrives on RWB-P4-E1022-CON, and the guard is a template capability (ASM-5332).

##### 11. Data

| BR Field ID | Entity (owner) | Field | Read or write |
|---|---|---|---|
| DF-PRT-001 | partner (S9, `rwb_partner`) | id | Read and write, the firm the users cite |
| DF-PRT-002 | partner (S9, `rwb_partner`) | partner_code | Read and write, the business key |
| DF-PRT-003 | partner (S9, `rwb_partner`) | partner_name | Read and write, the registered name |
| DF-PRT-004 | partner (S9, `rwb_partner`) | partner_type | Read and write over LOV-PARTNER-TYPE |
| DF-PRT-005 | partner (S9, `rwb_partner`) | panel_status | Read only here; written by the exit branch (BR6) |
| DF-PRT-006 | partner (S9, `rwb_partner`) | contract_end | Read, the date the pass tests |
| DF-PRT-007 | partner (S9, `rwb_partner`) | score | Read only, shown on SCR-34 |
| DF-REF-212 | partner_user (S9, `rwb_partner`) | identity_ref | Read, the sign-in mapped to this row; no name or contact value |
| DF-REF-213 | partner_user (S9, `rwb_partner`) | partner_id | Read, the firm that scopes the account |
| DF-REF-214 | partner_user (S9, `rwb_partner`) | role_code | Read, the partner role the account holds |
| DF-REF-215 | partner_user (S9, `rwb_partner`) | valid_from | Read, the start of the period |
| DF-REF-216 to DF-REF-217 | partner_user (S9, `rwb_partner`) | valid_to | Write, the end of the period this pass sets to the contract end |
| DF-PRT-008 to DF-PRT-016 | partner_instruction (S9, `rwb_partner`) | id, case_id, partner_id, instruction_type, instructed_at, due_at, status, result_code, fee_amount | Read only here, to show the recalled instruction on PRT-01 |
| DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018 | decision record (PLT library, in `rwb_partner`) | rule id, rule version, decision code, inputs, from and to state, decided at | Write through the library, before the validity changes |
| DF-CAS-001 to DF-CAS-023 | recovery_case (P3) | id, case_no, status, stage_code and 20 more | Not read as a table and not written: the exit branch commands the case |
| every `v_ace_*` view | ACE (P1) | Any | Not read: no `v_ace_*` grant, and DP-05 is a prohibition (ASM-5332) |

The firm's fields are those of TSD S9 T3.1 and the Logical Data Model; the user's fields are DF-REF-212 to DF-REF-217 of the Logical Data Model, because TSD S9 T3.1 catalogues the firm and the instruction and not the user (GAP-3103; ASM-5329). **No new table, no new column and no migration** is declared: the three tables arrive with the DB story of this service, and `decision_record`, `idempotency_key` and `outbox_event` are library objects created in `rwb_partner` by the library's migration (DP-03).

**No personal data.** The rows carry a firm, codes, dates, a list value and an identity reference. The partner user is a key, a firm, a role and a period, never a name: no e-mail, phone number, address or identity number is read into a row, an answer, a log or a workflow input, and every fixture is synthetic.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner rwb-partner (S9); base `/api/recovery/partner/v1` (DP-13). This story supplies the two reads its screens use; the four mutations of the same baseline are built by the instruction stories.

| Method | Path | Documented shape | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/partners` (API-S9-001) | Query `type`, `status`; `Partner[]` out with the panel status and the score | Partner portal, right R, scope applied | Not applicable |
| GET | `/partner/instructions` (API-S9-003) | Query `status`, `page`, `size`; `InstructionPage` out for the caller's firm | Partner portal, right R, scope applied | Not applicable |

The answers 401, 403 with MSG-P4-002 and 503 are the published error sets of TSD S9 T-A.2 for the two operations. The user edit and the contract-end pass have no published operation: the ownership rows give the service six operations and none of them maintains a user or ends a contract, so the account effect is read through `GET /partners` and the recall through `GET /partner/instructions` (GAP-3103; ASM-5329).

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| The partner-portal right and identity read (operation Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3103; ASM-5332)) | `/api/recovery/access/v1` | P4 rwb-access | The right of the caller per operation and the status of the partner's sign-in, once per request and once per pass; faked |

The row is one hop with a 2 s timeout and a breaker (ADR-020), and it is the contract dependency RWB-P4-E1022-CON of the metadata table. No read of rwb-case is declared: the case reference arrives on the instruction row as an identifier, and the re-selection is the exit branch's command (ASM-5331).

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The service publishes on `rwb.partner.events.v1` (DP-14) and its set carries EV-20 `InstructionIssued` and EV-21 `PartnerResultSubmitted`, both belonging to the instruction stories (TSD S9 T5.3; context pack events). Neither announces an account ending or a recall, so this story declares no event, no producer group and no outbox row, and the absence test fails a build that adds one (GAP-3103; ASM-5337).

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. Work arrives as a row placed through API-S9-002 and the pass is date-driven, so this story holds no consumer group, no subscription and no inbox row. FSD S9 A2.12.4.4 declares no background event for the feature, which is the conflict recorded for the date trigger (GAP-3103; ASM-5330).

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Contract element |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb-partner-contract-end` pass | Schedule-started workflow execution, one per run, one child per firm | `rwb-partner` in namespace `rwb-recovery` | Input: the business date; outcome: the firms with users closed and the commands sent |
| `sweepContractEnd` | Activity, the selection of firms and their live users | `rwb-partner` | The business date in; the firms with their users and their contract end out |
| `endAccountValidity` | Activity, the record and the one transaction of a firm | `rwb-partner` | The firm, the users and the end date in; the record reference and the count out, record first |
| `InstructionWorkflow` | Workflow, one per firm, owned by RWB-S9-E7015-APP | `rwb-partner` | The `contractEnd` command with the firm reference and the end date; the panel, the recall, the case request and the clock are its branch's |

`InstructionWorkflow` is the one workflow in the context pack's ownership rows for this service, and the pass with its two activities is the service's dated step, a target design name. This story sends the command and changes no signal of the workflow; `CaseWorkflow` stays with rwb-case.

###### 12.6 Schedules

| Name | Schedule | Task queue | What it starts |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb-partner-contract-end` | Daily at 00:05, business calendar, overlap skipped, catch-up once | `rwb-partner` in namespace `rwb-recovery` | The contract-end pass, one run per business date |

The service owns no Quartz job and no shared job table (context pack, Jobs: None), and Temporal Schedules replace Quartz (ADR-016). No source names a Schedule, a clock time or an overlap rule for this pass and FSD S9 A2.12.4.4 declares no background event, so the name, the time and the catch-up rule are a target design and the absence of DP-10 and of RWB-PLT-E1071-CON from the pattern and build rows is recorded (GAP-3103; ASM-5330).

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Note |
|---|---|---|
| partner | S9 (`rwb_partner`) | The firm, its panel status and its contract end; this story reads it and writes no status |
| partner_user | S9 (`rwb_partner`) | The firm's users and their periods; this story writes `valid_to` and the audit columns |
| partner_instruction | S9 (`rwb_partner`) | The work placed with a firm; this story reads the recalled status and writes none |
| decision_record | PLT library, in `rwb_partner` | The local hash-linked record of the pass (DP-03) |
| idempotency_key | PLT library, in `rwb_partner` | The keys of the instruction operations; the pass uses none |
| outbox_event | PLT library, in `rwb_partner` | Present as a library object; this pass writes no row (§12.3) |

Not owned and never read as a table: `recovery_case` (P3), every `v_ace_*` view (P1), `decision_log_entry` (P7), `document` (P5), `notice` (P6), `payment` (P8). No foreign key leaves the schema (DP-01).

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Documented answer | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| rwb-access right and identity fake (`RWB-P4-E1022-CON`) | The partner-portal right per operation and a partner sign-in whose validity is live, open or ended | AC2, X1, X2, X3 |
| Local decision-record library stub (`RWB-PLT-E1027-CON`) | A healthy chain and outbox, and a stopped chain | AC2, X1 |
| gateway-bff composite route fake | The merged SCR-34 and PRT-01 answers for a firm before and after its exit | AC2, X5 |
| `contractEnd` command fake of the exit branch | The command accepted, the panel returned at `EXITED` and the instruction set at `RECALLED` | AC2, X7 |
| Clock fake for the Schedule | A business date before, on and after `contract_end` | AC2, X5 |

The fakes are test-only and are replaced by the real services in SIT; the operation name of the rwb-access read carries the placeholder until its owner confirms it (GAP-3103; ASM-5332).

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Count | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| REST | 2 provided, 1 consumed | API-S9-001 and API-S9-003 on `/api/recovery/partner/v1`; the rwb-access read; one hop, 2 s |
| Kafka | 0 published, 0 consumed | EV-20 and EV-21 belong to the instruction stories; the pass announces nothing |
| Temporal | 1 Schedule, 2 activities, 1 command | `rwb-partner-contract-end`, `sweepContractEnd`, `endAccountValidity`, and the `contractEnd` command to `InstructionWorkflow` |
| File | None | No file is read, built or delivered; the partner portal of INT-24 is screen traffic |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.partner`, module `firm`; front end `src/modules/recovery/partner/PartnerList.tsx` and `PartnerHome.tsx`.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-05 is applied as a prohibition: this service holds no `AceSourceQuery` and no `v_ace_*` grant, and a case or account reference arrives on the instruction request, so no view is read and no dependency is added. DP-13 moves the two legacy paths to the partner base. DP-19 is how SCR-34 and PRT-01 reach this service, one hop through the gateway. These three are the whole pattern set: DP-10 for the dated pass, DP-08 for the guard and DP-09 for an event are not in it, and their absence is recorded rather than added to the metadata table (GAP-3103; ASM-5330, ASM-5332, ASM-5337).

**Dependencies the tables add and the plan does not hold.** The pattern table adds `RWB-PLT-N001-CON` for DP-19, which the plan's H row carries. It does not carry `RWB-PLT-E1071-CON` for the Schedule of DP-10 or `RWB-PLT-TE006-CON` for the outbox of DP-09, and it does not carry the in-lane story RWB-S9-E7015-APP whose branch this pass commands; all three are recorded as absent from the metadata rows (ASM-5330, ASM-5331).

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| `ContractEndPass` | Workflow | Runs once per business date, one child per firm, and reports the counts |
| `sweepContractEnd` | Activity | Selects the firms due to exit with their live users |
| `endAccountValidity` | Activity | Writes the record and the user periods in one transaction, then sends the command |
| `PartnerAccountGuard` | Service | Maps the caller to its `partner_user` row and firm, refuses an unknown or expired account and reads the right |
| `AccessRightClient` | Client | The rwb-access right and identity read, one hop, 2 s, breaker |
| `PartnerController`, `PartnerList`, `PartnerHome` | Controller and React components | `GET /partners` and `GET /partner/instructions` with the scope and the problem mapping, and the two screen fragments |

**Database and migrations.** No Flyway file: `partner`, `partner_user` and `partner_instruction` arrive with the DB story of this service, and the record is a library object created in `rwb_partner` by the library's migration (DP-03).

**Configuration and reference data.** The panel and instruction states and the partners' types are reference data with their version (BR2); the capability area "Partner portal" and its rights are access rows of rwb-access; the 00:05 clock, the overlap rule and the catch-up rule are service configuration, not constants (ASM-5330).

**Build steps**

1. `sweepContractEnd` against the clock fake, with the firm selection and the already-closed skip (AC2, X5, X7).
2. The record writer against the stub and `endAccountValidity` as one transaction over the users' `valid_to` (AC2, X1).
3. The `contractEnd` command with its retry and its 2 s budget, and the idempotent repeat (AC2, X5, X6).
4. `PartnerAccountGuard` and `AccessRightClient` against the fakes, with the unknown, expired and wrong-right paths (X2, X3).
5. `PartnerController` and the two screen fragments through the composite route fake, with the scope and the paging (§15).
6. The boundary test: no statement outside `rwb_partner`, no `v_ace_*` read, no case write, no panel or instruction write and no outbox row (X8, BR6, BR9, BR10).

**Feature flag.** `rwb.partner.contract-end-v1`, a flag of the platform library; off means the pass does not run and the users keep their periods, and the two reads are unaffected.

**Done when.** The tests of section 16 pass, a synthetic firm with a contract end of today has every live user closed and its work recalled in SIT, a second run of the same day changes nothing and writes no second record, a forced record failure leaves the users open and sends no command, an expired account is refused at 403, no `v_ace_*` read, no case write and no panel write exists in the build, and SCR-34 and PRT-01 answer through the composite route.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-GEN-001 | A required field of a request is absent or invalid: a code, a name, a type or a panel status (VR-S9-012-1) | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-P4-002 | The role lacks the partner-portal right, or the partner account is unknown or its validity has ended (X2, X3) | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P7-003 | The decision record cannot be written before the pass changes anything (X1) | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |

The three IDs are those of the legacy and FSD sets; the text is copied unchanged, no message is reworded and no new one is added. MSG-P4-002 is the legacy partner-portal message, MSG-GEN-001 is VR-S9-012-1, and MSG-P7-003 is AC-EXC-S9-012-02 of FSD S9 A2.12.4.3.

##### 15. Screens and states

SCR-34 Partner list holds the firms, their contracts, their panel status, their users and their scores, and PRT-01 Partner home holds the partner's own open instructions, due dates and messages (FSD S9 Screens; legacy table: SCR-34 "Loading; list", PRT-01 "Loading; list"). This story produces the pass's two visible results: SCR-34 shows the firm at `EXITED` with its users closed, and PRT-01 shows the recalled instructions with their due dates kept. Both are reached through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19), and a partner outside the bank arrives on the partner gateway of FAPI 2.0 (Arch v5 slide 8; INT-24).

No screen is described for the pass and FSD S9 A2.12.4.4 declares no background event, so the place and the time of the trigger are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3103; ASM-5330). The refusal, expired-account, already-closed and not-recorded states read the messages of section 14 on the same route.

| TC ID | Covers | Level | Data |
|---|---|---|---|
| TC-AD-022-01 | Firm scope | Component | A partner user of one firm and the instruction read; only that firm's instructions return and the scope comes from the user's row |
| TC-AD-022-02 | AC2 | Component | A firm with a contract end of today and two live users with open validity; every `valid_to` set, the command sent, the panel and the recall read back |
| TC-AD-022-03 | Access | Component | A role without the partner-portal right and an account whose validity has ended; 403 with MSG-P4-002 and no read |
| TC-S9-AD022-APP-01 | AC2, X5 | Component | The same pass twice on one business date; one record, one command and no second change |

The three legacy cases are those of RWB-AD-022 in their legacy order, with the Level column added: every case runs on the fakes and against this service's own rows, so every case is `Component`. TC-AD-022-01 exercises the firm-scope filter this story builds; the criterion it was written for, AC1, belongs to the partner-portal read story (ASM-5333). The three cases `TC-S9-AD022-APP-01` to `-03` are new. The full test is in Recovery Workbench Test Cases v7.xlsx, tab Story test cases, under the same ID; no `-ITG` copy is written by this story, and the cross-service journey belongs to the wave 4 harness.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the panel and instruction states, the types, the contract end, the right and the target stay reference data and rule rows, never a constant, a default or a branch.
- No personal data in a row, a workflow input or a log: a firm, codes, dates, a list value and an `identity_ref` only, and every fixture is synthetic.
- ACE data only through the owner's contract or `v_ace_*` views, and this service holds no `v_ace_*` grant at all (DP-05).
- The case stays with rwb-case: no `recovery_case` row and no case state is written here (ASM-5331).
- The firm and the instruction stay with their owner: this pass writes no `panel_status` and no instruction `status`; those are the exit branch's writes (BR6).
- One base, one topic, one queue, one schema and one login per service (DP-13, DP-14).
- No event, topic, consumer or outbox row is added by this pass; a build that publishes an account change or a recall fails the absence test (BR10).
- The record is written before the rows; a build that answers outside the record's transaction fails the review (DP-03).

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-AD-022 as the wave 4 integration proof that a partner user opening the partner portal sees only the instructions placed with that user's firm, that the firm and the user are resolved from rwb-partner and never from a client parameter or a copy in rwb-access, and that a missing right or another firm's identifier returns nothing; the build of the partner firms, the partner users, the instructions and the portal is RWB-S9-AD022-APP. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **QA integration engineer**, I want **the end-to-end proof that a partner user opening the partner portal sees only the instructions placed with that user's firm, that the firm and the partner user are resolved from rwb-partner and never from a client parameter or a copy in rwb-access, and that a missing right or a cross-firm identifier returns nothing**, so that **partners see only the work placed with their firm, on the internal list and on the portal alike**.

This story builds the harness and the evidence, and nothing else. S9 rwb-partner owns the partner firm, the partner user, the partner instruction, the recorded results and the panel, and it answers the staff side with `GET /api/recovery/partner/v1/partners`, `POST /api/recovery/partner/v1/cases/{caseId}/instructions` and the instruction reads of Arch v5 slide 17, and the partner side with `GET /api/recovery/partner/v1/partner/instructions`, `POST /api/recovery/partner/v1/partner/instructions/{instructionId}/accept` and `POST /api/recovery/partner/v1/partner/instructions/{instructionId}/results`. The partner gateway in the DMZ, with the second factor and the FAPI 2.0 profile, is the only route into the portal and fronts rwb-partner. P4 rwb-access answers the internal session, the internal role and the Partner portal R right, and holds no partner user at all, because the Ownership Map ruling ASM-0072 keeps partner users with S9 and leaves P4 the internal role model only. The partner data room is S6's operation, `GET /api/recovery/debtsale/v1/partner/data-room/{lotId}`, and is out of scope here.

The harness therefore drives the two sign-ins, reads the partner list and the portal instruction list through S9's own operations, reads the session through P4's operation, and asserts a refusal by its status and its message. It builds no endpoint, no table, no workflow, no activity, no schedule and no screen, and it writes no code in any service, no row in any schema and no partner, instruction or user state. Where the internal list and the portal would be composed for a screen the path is the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19), every path is the owner's own base `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` (DP-13), and no service reads another service's tables (DP-05).

##### 2. Business rationale

The legacy story RWB-AD-022 holds partner firms, their contracts and their panel status as data, requests one partner user per firm, and then states the whole point in one line: a partner sees only the work placed with that firm. The failure it is written against is quiet rather than loud — a law firm user who opens the portal and finds the instructions of another firm has been shown a case, a debtor and a piece of litigation strategy that the bank has no basis to disclose, and nothing in the ledger would ever record that the disclosure happened. The Ownership Map moves the source of every fact and none of the behaviour: the firm, the partner user, the instruction and the panel stay with S9 rwb-partner in `rwb_partner` (Arch v5 slides 17 and 41), the internal identity, the internal role and the rights stay with P4 rwb-access in `rwb_access` (Arch v5 slide 41), and the portal stays behind the partner gateway in the DMZ with a second factor and the FAPI 2.0 profile (Arch v5 slides 8, 20 and 41; ADR-019).

The split matters because firm scope is a fact about two services and one sign-in, and it is exactly the fact that a copy destroys. If rwb-access kept a partner user row, or if the firm were taken from a parameter the caller sends, the portal's idea of the firm and rwb-partner's idea of the firm could disagree, and the day they disagree is the day one firm's work is shown to another. That is why the Ownership Map ruling on `partner_user` (ASM-0072) is a rule of this story and not a filing decision: the partner user and its firm are resolved from rwb-partner, one owner, and the internal session is answered by rwb-access with the internal role only. Asserted inside one service this passes while the next component quietly reads a second copy; asserted across the two owners it fails the moment the copy exists.

The story owns the legacy AC1 (firm scope) and the cross-service criteria that no single slice can prove. Legacy AC2 — a firm whose contract ends today has its user accounts disabled and its open instructions recalled — is the S9 slice's and is not restated here: its expiry is `partner_user.valid_to` against the firm's `contract_end` and the recall is the instruction lifecycle, both inside rwb-partner, and RWB-S9-AD022-APP asserts them. What this story adds is the boundary: the firm is resolved from the partner user, a client-supplied firm is refused or ignored, another firm's identifier answers nothing, a caller without Partner portal R is refused with the right message, rwb-access holds no partner user, and every portal call is one hop on the partner base with a 2 s budget.

Decoupling follows the target. The partner and the instruction are read on `/api/recovery/partner/v1` and never from `rwb_partner`; the session and the right are read on `/api/recovery/access/v1` and never from `rwb_access`; the portal route is the partner gateway and, where a staff screen composes the same answers, the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19). No view is opened and no schema is queried by the harness, which is DP-05 applied as the rule that no service reads another service's tables: S9 answers the firm and the user, P4 answers the internal role, and neither reads the other's rows. The route specification of the portal, the name of the firm-scope field and the shape of the partner session are not fixed by any source read for this story, and that is carried as one gap and one assumption: GAP-0442 and ASM-0634.

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-S9-AD022-APP and RWB-P4-E1022-APP are the two I stories of this harness, and a stub generated from each published contract answers from Day 1, so the lane never waits: until an I story lands its stub answers and the run is reported as a stub pass.
- The published contract of S9 rwb-partner is in the contract registry: the partner read, the portal instruction read, the accept and the results operations, the staff instruction operation and the two events of `rwb.partner.events.v1`.
- The published contract of P4 rwb-access is in the contract registry: `GET /api/recovery/access/v1/me/session` answers the caller's roles and rights, and the access contract publishes no partner-user read, because partner users are S9's (ASM-0072).
- The partner gateway in the DMZ is available in front of rwb-partner, with the second factor and the FAPI 2.0 profile, and it is the only route the partner identity uses (Arch v5 slides 8, 20 and 41; ADR-019).
- The harness runs in SIT, against the stubs and then against the owners as the two I stories land, and never against UAT or production.
- The two synthetic firms, their panel status and contracts, the two synthetic partner users and the two synthetic instructions are held in the fixture as data. No production data is read, copied or connected to, and no real partner identity is used.
- The portal route specification, the name of the firm-scope field on the portal read, the shape of the partner session and MFA assertion, the partner_user field set as it is published, and the answer a cross-firm identifier receives (with any message for it): Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0442; ASM-0634).
- The permission matrix in force in SIT holds Partner portal R for RW-NPAMGR, RW-DEBTSALE, RW-LEGAL, RW-LITOFF, RW-ENFORCE, RW-CASEOWN, RW-TEAMMGR and RW-SALEOFF, and does not hold it for RW-OFF, which is the refused caller of AC4.
- The release date 28 February 2027 is tentative and is copied unchanged.
- No build dependency. Day 1, with both stubs in place from the first run.

##### 4. Flow

1. Harness: loads the fixture: firm `LAW-A` and firm `LAW-B`, each with its partner_code, partner_type, panel_status and contract_end; partner user `PU-SYN-LAW-A-01` bound to `LAW-A` and partner user `PU-SYN-LAW-B-01` bound to `LAW-B`, each with its identity_ref, role_code, valid_from and valid_to; instruction `INS-SYN-LAW-A-01` placed with `LAW-A` on case `RW-2027-001101` and instruction `INS-SYN-LAW-B-01` placed with `LAW-B` on case `RW-2027-001102`, each with its instruction_type, instructed_at, due_at and status; business date `2027-02-28`. It takes a snapshot of both instruction lists before it reads anything. On Day 1 the stubs of §12.8 return the same records.
2. PartnerSignIn: signs `PU-SYN-LAW-A-01` in through the partner gateway in the DMZ with a second factor, and asserts that the call is answered on the portal route with the FAPI 2.0 profile and that no owner is reached before the second factor is presented (AC1, AC6).
3. SessionProbe: calls `GET /api/recovery/access/v1/me/session` on the P4 base with the partner user's portal session and asserts the internal role answer and the Partner portal R right, and that the answer holds no partner user and no firm (AC5).
4. AccessProbe: asserts that rwb-access holds no partner user: the session answer carries no partner user id and no firm id, the access contract publishes no partner-user read, and the only answer that names the firm or the user is S9's; a partner user row is never read from `rwb_access` (AC5, X7).
5. FirmScopeProbe: reads `GET /api/recovery/partner/v1/partners` as the `LAW-A` user and asserts exactly one firm, `LAW-A`, with its partner_code, partner_type, panel_status and contract_end (AC1, AC2).
6. InstructionProbe: reads `GET /api/recovery/partner/v1/partner/instructions` as the same user and asserts exactly one instruction, `INS-SYN-LAW-A-01`, with its instruction_type, instructed_at, due_at and status, and that `INS-SYN-LAW-B-01` is not in the answer (AC1, AC2).
7. FirmScopeProbe: repeats the instruction read with firm `LAW-B` carried in a client parameter of the kind the legacy portal accepted, and asserts the parameter is refused or ignored and the answer still holds only the instruction of `LAW-A`; the report records which of the two it was (AC2, X6).
8. FirmScopeProbe: calls `POST /api/recovery/partner/v1/partner/instructions/INS-SYN-LAW-B-01/accept` as the `LAW-A` user, and asserts the answer is 404 and carries no instruction detail of `LAW-B`, that `LAW-B`'s instruction and its own are both unchanged, and that the list re-read is identical to the snapshot (AC3, X3). The accept of the user's own instruction is not taken, because this story changes no instruction state.
9. Refused caller: signs in a synthetic RW-OFF caller that does not hold Partner portal R, calls `GET /api/recovery/partner/v1/partner/instructions`, and asserts 403 with MSG-P4-002 and no instruction in the answer (AC4, X4).
10. Hop check: from the recorded call set, asserts that every call is one hop on `/api/recovery/partner/v1` or on `/api/recovery/access/v1` with a 2 s budget and a breaker per downstream, that no call passes through a second service, and that no service's table is read at any point (AC6, X10).
11. EvidenceReport: writes one report keyed by story and partner user, naming the contract version of each hop, whether the hop was a stub or the owner, the two firms, the two instructions, the panel status and contract of the firm read, the refusal status and message, and the verdict of each of the six criteria.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What the harness asserts | Message | ITG test case |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A stub answers a shape the published contract does not allow | The run fails at that hop and the report names the service, the operation and the contract version; no criterion is marked passed | None | TC-AD-022-01-ITG (ITG AC1) |
| X2 | The partner gateway answers the sign-in with no session | The run fails on AC1 and AC6 and the report names the gateway route, the second-factor assertion and the answer; no owner is called and no instruction is read | None, and no business message is specified for it | TC-AD-022-01-ITG (ITG AC6) |
| X3 | `LAW-A`'s user calls the identifier of `LAW-B`'s instruction and the answer carries instruction detail, or is not a 404 | The run fails on AC3 and the report names the caller's firm, the instruction identifier and the fields the answer carried; a 200 with an empty body is a failure too, because it confirms the identifier exists | None, and no cross-firm message is specified (GAP-0442; ASM-0634) | TC-AD-022-02-ITG (ITG AC3) |
| X4 | A caller without Partner portal R is allowed to read the instruction list | The run fails on AC4 and the report names the caller role, the right, the operation and the answer; a 200 is a failure even when the answer is empty | MSG-P4-002 (expected, and missing) | TC-AD-022-03-ITG (ITG AC4) |
| X5 | A firm in the fixture has no panel status, or a status that does not allow work to be placed | The run fails on AC1 and the report names the firm and the field that was empty; the harness never supplies a panel status of its own | None | TC-AD-022-01-ITG (ITG AC1) |
| X6 | The client-supplied firm parameter is honoured, so the answer carries `LAW-B`'s instruction | The run fails on AC2 and the report names the parameter, its value and the instructions the answer carried; an ignored parameter passes, a honoured one fails | None | TC-AD-022-02-ITG (ITG AC2) |
| X7 | rwb-access answers a partner user, or a partner user row is read from `rwb_access` at any point in the run | The run fails on AC5 and the report names the field, the hop and the owner it came from, because a second copy of the partner user is the drift this story exists to catch | None | TC-AD-022-01-ITG (ITG AC5) |
| X8 | The partner gateway does not answer inside the budget | The run fails on AC6 and the report names the route, the elapsed time and the budget; no criterion is marked passed on a timeout | None | TC-AD-022-01-ITG (ITG AC6) |
| X9 | rwb-partner answers 5xx, or answers a list without its firm scope | The run fails on AC1 and AC2 and the report names the operation, the status and the fields of the answer; a 5xx is never read as an empty list, because an empty list is the answer a broken scope rule also produces | None | TC-AD-022-02-ITG (ITG AC2) |
| X10 | A hop reads a table or a view directly instead of calling the owner | The run fails on AC6 and AC5 and the report names the schema, the table and the call that opened it, because a direct read is a pass that proves nothing about the contract | None | TC-AD-022-01-ITG (ITG AC6) |

X1 to X7 are the exception paths of the legacy story read across the two owners; X8 to X10 are the suite's own failure modes, so that a missing answer, a broken scope rule or a direct read never becomes a pass. Only two business messages exist for this story, in section 14; where a source specifies none the message column says so and the run asserts the status and the absence of detail instead.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Runs against the published contracts and the stubs from Day 1; the only waits are RWB-S9-AD022-APP and RWB-P4-E1022-APP, and their fixtures answer until they land; the harness owns no schema and no table |
| Negotiable | The fixture layout, the two firm and user keys, the business date, the report shape and the pass or fail gate are configuration agreed at the wave entry check, not business values in code |
| Valuable | Proves across two services and one portal route what no single slice can prove: the firm comes from the partner user, a client parameter does not move it, another firm's identifier answers nothing, rwb-access holds no partner user, and the missing right is refused with the right message |
| Estimable | One runner, one stub set, one two-firm fixture, five probes and one report |
| Small | Fits in one sprint with its three test cases and no service code and no schema change |
| Testable | Each criterion asserts a status, a message, a field of an answer, the absence of a field, or the recorded call set; every firm, user and instruction key is synthetic |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Partner firms and partner users - wave 4 integration harness

  Background:
    Given the environment is SIT and no production data and no real partner identity are used
    Given the synthetic firm "LAW-A" and the synthetic firm "LAW-B" are held in the fixture as data, each with its partner_code, partner_type, panel_status and contract_end
    Given the partner user "PU-SYN-LAW-A-01" is bound to "LAW-A" and the partner user "PU-SYN-LAW-B-01" is bound to "LAW-B"
    Given the instruction "INS-SYN-LAW-A-01" is placed with "LAW-A" and the instruction "INS-SYN-LAW-B-01" is placed with "LAW-B"

  Scenario: AC1 Firm scope (legacy RWB-AD-022 AC1)
    Given a law firm user
    When they open the partner portal
    Then only instructions placed with their firm show

  Scenario: AC2 The firm is resolved from the partner user and never from a client parameter (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the partner user "PU-SYN-LAW-A-01" signs in through the partner gateway with a second factor
    When the user reads GET /api/recovery/partner/v1/partner/instructions
    Then the answer holds "INS-SYN-LAW-A-01" and not "INS-SYN-LAW-B-01"
    And GET /api/recovery/partner/v1/partners answers only the firm the partner user belongs to
    And a request that carries firm "LAW-B" as a client parameter is refused or ignored, and the answer still holds only the instructions of "LAW-A"

  Scenario: AC3 An instruction of another firm is not returned by its identifier (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the partner user "PU-SYN-LAW-A-01" is signed in through the partner gateway
    When the user calls POST /api/recovery/partner/v1/partner/instructions/INS-SYN-LAW-B-01/accept
    Then the answer is 404 and it carries no instruction detail of "LAW-B"
    And no instruction of "LAW-B" is returned by the portal instruction list of "LAW-A"
    And the instruction of "LAW-A" and the instruction of "LAW-B" are both unchanged

  Scenario: AC4 A caller without Partner portal R is refused with MSG-P4-002 (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given a synthetic caller with role "RW-OFF" that does not hold Partner portal R
    When the caller reads GET /api/recovery/partner/v1/partner/instructions
    Then the answer is 403 with "MSG-P4-002"
    And no instruction is returned

  Scenario: AC5 The partner user and its firm come from rwb-partner and rwb-access holds no partner user (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the partner user "PU-SYN-LAW-A-01" is signed in through the partner gateway
    When the session is read through GET /api/recovery/access/v1/me/session
    Then the session answers the internal role and the rights of the caller only
    And no partner user and no firm is answered by rwb-access
    And the partner user and its firm are read only from rwb-partner
    And a partner user row is never read from "rwb_access"

  Scenario: AC6 Every portal call is one hop on the partner base with a 2 s budget (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the partner user "PU-SYN-LAW-A-01" is signed in through the partner gateway
    When the partner list and the portal instruction list are read
    Then every call is one hop on /api/recovery/partner/v1 with a 2 s budget and a breaker per downstream
    And no call passes through a second service
    And no service's table is read by any hop of the run
```

Legacy AC2 (a firm whose contract ends today has its user accounts disabled and its open instructions recalled) is owned by RWB-S9-AD022-APP and is not restated here: it is the expiry of the partner user against the firm's contract end and the recall of the instruction, both inside rwb-partner. AC1 is the business outcome the whole boundary has to reach, and it is asserted exactly as the legacy story words it.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | A partner user sees only the instructions placed with that user's firm, on the partner portal and on the internal list alike | Legacy RWB-AD-022 story line and AC1, Administration Stories v3 lines 1804 and 1811 to 1814 |
| BR2 | The partner firm, the partner user and the panel status are S9 rwb-partner's data in `rwb_partner`, and no other service holds a copy of the firm or of the partner user | Arch v5 slide 41 (S9 owns panel, partner users, instructions, results, fees, scorecards) and slide 17 (DB writes schema rwb_partner); ASM-0072 |
| BR3 | P4 rwb-access keeps the internal role model, answers the internal session and the Partner portal R right, and holds no partner user | Arch v5 slide 41 (P4 owns Recovery roles as data, scope, masking policy, DoA table, access log); ASM-0072 |
| BR4 | The firm is resolved from the partner user on every portal call and never from a parameter the caller supplies; a supplied firm parameter is refused or ignored | Derived from AC1 and from the gap that fixes no field name for it (GAP-0442; ASM-0634) |
| BR5 | An instruction of another firm is not returned or acted on by its identifier, and the answer carries no detail of it | Legacy AC1, Administration Stories v3 lines 1811 to 1814 |
| BR6 | A caller without Partner portal R is refused with MSG-P4-002 and no instruction is returned | Legacy permission table and messages, Administration Stories v3 lines 1845 to 1854 |
| BR7 | Partners reach the portal only through the partner gateway in the DMZ, with a second factor and the FAPI 2.0 profile; staff reach the same data through the internal edge | Arch v5 slide 17 (partner portal `/partner/v1/*` FAPI 2.0; via partner gateway, MFA), slides 8 and 20, ADR-019 |
| BR8 | Every call is one hop on the owner's base `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` with a 2 s budget and a breaker, never an in-process call and never a second hop | DP-13, DP-19, ADR-020 |
| BR9 | No service reads another service's tables: the firm, the user and the instruction come from S9's contract, the session and the right from P4's, and the data room of S6 is a separate owner and a separate story | DP-05, DP-01; Arch v5 slides 17, 19 and 41 |
| BR10 | The instruction lifecycle, its SLA timers and the contract-end disablement and recall are S9's, run by InstructionWorkflow on `rwb-partner`, and this story observes them without changing them | Arch v5 slide 17 (InstructionWorkflow, SLA timers, issueInstruction, recordResult); Temporal and Drools design slide 25; legacy AC2 |

The harness asserts these rules and changes none of them; the rules themselves are evaluated in RWB-S9-AD022-APP for the firm, the user and the instruction, and in RWB-P4-E1022-APP for the session, the role and the right.

##### 9. State transitions

None. The story reads and refuses: it changes no partner, no partner user, no partner instruction and no record of either service. The two sign-ins create a portal session and an internal session, which are the edge's, and the refused accept of another firm's instruction changes nothing on the instruction; every criterion of section 7 is a read, a refusal or an absence.

The transitions the legacy key does have are S9's and are asserted by RWB-S9-AD022-APP: the instruction moves from SENT through ACCEPTED, IN_PROGRESS and DONE or RECALLED, and the partner user's binding ends with `valid_to` no later than the firm's contract end, which is the contract-end disablement and the recall of legacy AC2. The harness never sets a state it then asserts, and a state it had set by hand would prove nothing.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| RW-NPAMGR, RW-DEBTSALE, RW-LEGAL, RW-LITOFF, RW-ENFORCE, RW-CASEOWN, RW-TEAMMGR, RW-SALEOFF | Hold Partner portal R on the staff side and may read the partner and the instruction list; they are the roles of the legacy permission table, which also names further holders |
| The partner user | Is S9's data, bound to one firm and one partner role, and holds the portal identity; it is the identity the portal route authenticates, and the run holds its firm and its role in the fixture, never a person |
| The partner gateway | Enforces the second factor and the FAPI 2.0 profile before rwb-partner is reached, and is the only route the partner identity uses |
| RW-OFF | Holds no Partner portal R and is the refused caller of AC4 |
| QA lead | Owns the harness configuration, the fixtures, the report shape and the pass or fail gate |
| Integration lead | Owns the harness code, the stub set and the swap from a stub to the real service |
| The owning services' identities | S9 holds the firm, the partner user, the instruction and the panel and answers the portal; P4 answers the session, the internal role and the right; they make every value the harness asserts |
| No delegation of authority level applies | The harness takes no business decision; authorisation is answered by rwb-access and the DoA is P4's |

##### 11. Data

| BR Field ID | Entity | Field | Read or write |
|---|---|---|---|
| DF-PRT-001 to DF-PRT-007 | partner | partner_code, partner_name, partner_type, panel_status, contract_end | Read through the rwb-partner contract; the harness writes nothing |
| DF-PRT-008 to DF-PRT-016 | partner_instruction | id, case_id, partner_id, instruction_type, instructed_at, due_at, status, result_code | Read through the rwb-partner contract; the harness writes nothing |
| DF-REF-212 to DF-REF-217 | partner_user | identity_ref, partner_id, role_code, valid_from, valid_to | Read through the rwb-partner contract, as the binding of the user to the firm; the harness writes nothing |
| DF-REF-034 to DF-REF-038 | role | role_code, role_name, role_class, default_scope | Read through the rwb-access contract, for the internal role of the caller |

Field IDs are those in the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8. The partner, the partner instruction and the partner user are S9's in `rwb_partner`; the role is P4's in `rwb_access`, and its `role_class` LOV names a partner-user class without any partner user row being held there. The harness owns no table and writes no row: it holds the two firms, their users, their instructions and their panel status in its own fixture as data, and it reads every asserted value back through the owner. `partner_user` has six fields in the data dictionary and is read for the binding only; its `identity_ref` is the partner identity directory reference and never a name, an address or an identity number, and the harness records the reference and the firm relation, never a personal value. The harness writes nothing.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None. The harness is a test runner and provides no REST operation.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/recovery/partner/v1/partners` | S9 rwb-partner | The firm the partner user belongs to, with its panel status and its contract end (AC1, AC2, AC5) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/partner/v1/partner/instructions` | S9 rwb-partner | The instructions placed with that firm, on the portal list; the list of the other firm is the absence it asserts (AC1, AC2, AC3, AC6) |
| POST | `/api/recovery/partner/v1/partner/instructions/{instructionId}/accept` | S9 rwb-partner | The only published portal operation that takes an instruction identifier, so it is where another firm's identifier is called; the run asserts 404 and no detail, and takes no accept on its own instruction (AC3) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/access/v1/me/session` | P4 rwb-access | The internal role and the Partner portal R right, and the proof that the answer holds no partner user and no firm (AC4, AC5) |

Every call is one hop on the owner's base `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` with a 2 s budget (DP-13, DP-19; ADR-020). No operation is invented in this story: each path is the owner's published operation in the Ownership Map. The Ownership Map publishes no instruction-by-id read for S9 and no partner-user read for P4, so the cross-firm identifier is called on the accept operation, which is published, and the absence of a partner user in rwb-access is asserted from the session answer and from the published contract set, never from an operation that does not exist. The partner data room of S6 is not consumed: it is a buyer-facing operation on `/api/recovery/debtsale/v1/partner/data-room/{lotId}` and belongs to the debt sale story, and nothing in this proof needs it.

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The harness publishes no Kafka event; it writes its report to the wave record.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. The harness consumes no topic in this story: the two firms, their users and their instructions are fixture data, and every criterion is a read, a refusal or an absence. `rwb.partner.InstructionIssued.v1` and `rwb.partner.PartnerResultSubmitted.v1` are the two events of the S9 contract (Arch v5 slide 43, rows 20 and 21) and they belong to the instruction lifecycle that RWB-S9-AD022-APP builds and asserts; this run places no instruction and records no result, so it counts no publication and replays none. A run that seeded its instructions through the staff instruction operation would publish an InstructionIssued event and would change instruction state, which section 9 rules out for this story.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None added. The harness observes InstructionWorkflow, S9's workflow on the task queue `rwb-partner` in the `rwb-recovery` namespace, as the workflow that carries an instruction placed with a firm, its SLA timers and its `issueInstruction` and `recordResult` steps (Arch v5 slide 17; Temporal and Drools design slide 25). It is observed from its history for the two instructions of the fixture and it is not built, started or changed here: no workflow, activity or Schedule is created, changed or owned by this story.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None added. The instruction lifecycle runs on its own SLA timers inside InstructionWorkflow, and the harness waits on nothing: it reads the two instructions as the fixture holds them and starts no cron, overlap policy or catch-up window.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

None. The harness owns no schema and no table (DP-05); partner, partner_instruction and partner_user are S9's in `rwb_partner`, and role is P4's in `rwb_access`.

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Contract | Stubbed answer in the run |
|---|---|---|
| Stub for rwb-partner (S9) | `GET /partners`, `GET /partner/instructions`, `POST /partner/instructions/{instructionId}/accept` | Firms `LAW-A` and `LAW-B` with their partner_code, partner_type, panel_status and contract_end; one instruction per firm with its case, type, dates and status; the partner read and the instruction list answer only the firm of the signed-in partner user, and a client-supplied firm parameter is ignored, never honoured; the accept of `INS-SYN-LAW-B-01` for the `LAW-A` user answers 404 with no instruction detail; a firm with no panel status answers the empty field for X5, and a 5xx variant answers for X9 |
| Stub for rwb-access (P4) | `GET /me/session` | Answers the internal role and the rights of the partner user, including Partner portal R, and no partner user and no firm; answers RW-OFF without Partner portal R with 403 and MSG-P4-002; a variant that answers a partner user is the X7 failure |
| Stub for the partner gateway | The portal route, the second factor and the FAPI 2.0 profile | Accepts the synthetic partner identity with a second factor and forwards one hop to the portal read of rwb-partner; refuses a call that presents no second factor; answers the timeout variant of X8 |
| Partner fixture | The two firms, their users, their instructions and the panel status | `LAW-A` and `LAW-B` as data, `PU-SYN-LAW-A-01` and `PU-SYN-LAW-B-01` bound one to one, `INS-SYN-LAW-A-01` and `INS-SYN-LAW-B-01` on their own cases, and the business date `2027-02-28` |

Each stub is generated from the published contract and its version is pinned in the run report, so a contract change shows up as a run failure and not as a silent pass. The portal route specification, the firm-scope field name, the partner session and MFA assertion shape, the partner_user field set as it is published, and the answer and the message a cross-firm identifier receives are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0442; ASM-0634). The run holds them as configuration and asserts the shape of the answer, never a value it invented.

| Kafka | None published and none consumed; the two partner events stay with the S9 slice of section 12.4 |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** Folder `itg/recovery`, package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.itg`, test scope only; not part of any deployed service.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through the owner's contract; no service reads another service's tables | none |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route, and the partner gateway for the portal | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-05 is applied here as the rule that no service reads another's tables: the firm, the partner user and the instruction are S9's and the session and the right are P4's, and the harness reads each only through its owner. DP-13 adds no dependency: the partner and the session paths are on each owner's own base and there is no shared base left. The H dependency DP-19 adds, RWB-PLT-N001-CON, is a platform story delivered in the platform wave and is not repeated in the metadata H field of this story, which stays None. The blocking dependencies are the two I stories, RWB-S9-AD022-APP and RWB-P4-E1022-APP, which replace their stubs; until they are live the run uses the stubs, and a stub pass is reported as a stub pass.

**Harness components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| PartnerSignIn | Service | Signs the synthetic partner user in through the partner gateway with a second factor, records the portal route and the FAPI 2.0 profile, and holds the synthetic partner identity and its firm |
| FirmScopeProbe | Service | Reads the partner and the instruction list, asserts the one firm and its panel status, repeats the read with a client-supplied firm, and calls another firm's identifier |
| InstructionProbe | Service | Reads the portal instruction list and asserts the one instruction of the firm with its type, dates and status, and the absence of the other firm's instruction |
| AccessProbe | Service | Asserts that rwb-access answers the internal role and the right only, and that no partner user and no firm is answered or read from `rwb_access` |
| SessionProbe | Service | Reads `GET /api/recovery/access/v1/me/session`, asserts the role and the Partner portal R right, and holds the refused caller of AC4 |
| StubSet | Fake | The three stubs and the partner fixture of §12.8, generated from the published contracts with the version pinned |
| EvidenceReport | Service | Writes one report keyed by story and partner user, with the two firms, the two instructions, the refusals and the verdict of each criterion, and holds the pass or fail gate |

**Environment and test data.** SIT, against the stubs from Day 1 and the real services as RWB-S9-AD022-APP and RWB-P4-E1022-APP land, on the synthetic firms `LAW-A` and `LAW-B`, the partner users `PU-SYN-LAW-A-01` and `PU-SYN-LAW-B-01`, the instructions `INS-SYN-LAW-A-01` on case `RW-2027-001101` and `INS-SYN-LAW-B-01` on case `RW-2027-001102`, and the business date `2027-02-28`. The harness seeds nothing by hand and never writes a schema row. The portal route, the firm-scope field name, the partner session and MFA assertion shape and the cross-firm answer are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0442; ASM-0634).

**Build steps**

1. Generate the three stubs and the partner fixture from the published contracts and pin each contract version in the run report; fail the run on a mismatch (X1).
2. Build PartnerSignIn: the portal sign-in with a second factor, the route recorded, and the firm and the role of the synthetic user held as data (AC1, AC6, X2).
3. Add SessionProbe: the session read returns the internal role and Partner portal R, and the report names them (AC5).
4. Add AccessProbe for AC5: the session answer carries no partner user and no firm, the access contract publishes no partner-user read, and no hop reads `rwb_access`; a stub that answers a partner user fails the run (X7).
5. Add FirmScopeProbe for AC1 and AC2: the partner read returns one firm with its panel status and contract end, and a firm with no panel status fails the run (X5).
6. Add InstructionProbe for AC1 and AC2: the portal list returns the one instruction of the firm, and the other firm's instruction is absent (X9).
7. Add the firm parameter and the cross-firm identifier to FirmScopeProbe for AC2 and AC3: the client-supplied firm is refused or ignored and is recorded as which, and another firm's identifier answers 404 with no detail and changes nothing (X3, X6).
8. Add the refused caller of AC4 through the session read and the instruction list, and assert 403 with MSG-P4-002 and no instruction (X4).
9. Add the hop and budget check for AC6, the EvidenceReport and the gate, and swap a stub for the real owner as each I story lands (X8, X10).

**Feature switch.** None. The harness has no production flag and runs in the test environment only.

**Done when.** The tests of section 16 pass against the fakes and again against both I stories when they land, and the wave entry check holds a run report keyed by story and partner user that names, for every call, the contract version and whether the hop was a stub or the owner.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | Type | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-GEN-001 | Error | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-P4-002 | Error | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |

The harness asserts the message ID and the substituted values on the answer it reads, and owns no message text. MSG-P4-002 is asserted with the refused read of the instruction list by the RW-OFF caller (step 9, AC4). MSG-GEN-001 is the general message of the legacy story and is asserted where a requested read is short of a required field, naming the missing field; the legacy story carries it and this run changes neither its text nor its use. No message is specified in any source read for a cross-firm identifier or for a gateway refusal: the 404 of AC3 therefore carries no business message and the run asserts the status and the absence of instruction detail instead, and the gateway refusal of X2 is asserted the same way. That absence is part of GAP-0442 and ASM-0634.

##### 15. Screens and states

The legacy story's screens are SCR-34 Partner list and PRT-01 Partner home, and neither is built or rendered here: the harness calls the operations behind them and reads the states through the owners. What the wave entry check looks at instead is the run report, whose environment, layout and retention are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0442; ASM-0634).

| State | Read through | What the run asserts |
|---|---|---|
| Loading | The partner gateway route and the portal reads | The call is on the portal route with a second factor and the answer arrives inside the 2 s budget and the breaker |
| List | S9 partner read and portal instruction read | One firm with its panel status and contract end, and one instruction with its type, dates and status, for the firm of the signed-in user |
| Refused | P4 session read and the refuse answer | 403 with MSG-P4-002 for the caller without Partner portal R, and 404 with no detail for another firm's identifier |
| No instruction | S9 portal instruction read | A firm with no instruction answers an empty list and never the instruction of another firm; the empty answer is never read as a 5xx |

##### 16. Test cases

| TC ID | Covers | Level | Data |
|---|---|---|---|
| TC-AD-022-01-ITG | AC1 (legacy); ITG AC1, AC5 and AC6 | End to end | The two firms, their two users and their two instructions, the portal sign-in with a second factor, the partner and instruction reads, the session read, and the recorded call set |
| TC-AD-022-02-ITG | ITG AC2 and AC3 | Integration | The same user reading with firm `LAW-B` in a client parameter, and calling `INS-SYN-LAW-B-01` on the accept operation, with both instruction lists read before and after |
| TC-AD-022-03-ITG | Access; ITG AC4 | Component | A synthetic RW-OFF caller without Partner portal R, and a read short of its required field |

The AC column names the legacy test case each -ITG copy derives from and the ITG criteria it asserts, and the full legacy test, with its Given, When and Then, is in Recovery Workbench Test Cases v7.xlsx under the same legacy test case ID. The legacy test cases TC-AD-022-01 to TC-AD-022-03 are kept as the `-ITG` copies with the legacy Covers (AC1, AC2, Access): the legacy Covers of TC-AD-022-01 is AC1 and is AC1 here, the legacy Covers of TC-AD-022-03 is Access and is AC4 here, and TC-AD-022-02 is the copy whose legacy AC2 (the contract-end disablement and the recall) stays with RWB-S9-AD022-APP — the -ITG copy asserts the same firm boundary from the portal side, which is the answer the firm's user gets when the firm scope moves. AC5 and AC6 have no legacy test case of their own in this key and are folded into the one end-to-end run of TC-AD-022-01-ITG.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the two firms, their panel status and contracts, the two partner users and their bindings, the two instructions, the business date, the report layout and the gate are data.
- No personal data anywhere: the run holds partner and user keys only, and never a name, an address, an identity number, a telephone number or a document; the partner identity is the directory reference of the synthetic binding and nothing else.
- No cross-schema read: the firm, the partner user and the instruction come from S9's contract, the session and the right from P4's, and a hop that opens `rwb_partner` or `rwb_access` fails the run (DP-05).
- P4 holds no partner user: a partner user answered by rwb-access, or read from `rwb_access`, fails the run, because that copy is the drift the story exists to catch (ASM-0072).
- One hop and a 2 s budget per call, with a breaker per downstream, so the harness fails where a screen would (DP-13, DP-19; ADR-020).
- The second factor is on the partner gateway and is never bypassed by the harness: a run that reached rwb-partner without presenting it is not a pass (ADR-019).
- SIT only, with synthetic identities only: the harness never runs against UAT or production and never writes a row by hand or sets a state it then asserts.
- A stub pass is never reported as a real pass: the report names the contract version and whether the hop was a stub or the owner.
- A failing criterion is fixed in the owning service or raised as a gap; it is never waived in the script.

##### 19. Out of scope

- RWB-S9-AD022-CON and RWB-S9-AD022-APP: the partner firms, the partner users, the panel, the instructions, the results and the portal reads themselves.
- RWB-P4-E1022-APP: the sign-on, the second factor, the group-to-role mapping and the first roles; this story consumes its session contract as an I dependency.
- The contract-end disablement and the recall of legacy AC2: the expiry of the partner user's binding against the firm's contract end and the recall of the open instructions, inside rwb-partner.
- The partner data room of S6, `GET /api/recovery/debtsale/v1/partner/data-room/{lotId}`, and every buyer-facing operation of the debt sale story.
- The fees and the scorecards of S9, the fee approval and the partner review of the same service.
- SCR-34 Partner list and PRT-01 Partner home, and every gateway-bff composite route behind a staff screen.
- The partner gateway build, its FAPI 2.0 profile and its second-factor configuration, which are the platform's and the portal's own product.
- The platform stories named in section 13, including RWB-PLT-N001-CON.
- Any production change: no endpoint, table, workflow, activity, schedule, screen, feature flag or configuration in any service.
